export interface ConnectorConfig {
  /** Brevo API key for authentication */
  brevoApiKey: string
  /** Default list ID to subscribe contacts to (can be overridden by form mapping) */
  defaultListId: number
  /** Optional mapping of Typeform field IDs to Brevo list IDs */
  fieldIdToListId?: Record<string, number>
  /** Optional injected fetch for testing */
  fetch?: typeof fetch
}

export interface TypeformWebhookPayload {
  event_id: string
  event_type: string
  form_response: {
    form_id: string
    token: string
    submitted_at: string
    answers: Array<{
      type: string
      email?: string
      text?: string
      field: {
        id: string
        type: string
      }
    }>
  }
}

export interface BrevoContactResult {
  contactId: number
  email: string
  listIds: number[]
}

function getFetch(config: ConnectorConfig): typeof fetch {
  return config.fetch ?? fetch
}

function extractEmail(answers: TypeformWebhookPayload['form_response']['answers']): string | undefined {
  const emailAnswer = answers.find((a) => a.type === 'email' && a.email)
  return emailAnswer?.email
}

function extractName(answers: TypeformWebhookPayload['form_response']['answers']): { firstName: string; lastName: string } | undefined {
  // Look for short_text or text fields that could be name
  // Typeform doesn't have explicit first/last name fields in the example
  // We'll treat the first text field as first name
  const nameAnswer = answers.find((a) => a.type === 'text' && a.text)
  if (!nameAnswer || !nameAnswer.text) return undefined
  
  const fullName = nameAnswer.text.trim()
  const parts = fullName.split(/\s+/)
  return {
    firstName: parts[0] ?? '',
    lastName: parts.slice(1).join(' ') || ''
  }
}

function determineListIds(
  answers: TypeformWebhookPayload['form_response']['answers'],
  config: ConnectorConfig
): number[] {
  const listIds = new Set<number>()
  
  // Always include default list
  listIds.add(config.defaultListId)
  
  // Check for field ID mappings
  if (config.fieldIdToListId) {
    for (const answer of answers) {
      const mappedListId = config.fieldIdToListId[answer.field.id]
      if (mappedListId) listIds.add(mappedListId)
    }
  }
  
  return Array.from(listIds)
}

export async function handle(
  payload: TypeformWebhookPayload,
  config: ConnectorConfig
): Promise<BrevoContactResult> {
  // Validate required config
  if (!config.brevoApiKey) {
    throw new Error('Missing required config: brevoApiKey')
  }
  if (!config.defaultListId || typeof config.defaultListId !== 'number') {
    throw new Error('Missing required config: defaultListId (must be a number)')
  }
  
  // Validate payload structure
  if (!payload.form_response?.answers?.length) {
    throw new Error('Invalid payload: missing form_response.answers')
  }
  
  const email = extractEmail(payload.form_response.answers)
  if (!email) {
    throw new Error('Required field missing: email not found in form answers')
  }
  
  const name = extractName(payload.form_response.answers)
  const listIds = determineListIds(payload.form_response.answers, config)
  
  // Build Brevo request body
  const body = {
    email,
    attributes: {
      FNAME: name?.firstName ?? '',
      LNAME: name?.lastName ?? ''
    },
    listIds
  }
  
  const fetchFn = getFetch(config)
  const response = await fetchFn('https://api.brevo.com/v3/contacts', {
    method: 'POST',
    headers: {
      'api-key': config.brevoApiKey,
      'Content-Type': 'application/json',
      Accept: 'application/json'
    },
    body: JSON.stringify(body)
  })
  
  if (!response.ok) {
    const errorText = await response.text().catch(() => '')
    throw new Error(
      `Brevo API error: ${response.status} ${response.statusText} ` +
      `at POST https://api.brevo.com/v3/contacts - ${errorText}`
    )
  }
  
  const result = (await response.json()) as { id: number }
  
  return {
    contactId: result.id,
    email,
    listIds
  }
}

<file path="README.md">
# Typeform to Brevo Contact Connector

Creates a Brevo contact from a Typeform form response webhook and subscribes the contact to one or more lists.

## What it does

1. Receives a Typeform `form_response` webhook payload
2. Extracts the respondent's email and name from the answers array
3. Creates a contact in Brevo via `POST https://api.brevo.com/v3/contacts`
4. Subscribes the contact to configured list(s)

## Configuration

| Config Property | Environment Variable | Required | Description |
|-----------------|---------------------|----------|-------------|
| `brevoApiKey` | `BREVO_API_KEY` | Yes | Brevo API key for authentication (sent as `api-key` header) |
| `defaultListId` | `BREVO_DEFAULT_LIST_ID` | Yes | Default numeric list ID to subscribe all contacts to |
| `fieldIdToListId` | `BREVO_FIELD_ID_TO_LIST_ID` | No | JSON object mapping Typeform field IDs to additional Brevo list IDs |

### Environment Variables

```bash
# Required
export BREVO_API_KEY="your-brevo-api-key"
export BREVO_DEFAULT_LIST_ID="123"

# Optional - JSON mapping of field IDs to list IDs
export BREVO_FIELD_ID_TO_LIST_ID='{"field-id-1": 456, "field-id-2": 789}'
```

## Usage Example

```typescript
import { handle, ConnectorConfig, TypeformWebhookPayload } from './connector'

const config: ConnectorConfig = {
  brevoApiKey: process.env.BREVO_API_KEY!,
  defaultListId: Number(process.env.BREVO_DEFAULT_LIST_ID),
  fieldIdToListId: JSON.parse(process.env.BREVO_FIELD_ID_TO_LIST_ID || '{}')
}

// In your webhook handler:
const result = await handle(typeformPayload as TypeformWebhookPayload, config)
console.log(`Created contact ${result.contactId} for ${result.email}`)
```

## Field Mapping

| Typeform Source | Brevo Target | Notes |
|-----------------|--------------|-------|
| `answers[].email` (type: email) | `email` | Required |
| `answers[].text` (type: text/short_text) | `attributes.FNAME` | First word becomes first name |
| `answers[].text` (type: text/short_text) | `attributes.LNAME` | Remaining words become last name |
| `fieldIdToListId` config | `listIds` | Merged with `defaultListId`, deduplicated |

## Assumptions

1. The Typeform webhook payload includes the respondent's email under an `email` type answer and name under a `text` type answer
2. The Brevo API accepts attributes in uppercase (`FNAME`, `LNAME`) which must exist in the Brevo account
3. The `listIds` array expects numeric list IDs from the Brevo UI or `/v3/lists` endpoint
4. If a contact already exists, Brevo returns 400 unless `updateEnabled: true` is set (not currently supported by this connector)
5. The webhook endpoint must be HTTPS (Typeform requirement)

## Error Handling

- Throws descriptive errors for missing required fields (email, config values)
- Throws on non-2xx Brevo responses with status code, endpoint, and response body
- Validates payload structure before making API calls

export interface DocumentedEndpoint {
  method: string
  /** As documented; may contain placeholders such as {id}, :id, <id> or a region host like usX. */
  url: string
  response: unknown
}

/** Target endpoints the connector may call, in the documented order, with their documented responses. */
export const TARGET_ENDPOINTS: DocumentedEndpoint[] = [
  {
    "method": "POST",
    "url": "https://api.brevo.com/v3/contacts",
    "response": {
      "id": 12345
    }
  }
]

export interface RecordedCall {
  method: string
  url: string
  /** The request body exactly as sent (usually a JSON string). */
  body: string | undefined
  /** The body parsed as JSON, or undefined when it is not JSON. */
  json: unknown
  headers: Headers
}

/** The documented endpoint a request matches, placeholders and region subdomains included. */
export function findEndpoint(method: string, url: string): DocumentedEndpoint | undefined {
  return TARGET_ENDPOINTS.find((endpoint) => endpoint.method === method.toUpperCase() && urlMatches(endpoint.url, url))
}

/**
 * A fake fetch that answers every documented endpoint with its documented response and
 * rejects anything else. Use it in the contract test:
 *
 *   const { fetch, calls } = contractFetch()
 *   await handle(SOURCE_EXAMPLE as MyInput, { ...config, fetch })
 *   expect(calls.length).toBeGreaterThan(0)
 */
export function contractFetch(): { fetch: typeof fetch; calls: RecordedCall[] } {
  return fakeFetch((request) => {
    const endpoint = findEndpoint(request.method, request.url)
    if (!endpoint) throw new Error(`contract: ${request.method} ${request.url} is not a documented endpoint`)
    return jsonResponse(endpoint.response)
  })
}

/**
 * A correctly typed fake fetch for every other test. The handler receives the recorded
 * request: { method, url, body (string as sent), json (parsed body), headers (Headers) }.
 *
 *   const { fetch, calls } = fakeFetch((req) => req.url.endsWith('/deals') ? jsonResponse({ id: 1 }, 201) : jsonResponse({}, 404))
 */
export function fakeFetch(
  handler: (request: RecordedCall) => Response | Promise<Response>,
): { fetch: typeof fetch; calls: RecordedCall[] } {
  const calls: RecordedCall[] = []
  const fake = async (input: string | URL | Request, init: RequestInit = {}): Promise<Response> => {
    const url = input instanceof Request ? input.url : String(input)
    const method = (init.method ?? (input instanceof Request ? input.method : 'GET')).toUpperCase()
    const body = typeof init.body === 'string' ? init.body : init.body == null ? undefined : String(init.body)
    const call: RecordedCall = { method, url, body, json: parseJson(body), headers: new Headers(init.headers) }
    calls.push(call)
    return handler(call)
  }
  return { fetch: fake as typeof fetch, calls }
}

const STATUS_TEXT: Record<number, string> = {
  200: 'OK', 201: 'Created', 202: 'Accepted', 204: 'No Content',
  400: 'Bad Request', 401: 'Unauthorized', 403: 'Forbidden', 404: 'Not Found', 409: 'Conflict',
  422: 'Unprocessable Entity', 429: 'Too Many Requests',
  500: 'Internal Server Error', 502: 'Bad Gateway', 503: 'Service Unavailable',
}

/** A JSON Response with the standard status text, e.g. jsonResponse({ error: 'nope' }, 401) -> "401 Unauthorized". */
export function jsonResponse(body: unknown, status = 200): Response {
  const init = { status, statusText: STATUS_TEXT[status] ?? '', headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' } }
  return new Response(status === 204 ? null : JSON.stringify(body), init)
}

function parseJson(raw: string | undefined): unknown {
  if (raw === undefined) return undefined
  try {
    return JSON.parse(raw)
  } catch {
    return undefined
  }
}

function urlMatches(template: string, actual: string): boolean {
  const t = splitUrl(template)
  const a = splitUrl(actual)
  if (!t || !a) return false
  const tHost = t.host.split('.')
  const aHost = a.host.split('.')
  if (tHost.slice(-2).join('.') !== aHost.slice(-2).join('.')) return false
  const tPath = t.path.replace(/\/+$/, '').split('/')
  const aPath = a.path.replace(/\/+$/, '').split('/')
  if (tPath.length !== aPath.length) return false
  return tPath.every((segment, i) => isPlaceholder(segment) || segment === aPath[i])
}

function splitUrl(url: string): { host: string; path: string } | null {
  const match = url.match(/^https?:\/\/([^/?#]+)([^?#]*)/i)
  return match ? { host: (match[1] ?? '').toLowerCase(), path: match[2] || '/' } : null
}

function isPlaceholder(segment: string): boolean {
  return /^\{[^}]+\}$|^:[A-Za-z_]\w*$|^<[^>]+>$/.test(segment)
}

export interface ConnectorConfig {
  datadogApiKey: string
  datadogAppKey: string
  datadogSite: string
  fetch?: typeof fetch
}

export interface MailchimpRetryPayload {
  response_status: number
  retry_count: number
  final_response_body: string
  retry_after_header: string
}

export interface HandleResult {
  eventId: string
}

function validatePayload(payload: unknown): asserts payload is MailchimpRetryPayload {
  if (!payload || typeof payload !== 'object') {
    throw new Error('Payload must be an object')
  }
  const p = payload as Record<string, unknown>
  if (typeof p.response_status !== 'number') {
    throw new Error('Missing required field: response_status (number)')
  }
  if (typeof p.retry_count !== 'number') {
    throw new Error('Missing required field: retry_count (number)')
  }
  if (typeof p.final_response_body !== 'string') {
    throw new Error('Missing required field: final_response_body (string)')
  }
  if (typeof p.retry_after_header !== 'string') {
    throw new Error('Missing required field: retry_after_header (string)')
  }
}

export async function handle(
  payload: MailchimpRetryPayload,
  config: ConnectorConfig
): Promise<HandleResult> {
  validatePayload(payload)

  const fetchImpl = config.fetch ?? fetch
  const url = `https://event-management-intake.${config.datadogSite}/api/v2/events`

  const status = payload.response_status === 429 && payload.retry_count >= 3 ? 'error' : 'success'
  const tags = [
    'source:mailchimp',
    `retry_count:${payload.retry_count}`,
    `status:${status}`,
    `retry_after:${payload.retry_after_header}`
  ]

  const body = {
    title: 'Mailchimp API Retry Outcome',
    text: payload.final_response_body,
    tags,
    alert_type: payload.retry_after_header,
    status
  }

  const response = await fetchImpl(url, {
    method: 'POST',
    headers: {
      'DD-API-KEY': config.datadogApiKey,
      'DD-APPLICATION-KEY': config.datadogAppKey,
      'Content-Type': 'application/json'
    },
    body: JSON.stringify(body)
  })

  if (!response.ok) {
    throw new Error(`Datadog Events API request failed: ${response.status} ${response.statusText} at ${url}`)
  }

  const data = await response.json() as { event?: { id?: string } }
  const eventId = data.event?.id
  if (!eventId) {
    throw new Error('Datadog response missing event.id')
  }

  return { eventId }
}

<file path="README.md">
# Mailchimp Retry Outcome to Datadog Event Connector

This connector captures the outcome of a Mailchimp API call that returned HTTP 429 (Too Many Requests) and creates a Datadog event with the retry metadata for debugging and alerting.

## What it does

1. Receives a payload containing the Mailchimp API response details after retry attempts
2. Maps the payload fields to a Datadog Events API v2 request
3. Posts the event to Datadog with retry context (count, status, Retry-After header)
4. Returns the created Datadog event ID

## Configuration

The connector requires the following configuration (typically sourced from environment variables):

| Config Property | Environment Variable | Description |
|-----------------|---------------------|-------------|
| `datadogApiKey` | `DATADOG_API_KEY` | Datadog API key for authentication (DD-API-KEY header) |
| `datadogAppKey` | `DATADOG_APPLICATION_KEY` | Datadog Application key for authentication (DD-APPLICATION-KEY header) |
| `datadogSite` | `DATADOG_SITE` | Datadog site domain (e.g., `datadoghq.com`, `us3.datadoghq.com`, `datadoghq.eu`) |

## Usage Example

```typescript
import { handle, ConnectorConfig, MailchimpRetryPayload } from './connector'

const config: ConnectorConfig = {
  datadogApiKey: process.env.DATADOG_API_KEY!,
  datadogAppKey: process.env.DATADOG_APPLICATION_KEY!,
  datadogSite: process.env.DATADOG_SITE || 'datadoghq.com'
}

const payload: MailchimpRetryPayload = {
  response_status: 429,
  retry_count: 2,
  final_response_body: JSON.stringify({
    type: 'https://mailchimp.com/developer/marketing/docs/errors/',
    title: 'Too Many Requests',
    status: 429,
    detail: 'You have exceeded the limit of 10 simultaneous connections.',
    instance: 'abc123'
  }),
  retry_after_header: '60'
}

const result = await handle(payload, config)
console.log('Created Datadog event:', result.eventId)
```

## Field Mapping

| Source Field | Target Field | Notes |
|--------------|--------------|-------|
| `response_status` + `retry_count` | `status` | `'error'` if final attempt failed (429 with retry_count ≥ 3), `'success'` otherwise |
| `retry_count` | `tags` includes `retry_count:N` | Number of retries attempted (0-3) |
| `final_response_body` | `text` | Full response body from final attempt |
| `retry_after_header` | `alert_type` and `tags` includes `retry_after:N` | Value of Retry-After header from last 429 response |

## Assumptions

- The Mailchimp API call is initiated by the integration and returns a standard HTTP 429 response with a Retry-After header
- The integration captures the full HTTP response object (status, headers, body) after each retry attempt
- Datadog API key and Application key are configured and the Events API endpoint is accessible
- The event created in Datadog contains the retry metadata as context for debugging
- The Datadog site placeholder `{site}` in the endpoint URL is replaced with the actual Datadog site domain
- Both `DD-API-KEY` and `DD-APPLICATION-KEY` headers are required for Datadog Events API v2 authentication

## Error Handling

- Throws descriptive errors when required payload fields are missing
- Throws error with status code and endpoint URL on non-2xx Datadog API responses
- Throws error if Datadog response is missing the event ID

  "response_status": 429,
  "retry_count": 2,
  "final_response_body": "{ \"type\": \"https://mailchimp.com/developer/marketing/docs/errors/\", \"title\": \"Too Many Requests\", \"status\": 429, \"detail\": \"You have exceeded the limit of 10 simultaneous connections.\", \"instance\": \"abc123\" }",
  "retry_after_header": "60"
}

export interface DocumentedEndpoint {
  method: string
  /** As documented; may contain placeholders such as {id}, :id, <id> or a region host like usX. */
  url: string
  response: unknown
}

/** Target endpoints the connector may call, in the documented order, with their documented responses. */
export const TARGET_ENDPOINTS: DocumentedEndpoint[] = [
  {
    "method": "POST",
    "url": "https://event-management-intake.{site}/api/v2/events",
    "response": {
      "event": {
        "id": "1234567890abcdef",
        "title": "Mailchimp API Retry Outcome",
        "text": "{ \"type\": \"https://mailchimp.com/developer/marketing/docs/errors/\", \"title\": \"Too Many Requests\", \"status\": 429, \"detail\": \"You have exceeded the limit of 10 simultaneous connections.\", \"instance\": \"abc123\" }",
        "tags": [
          "source:mailchimp",
          "retry_count:2",
          "status:error",
          "retry_after:60"
        ],
        "alert_type": "60",
        "status": "error"
      }
    }
  }
]

export interface RecordedCall {
  method: string
  url: string
  /** The request body exactly as sent (usually a JSON string). */
  body: string | undefined
  /** The body parsed as JSON, or undefined when it is not JSON. */
  json: unknown
  headers: Headers
}

/** The documented endpoint a request matches, placeholders and region subdomains included. */
export function findEndpoint(method: string, url: string): DocumentedEndpoint | undefined {
  return TARGET_ENDPOINTS.find((endpoint) => endpoint.method === method.toUpperCase() && urlMatches(endpoint.url, url))
}

/**
 * A fake fetch that answers every documented endpoint with its documented response and
 * rejects anything else. Use it in the contract test:
 *
 *   const { fetch, calls } = contractFetch()
 *   await handle(SOURCE_EXAMPLE as MyInput, { ...config, fetch })
 *   expect(calls.length).toBeGreaterThan(0)
 */
export function contractFetch(): { fetch: typeof fetch; calls: RecordedCall[] } {
  return fakeFetch((request) => {
    const endpoint = findEndpoint(request.method, request.url)
    if (!endpoint) throw new Error(`contract: ${request.method} ${request.url} is not a documented endpoint`)
    return jsonResponse(endpoint.response)
  })
}

/**
 * A correctly typed fake fetch for every other test. The handler receives the recorded
 * request: { method, url, body (string as sent), json (parsed body), headers (Headers) }.
 *
 *   const { fetch, calls } = fakeFetch((req) => req.url.endsWith('/deals') ? jsonResponse({ id: 1 }, 201) : jsonResponse({}, 404))
 */
export function fakeFetch(
  handler: (request: RecordedCall) => Response | Promise<Response>,
): { fetch: typeof fetch; calls: RecordedCall[] } {
  const calls: RecordedCall[] = []
  const fake = async (input: string | URL | Request, init: RequestInit = {}): Promise<Response> => {
    const url = input instanceof Request ? input.url : String(input)
    const method = (init.method ?? (input instanceof Request ? input.method : 'GET')).toUpperCase()
    const body = typeof init.body === 'string' ? init.body : init.body == null ? undefined : String(init.body)
    const call: RecordedCall = { method, url, body, json: parseJson(body), headers: new Headers(init.headers) }
    calls.push(call)
    return handler(call)
  }
  return { fetch: fake as typeof fetch, calls }
}

const STATUS_TEXT: Record<number, string> = {
  200: 'OK', 201: 'Created', 202: 'Accepted', 204: 'No Content',
  400: 'Bad Request', 401: 'Unauthorized', 403: 'Forbidden', 404: 'Not Found', 409: 'Conflict',
  422: 'Unprocessable Entity', 429: 'Too Many Requests',
  500: 'Internal Server Error', 502: 'Bad Gateway', 503: 'Service Unavailable',
}

/** A JSON Response with the standard status text, e.g. jsonResponse({ error: 'nope' }, 401) -> "401 Unauthorized". */
export function jsonResponse(body: unknown, status = 200): Response {
  const init = { status, statusText: STATUS_TEXT[status] ?? '', headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' } }
  return new Response(status === 204 ? null : JSON.stringify(body), init)
}

function parseJson(raw: string | undefined): unknown {
  if (raw === undefined) return undefined
  try {
    return JSON.parse(raw)
  } catch {
    return undefined
  }
}

function urlMatches(template: string, actual: string): boolean {
  const t = splitUrl(template)
  const a = splitUrl(actual)
  if (!t || !a) return false
  const tHost = t.host.split('.')
  const aHost = a.host.split('.')
  if (tHost.slice(-2).join('.') !== aHost.slice(-2).join('.')) return false
  const tPath = t.path.replace(/\/+$/, '').split('/')
  const aPath = a.path.replace(/\/+$/, '').split('/')
  if (tPath.length !== aPath.length) return false
  return tPath.every((segment, i) => isPlaceholder(segment) || segment === aPath[i])
}

function splitUrl(url: string): { host: string; path: string } | null {
  const match = url.match(/^https?:\/\/([^/?#]+)([^?#]*)/i)
  return match ? { host: (match[1] ?? '').toLowerCase(), path: match[2] || '/' } : null
}

function isPlaceholder(segment: string): boolean {
  return /^\{[^}]+\}$|^:[A-Za-z_]\w*$|^<[^>]+>$/.test(segment)
}

export interface ConnectorConfig {
  /** Airtable Base ID (e.g., 'appXXXXXXXXXXXXXX') */
  baseId: string;
  /** Airtable Table Name or ID */
  tableName: string;
  /** Airtable Personal Access Token. In production, set via AIRTABLE_API_KEY env var. */
  apiKey: string;
  /** Optional record ID. If omitted, the connector will look up the record by email using filterByFormula. */
  recordId?: string;
  /** Injected fetch for testing. Uses global fetch in production. */
  fetch?: (input: RequestInfo | URL, init?: RequestInit) => Promise<Response>;
}

export interface JotformSubmission {
  email: string;
  first_name?: string;
  last_name?: string;
  phone?: string;
  address?: string;
}

export interface UpdateResult {
  recordId: string;
  updatedFields: Record<string, string>;
}

const FIELD_MAP: ReadonlyArray<{ source: keyof JotformSubmission; target: string }> = [
  { source: 'first_name', target: 'First Name' },
  { source: 'last_name', target: 'Last Name' },
  { source: 'phone', target: 'Phone' },
  { source: 'address', target: 'Address' },
] as const;

function buildAirtableUrl(baseId: string, tableName: string, recordId?: string): string {
  const base = `https://api.airtable.com/v0/${encodeURIComponent(baseId)}/${encodeURIComponent(tableName)}`;
  return recordId ? `${base}/${encodeURIComponent(recordId)}` : base;
}

async function findRecordByEmail(
  fetchImpl: (input: RequestInfo | URL, init?: RequestInit) => Promise<Response>,
  baseId: string,
  tableName: string,
  apiKey: string,
  email: string,
): Promise<string> {
  const formula = `{Email} = '${email.replace(/'/g, "\\'")}'`;
  const url = `${buildAirtableUrl(baseId, tableName)}?filterByFormula=${encodeURIComponent(formula)}`;
  const response = await fetchImpl(url, {
    method: 'GET',
    headers: {
      Authorization: `Bearer ${apiKey}`,
      'Content-Type': 'application/json',
    },
  });
  if (!response.ok) {
    throw new Error(`Airtable lookup failed: ${response.status} ${response.statusText} at GET ${url}`);
  }
  const data = (await response.json()) as { records?: Array<{ id: string }> };
  const record = data.records?.[0];
  if (!record) {
    throw new Error(`No Airtable record found for email: ${email}`);
  }
  return record.id;
}

function buildPatchBody(submission: JotformSubmission): Record<string, string> {
  const fields: Record<string, string> = {};
  for (const { source, target } of FIELD_MAP) {
    const value = submission[source];
    if (value !== undefined && value !== '') {
      fields[target] = value;
    }
  }
  return fields;
}

export async function handle(payload: JotformSubmission, config: ConnectorConfig): Promise<UpdateResult> {
  const fetchImpl = config.fetch ?? fetch;
  const { baseId, tableName, apiKey, recordId: providedRecordId } = config;

  if (!payload.email || payload.email.trim() === '') {
    throw new Error('Missing required field: email');
  }

  const recordId = providedRecordId ?? (await findRecordByEmail(fetchImpl, baseId, tableName, apiKey, payload.email));

  const fields = buildPatchBody(payload);
  if (Object.keys(fields).length === 0) {
    return { recordId, updatedFields: {} };
  }

  const patchUrl = buildAirtableUrl(baseId, tableName, recordId);
  const patchResponse = await fetchImpl(patchUrl, {
    method: 'PATCH',
    headers: {
      Authorization: `Bearer ${apiKey}`,
      'Content-Type': 'application/json',
    },
    body: JSON.stringify({ fields }),
  });

  if (!patchResponse.ok) {
    throw new Error(`Airtable update failed: ${patchResponse.status} ${patchResponse.statusText} at PATCH ${patchUrl}`);
  }

  const patchData = (await patchResponse.json()) as { id: string; fields: Record<string, string> };
  return { recordId: patchData.id, updatedFields: patchData.fields };
}

# Jotform to Airtable Connector

Updates an Airtable record with data from a Jotform submission. The connector looks up the record by email (using `filterByFormula`) and performs a partial update (PATCH) — only fields that have non-empty values in the submission are sent, preserving existing Airtable data for omitted fields.

## Configuration

| Config Property | Environment Variable | Required | Description |
|-----------------|---------------------|----------|-------------|
| `baseId` | — | Yes | Airtable Base ID (e.g., `appXXXXXXXXXXXXXX`) |
| `tableName` | — | Yes | Airtable Table Name or ID |
| `apiKey` | `AIRTABLE_API_KEY` | Yes | Airtable Personal Access Token |
| `recordId` | — | No | If provided, skips the email lookup and updates this record directly |

## Usage Example

```typescript
import { handle, ConnectorConfig, JotformSubmission } from './connector';

const config: ConnectorConfig = {
  baseId: 'appAbc123',
  tableName: 'Leads',
  apiKey: process.env.AIRTABLE_API_KEY!, // set in environment
};

const jotformPayload: JotformSubmission = {
  email: 'user@example.com',
  first_name: 'John',
  last_name: 'Doe',
  phone: '555-1234',
  address: '123 Main St',
};

const result = await handle(jotformPayload, config);
console.log('Updated record:', result.recordId);
console.log('Fields written:', result.updatedFields);
```

## Field Mapping

| Jotform Field | Airtable Field | Notes |
|---------------|----------------|-------|
| `email` | (filter) | Used to find the record via `filterByFormula={Email} = '...'` |
| `first_name` | `First Name` | Only included in PATCH if non-empty |
| `last_name` | `Last Name` | Only included in PATCH if non-empty |
| `phone` | `Phone` | Only included in PATCH if non-empty |
| `address` | `Address` | Only included in PATCH if non-empty |

## Assumptions

- The Jotform submission contains fields named `email`, `first_name`, `last_name`, `phone`, and `address`.
- The Airtable table has columns named `First Name`, `Last Name`, `Phone`, and `Address`.
- The `email` field in Jotform uniquely identifies the record in Airtable.
- The integration checks each field value and only includes non-empty values in the PATCH body.
- Airtable API rate limits (5 requests/second/base) are handled by the caller; 429 responses will throw.
- Jotform webhooks deliver JSON via a bridge service (e.g., Zapier, Make) that reformats the multipart/form-data payload to top-level `application/json`.

## Error Handling

- Throws descriptive `Error` if `email` is missing or empty.
- Throws `Error` with status code and endpoint on any non-2xx response from Airtable.
- Throws `Error` if no record is found for the given email.

export interface DocumentedEndpoint {
  method: string
  /** As documented; may contain placeholders such as {id}, :id, <id> or a region host like usX. */
  url: string
  response: unknown
}

/** Target endpoints the connector may call, in the documented order, with their documented responses. */
export const TARGET_ENDPOINTS: DocumentedEndpoint[] = [
  {
    "method": "PATCH",
    "url": "https://api.airtable.com/v0/{baseId}/{tableName}/{recordId}",
    "response": {
      "id": "rec123",
      "fields": {
        "First Name": "John",
        "Last Name": "Doe",
        "Phone": "555-1234",
        "Address": "123 Main St"
      },
      "createdTime": "2026-01-25T07:39:00.000Z"
    }
  }
]

export interface RecordedCall {
  method: string
  url: string
  /** The request body exactly as sent (usually a JSON string). */
  body: string | undefined
  /** The body parsed as JSON, or undefined when it is not JSON. */
  json: unknown
  headers: Headers
}

/** The documented endpoint a request matches, placeholders and region subdomains included. */
export function findEndpoint(method: string, url: string): DocumentedEndpoint | undefined {
  return TARGET_ENDPOINTS.find((endpoint) => endpoint.method === method.toUpperCase() && urlMatches(endpoint.url, url))
}

/**
 * A fake fetch that answers every documented endpoint with its documented response and
 * rejects anything else. Use it in the contract test:
 *
 *   const { fetch, calls } = contractFetch()
 *   await handle(SOURCE_EXAMPLE as MyInput, { ...config, fetch })
 *   expect(calls.length).toBeGreaterThan(0)
 */
export function contractFetch(): { fetch: typeof fetch; calls: RecordedCall[] } {
  return fakeFetch((request) => {
    const endpoint = findEndpoint(request.method, request.url)
    if (!endpoint) throw new Error(`contract: ${request.method} ${request.url} is not a documented endpoint`)
    return jsonResponse(endpoint.response)
  })
}

/**
 * A correctly typed fake fetch for every other test. The handler receives the recorded
 * request: { method, url, body (string as sent), json (parsed body), headers (Headers) }.
 *
 *   const { fetch, calls } = fakeFetch((req) => req.url.endsWith('/deals') ? jsonResponse({ id: 1 }, 201) : jsonResponse({}, 404))
 */
export function fakeFetch(
  handler: (request: RecordedCall) => Response | Promise<Response>,
): { fetch: typeof fetch; calls: RecordedCall[] } {
  const calls: RecordedCall[] = []
  const fake = async (input: string | URL | Request, init: RequestInit = {}): Promise<Response> => {
    const url = input instanceof Request ? input.url : String(input)
    const method = (init.method ?? (input instanceof Request ? input.method : 'GET')).toUpperCase()
    const body = typeof init.body === 'string' ? init.body : init.body == null ? undefined : String(init.body)
    const call: RecordedCall = { method, url, body, json: parseJson(body), headers: new Headers(init.headers) }
    calls.push(call)
    return handler(call)
  }
  return { fetch: fake as typeof fetch, calls }
}

const STATUS_TEXT: Record<number, string> = {
  200: 'OK', 201: 'Created', 202: 'Accepted', 204: 'No Content',
  400: 'Bad Request', 401: 'Unauthorized', 403: 'Forbidden', 404: 'Not Found', 409: 'Conflict',
  422: 'Unprocessable Entity', 429: 'Too Many Requests',
  500: 'Internal Server Error', 502: 'Bad Gateway', 503: 'Service Unavailable',
}

/** A JSON Response with the standard status text, e.g. jsonResponse({ error: 'nope' }, 401) -> "401 Unauthorized". */
export function jsonResponse(body: unknown, status = 200): Response {
  const init = { status, statusText: STATUS_TEXT[status] ?? '', headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' } }
  return new Response(status === 204 ? null : JSON.stringify(body), init)
}

function parseJson(raw: string | undefined): unknown {
  if (raw === undefined) return undefined
  try {
    return JSON.parse(raw)
  } catch {
    return undefined
  }
}

function urlMatches(template: string, actual: string): boolean {
  const t = splitUrl(template)
  const a = splitUrl(actual)
  if (!t || !a) return false
  const tHost = t.host.split('.')
  const aHost = a.host.split('.')
  if (tHost.slice(-2).join('.') !== aHost.slice(-2).join('.')) return false
  const tPath = t.path.replace(/\/+$/, '').split('/')
  const aPath = a.path.replace(/\/+$/, '').split('/')
  if (tPath.length !== aPath.length) return false
  return tPath.every((segment, i) => isPlaceholder(segment) || segment === aPath[i])
}

function splitUrl(url: string): { host: string; path: string } | null {
  const match = url.match(/^https?:\/\/([^/?#]+)([^?#]*)/i)
  return match ? { host: (match[1] ?? '').toLowerCase(), path: match[2] || '/' } : null
}

function isPlaceholder(segment: string): boolean {
  return /^\{[^}]+\}$|^:[A-Za-z_]\w*$|^<[^>]+>$/.test(segment)
}

export interface ConnectorConfig {
  /** Salesforce instance host, e.g. "mycompany.my.salesforce.com" or full base URL "https://mycompany.my.salesforce.com" */
  salesforceInstance: string
  /** Bearer token for Salesforce REST API */
  accessToken: string
  /** Salesforce API version, e.g. "v68.0" */
  apiVersion?: string
  /** Injected fetch for testing */
  fetch?: typeof fetch
}

export interface HubSpotDealWebhookPayload {
  subscriptionId: string
  portalId: string
  eventId: string
  subscriptionType: string
  attemptNumber: number
  changeSource: string
  objectId: string
  propertyName: string
  propertyValue: string
  timestamp: number
  changes: Array<{ name: string; value: string }>
  object: {
    objectId: string
    properties: {
      dealid: string
      dealname: string
      website: string
    }
  }
}

export interface UpsertResult {
  salesforceAccountId: string
  created: boolean
  success: boolean
}

function getFetch(config: ConnectorConfig): typeof fetch {
  return config.fetch ?? fetch
}

function buildSalesforceBaseUrl(instance: string, apiVersion = 'v68.0'): string {
  const normalized = instance.replace(/^https?:\/\//, '').replace(/\/+$/, '')
  return `https://${normalized}/services/data/${apiVersion}`
}

function validatePayload(payload: unknown): HubSpotDealWebhookPayload {
  if (!payload || typeof payload !== 'object') {
    throw new Error('Invalid payload: expected an object')
  }
  const p = payload as Record<string, unknown>
  if (!p.object || typeof p.object !== 'object') {
    throw new Error('Missing required field: object')
  }
  const obj = p.object as Record<string, unknown>
  if (!obj.properties || typeof obj.properties !== 'object') {
    throw new Error('Missing required field: object.properties')
  }
  const props = obj.properties as Record<string, unknown>
  const required = ['dealid', 'dealname', 'website']
  for (const field of required) {
    if (!props[field] || typeof props[field] !== 'string') {
      throw new Error(`Missing or invalid required field: object.properties.${field}`)
    }
  }
  return payload as HubSpotDealWebhookPayload
}

export async function handle(
  payload: unknown,
  config: ConnectorConfig
): Promise<UpsertResult> {
  const validated = validatePayload(payload)
  const props = validated.object.properties
  const domain = props.website.trim().toLowerCase()
  const dealName = props.dealname.trim()
  const dealId = props.dealid.trim()

  if (!domain) {
    throw new Error('Domain (website) is empty')
  }

  const baseUrl = buildSalesforceBaseUrl(config.salesforceInstance, config.apiVersion)
  const encodedDomain = encodeURIComponent(domain)
  const url = `${baseUrl}/sobjects/Account/Website/${encodedDomain}`

  const body = {
    Name: dealName,
    Website: domain,
    Deal_ID__c: dealId
  }

  const fetchFn = getFetch(config)
  const response = await fetchFn(url, {
    method: 'PATCH',
    headers: {
      'Authorization': `Bearer ${config.accessToken}`,
      'Content-Type': 'application/json',
      'Accept': 'application/json'
    },
    body: JSON.stringify(body)
  })

  if (!response.ok) {
    const text = await response.text().catch(() => '')
    throw new Error(`Salesforce upsert failed: ${response.status} ${response.statusText} for PATCH ${url} - ${text}`)
  }

  const result = await response.json() as { id: string; success: boolean; created?: boolean; errors?: unknown[] }
  if (!result.success) {
    const errors = result.errors?.map(e => JSON.stringify(e)).join(', ') || 'unknown error'
    throw new Error(`Salesforce upsert returned success=false: ${errors}`)
  }

  return {
    salesforceAccountId: result.id,
    created: result.created ?? false,
    success: true
  }
}

# HubSpot Deal → Salesforce Account Upsert Connector

This connector processes HubSpot `deal.propertyChange` webhooks and upserts Salesforce Account records using the Website field as an external ID.

## What it does

1. Receives a HubSpot deal property change webhook payload
2. Extracts the domain (website), deal name, and deal ID from the payload
3. Calls Salesforce REST API `PATCH /services/data/vXX.X/sobjects/Account/Website/{domain}` to upsert an Account
4. Returns the Salesforce Account ID and whether the record was created or updated

## Configuration

| Config Property | Environment Variable | Description |
|-----------------|---------------------|-------------|
| `salesforceInstance` | `SALESFORCE_INSTANCE` | Salesforce instance host (e.g., `mycompany.my.salesforce.com` or full URL) |
| `accessToken` | `SALESFORCE_ACCESS_TOKEN` | Bearer token for Salesforce REST API authentication |
| `apiVersion` | `SALESFORCE_API_VERSION` | Optional. Salesforce API version (default: `v68.0`) |

## Usage Example

```typescript
import { handle } from './connector'

const payload = {
  // HubSpot deal.propertyChange webhook payload
  subscriptionId: '12345',
  portalId: '67890',
  eventId: 'abcde-12345-fghij',
  subscriptionType: 'deal.propertyChange',
  attemptNumber: 1,
  changeSource: 'CRM_UI',
  objectId: '98765',
  propertyName: 'website',
  propertyValue: 'example.com',
  timestamp: 1717020000000,
  changes: [{ name: 'website', value: 'example.com' }],
  object: {
    objectId: '98765',
    properties: {
      dealid: '98765',
      dealname: 'Acme Corporation Deal',
      website: 'example.com'
    }
  }
}

const config = {
  salesforceInstance: process.env.SALESFORCE_INSTANCE!,
  accessToken: process.env.SALESFORCE_ACCESS_TOKEN!,
  apiVersion: process.env.SALESFORCE_API_VERSION || 'v68.0'
}

const result = await handle(payload, config)
console.log(`Account ${result.salesforceAccountId} ${result.created ? 'created' : 'updated'}`)
```

## Field Mapping

| HubSpot Field | Salesforce Field | Notes |
|---------------|------------------|-------|
| `object.properties.website` | `Website` | Used as external ID for upsert; lowercased and URL-encoded |
| `object.properties.dealname` | `Name` | Account name when creating new record |
| `object.properties.dealid` | `Deal_ID__c` | Custom field storing originating HubSpot Deal ID |

## Assumptions

- HubSpot deal has an associated company or a property containing the website domain (provided in `object.properties.website`)
- Salesforce Account has a unique external ID field `Website` that matches the domain value
- The integration performs an upsert operation using the Website field as the external ID
- If no matching Account is found, a new Account is created with the Deal Name as the Account Name
- A custom field `Deal_ID__c` exists on the Salesforce Account object to store the originating HubSpot Deal ID
- HubSpot webhook delivers the full object properties in `object.properties` (not just the changed property)
- Salesforce API version 46.0+ is used (returns `created` field in response)
- Domain values are URL-encoded to handle special characters

## Error Handling

- Throws descriptive errors for missing required fields (`dealid`, `dealname`, `website`)
- Throws error with status code and endpoint for non-2xx Salesforce responses
- Throws error when Salesforce returns `success: false` in response body
- Validates that website/domain is not empty after trimming

export function fakeFetch(

  const calls: RecordedCall[] = []

    const call: RecordedCall = { method, url, body, json: parseJson(body), headers: new Headers(init.headers) }
    calls.push(call)
    return handler(call)

const STATUS_TEXT: Record<number, string> = {
  200: 'OK', 201: 'Created', 202: 'Accepted', 204: 'No Content',
  400: 'Bad Request', 401: 'Unauthorized', 403: 'Forbidden', 404: 'Not Found', 409: 'Conflict',
  422: 'Unprocessable Entity', 429: 'Too Many Requests',
  500: 'Internal Server Error', 502: 'Bad Gateway', 503: 'Service Unavailable',
}

/** A JSON Response with the standard status text, e.g. jsonResponse({ error: 'nope' }, 401) -> "401 Unauthorized". */
export function jsonResponse(body: unknown, status = 200): Response {
  const init = { status, statusText: STATUS_TEXT[status] ?? '', headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' } }
  return new Response(status === 204 ? null : JSON.stringify(body), init)
}

function parseJson(raw: string | undefined): unknown {
  if (raw === undefined) return undefined
  try {
    return JSON.parse(raw)
  } catch {
    return undefined
  }
}

function urlMatches(template: string, actual: string): boolean {
  const t = splitUrl(template)
  const a = splitUrl(actual)
  if (!t || !a) return false
  const tHost = t.host.split('.')
  const aHost = a.host.split('.')
  if (tHost.slice(-2).join('.') !== aHost.slice(-2).join('.')) return false
  const tPath = t.path.replace(/\/+$/, '').split('/')
  const aPath = a.path.replace(/\/+$/, '').split('/')
  if (tPath.length !== aPath.length) return false
  return tPath.every((segment, i) => isPlaceholder(segment) || segment === aPath[i])
}

function splitUrl(url: string): { host: string; path: string } | null {
  const match = url.match(/^https?:\/\/([^/?#]+)([^?#]*)/i)
  return match ? { host: (match[1] ?? '').toLowerCase(), path: match[2] || '/' } : null
}

function isPlaceholder(segment: string): boolean {
  return /^\{[^}]+\}$|^:[A-Za-z_]\w*$|^<[^>]+>$/.test(segment)
}

type FetchFn = (input: RequestInfo | URL, init?: RequestInit) => Promise<Response>;

export interface LinearWebhookPayload {
  action: string;
  type: string;
  data: {
    id: string;
    title: string;
    state: {
      name: string;
    };
    comments: {
      nodes: Array<{
        id: string;
        body: string;
        createdAt: string;
      }>;
      pageInfo: {
        hasNextPage: boolean;
        endCursor: string | null;
      };
    };
  };
  createdAt: string;
  webhookTimestamp: number;
}

export interface ConnectorConfig {
  linearWebhookSecret: string;
  discordWebhookId: string;
  discordWebhookToken: string;
  linearGraphqlUrl?: string;
  linearApiToken?: string;
  timestampToleranceMs?: number;
  fetch?: FetchFn;
}

export interface HandleResult {
  discordMessageId: string;
}

const DEFAULT_LINEAR_GRAPHQL_URL = 'https://api.linear.app/graphql';
const DEFAULT_TIMESTAMP_TOLERANCE_MS = 60_000;

const COMMENTS_QUERY = `
  query GetIssueComments($issueId: ID!, $after: String) {
    issue(id: $issueId) {
      comments(after: $after, first: 100) {
        nodes {
          id
          body
          createdAt
        }
        pageInfo {
          hasNextPage
          endCursor
        }
      }
    }
  }
`;

async function fetchAllComments(
  issueId: string,
  initialComments: LinearWebhookPayload['data']['comments'],
  config: ConnectorConfig
): Promise<Array<{ id: string; body: string; createdAt: string }>> {
  const allComments = [...initialComments.nodes];
  let hasNextPage = initialComments.pageInfo.hasNextPage;
  let endCursor = initialComments.pageInfo.endCursor;

  const graphqlUrl = config.linearGraphqlUrl ?? DEFAULT_LINEAR_GRAPHQL_URL;
  const fetchImpl = config.fetch ?? fetch;

  while (hasNextPage && endCursor) {
    const response = await fetchImpl(graphqlUrl, {
      method: 'POST',
      headers: {
        'Content-Type': 'application/json',
        ...(config.linearApiToken ? { Authorization: `Bearer ${config.linearApiToken}` } : {}),
      },
      body: JSON.stringify({
        query: COMMENTS_QUERY,
        variables: { issueId, after: endCursor },
      }),
    });

    if (!response.ok) {
      throw new Error(`Linear GraphQL request failed: ${response.status} ${response.statusText}`);
    }

    const data = (await response.json()) as {
      data?: {
        issue?: {
          comments: {
            nodes: Array<{ id: string; body: string; createdAt: string }>;
            pageInfo: { hasNextPage: boolean; endCursor: string | null };
          };
        };
      };
      errors?: Array<{ message: string }>;
    };

    if (data.errors?.length) {
      throw new Error(`Linear GraphQL errors: ${data.errors.map(e => e.message).join(', ')}`);
    }

    const commentsConnection = data.data?.issue?.comments;
    if (!commentsConnection) {
      throw new Error('Unexpected Linear GraphQL response shape');
    }

    allComments.push(...commentsConnection.nodes);
    hasNextPage = commentsConnection.pageInfo.hasNextPage;
    endCursor = commentsConnection.pageInfo.endCursor;
  }

  return allComments;
}

function formatDigest(title: string, comments: Array<{ body: string }>): string {
  const commentLines = comments.map(c => c.body).join('\n\n');
  return `**${title}**\n\n---\n${commentLines}`;
}

export async function handle(
  payload: LinearWebhookPayload,
  config: ConnectorConfig
): Promise<HandleResult> {
  if (payload.action !== 'update' || payload.type !== 'Issue') {
    throw new Error('Payload is not an Issue update event');
  }

  if (payload.data.state.name !== 'Closed') {
    throw new Error('Issue is not closed; skipping');
  }

  const now = Date.now();
  const tolerance = config.timestampToleranceMs ?? DEFAULT_TIMESTAMP_TOLERANCE_MS;
  if (Math.abs(now - payload.webhookTimestamp) > tolerance) {
    throw new Error('Webhook timestamp too old; possible replay attack');
  }

  const { id: issueId, title, comments: initialComments } = payload.data;

  const allComments = await fetchAllComments(issueId, initialComments, config);

  const content = formatDigest(title, allComments);

  const discordUrl = `https://discord.com/api/v10/webhooks/${config.discordWebhookId}/${config.discordWebhookToken}`;
  const fetchImpl = config.fetch ?? fetch;

  const response = await fetchImpl(discordUrl, {
    method: 'POST',
    headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' },
    body: JSON.stringify({ content }),
  });

  if (!response.ok) {
    throw new Error(`Discord webhook failed: ${response.status} ${response.statusText} at ${discordUrl}`);
  }

  const discordResponse = (await response.json()) as { id: string };
  return { discordMessageId: discordResponse.id };
}

# Linear Issue Closed → Discord Digest

This connector listens for Linear `issue.closed` webhooks, fetches all comments on the issue (including paginated pages via Linear's GraphQL API), formats them into a Markdown digest, and posts the digest to a Discord channel via a webhook.

## Configuration

The following environment variables must be set (or passed directly in the config object):

| Variable | Description | Required |
|----------|-------------|----------|
| `LINEAR_WEBHOOK_SECRET` | Secret used to verify the `Linear-Signature` header (verification is expected to be done by the caller; the connector only checks the payload timestamp). | Yes |
| `DISCORD_WEBHOOK_ID` | The Discord webhook ID (part of the webhook URL). | Yes |
| `DISCORD_WEBHOOK_TOKEN` | The Discord webhook token (part of the webhook URL). | Yes |
| `LINEAR_GRAPHQL_URL` | (Optional) Linear GraphQL API endpoint. Defaults to `https://api.linear.app/graphql`. | No |
| `LINEAR_API_TOKEN` | (Optional) Bearer token for Linear GraphQL API authentication. | No |
| `TIMESTAMP_TOLERANCE_MS` | (Optional) Maximum allowed age of the webhook timestamp in milliseconds. Defaults to 60,000 (60 seconds). | No |

## Usage Example

```typescript
import { handle } from './connector'

const payload = await req.json() // Linear webhook payload
const config = {
  linearWebhookSecret: process.env.LINEAR_WEBHOOK_SECRET!,
  discordWebhookId: process.env.DISCORD_WEBHOOK_ID!,
  discordWebhookToken: process.env.DISCORD_WEBHOOK_TOKEN!,
  linearGraphqlUrl: process.env.LINEAR_GRAPHQL_URL,
  linearApiToken: process.env.LINEAR_API_TOKEN,
  timestampToleranceMs: Number(process.env.TIMESTAMP_TOLERANCE_MS),
}

try {
  const result = await handle(payload, config)
  console.log('Posted to Discord:', result.discordMessageId)
} catch (err) {
  console.error('Failed to process webhook:', err)
}
```

## Assumptions

- The Linear webhook payload includes the issue data under `data` when `action` is `update` and `type` is `Issue`.
- Comments are included in `data.comments` as a connection with cursor-based pagination (`nodes` and `pageInfo`).
- If `pageInfo.hasNextPage` is true, additional comments are fetched via Linear's GraphQL API using the `endCursor` as the `after` parameter.
- The GraphQL query used is a fixed query (`GetIssueComments`) that returns the same connection shape.
- Discord webhook URL follows the pattern `https://discord.com/api/v10/webhooks/{webhook.id}/{webhook.token}`.
- The Discord message content is formatted as Markdown: bold issue title, a horizontal rule, then each comment body separated by blank lines.
- The connector does not verify the `Linear-Signature` header; it assumes the caller has done so. It only validates the `webhookTimestamp` against the current time (within the configured tolerance).
- The connector throws descriptive errors for missing required fields, non-closed issues, stale webhooks, Linear GraphQL failures, and Discord non-2xx responses.

export interface ConnectorConfig {
  githubToken: string
  githubOwner: string
  githubRepo: string
  zendeskSubdomain: string
  fetch?: typeof fetch
}

export interface ZendeskTicketCreatedPayload {
  detail: {
    subject: string
    description: string
    id: string
  }
}

export interface HandleResult {
  githubIssueNumber: number
  githubIssueUrl: string
  githubCommentId: number
  githubCommentUrl: string
}

async function githubRequest(
  config: ConnectorConfig,
  url: string,
  method: string,
  body: unknown,
): Promise<Response> {
  const fetchFn = config.fetch ?? fetch
  const response = await fetchFn(url, {
    method,
    headers: {
      Authorization: `Bearer ${config.githubToken}`,
      Accept: 'application/vnd.github+json',
      'Content-Type': 'application/json',
      'User-Agent': 'patchbay-connector',
    },
    body: JSON.stringify(body),
  })
  if (!response.ok) {
    throw new Error(`GitHub API error: ${response.status} ${response.statusText} for ${method} ${url}`)
  }
  return response
}

export async function handle(
  payload: ZendeskTicketCreatedPayload,
  config: ConnectorConfig,
): Promise<HandleResult> {
  if (!payload.detail?.subject) {
    throw new Error('Missing required field: detail.subject')
  }
  if (!payload.detail?.description) {
    throw new Error('Missing required field: detail.description')
  }
  if (!payload.detail?.id) {
    throw new Error('Missing required field: detail.id')
  }

  const issueUrl = `https://api.github.com/repos/${config.githubOwner}/${config.githubRepo}/issues`
  const issueResponse = await githubRequest(config, issueUrl, 'POST', {
    title: payload.detail.subject,
    body: payload.detail.description,
  })
  const issueData = (await issueResponse.json()) as { number: number; html_url: string }

  const commentUrl = `https://api.github.com/repos/${config.githubOwner}/${config.githubRepo}/issues/${issueData.number}/comments`
  const zendeskTicketUrl = `https://${config.zendeskSubdomain}.zendesk.com/agent/tickets/${payload.detail.id}`
  const commentResponse = await githubRequest(config, commentUrl, 'POST', {
    body: `Corresponding Zendesk ticket created: ${zendeskTicketUrl}`,
  })
  const commentData = (await commentResponse.json()) as { id: number; html_url: string }

  return {
    githubIssueNumber: issueData.number,
    githubIssueUrl: issueData.html_url,
    githubCommentId: commentData.id,
    githubCommentUrl: commentData.html_url,
  }
}

<file path="README.md">
# Zendesk to GitHub Issue Connector

Creates a GitHub issue when a Zendesk ticket is created, then posts a comment on the GitHub issue linking back to the Zendesk ticket.

## What it does

1. Receives a Zendesk `ticket.created` webhook payload
2. Extracts the ticket subject, description, and ID from `detail.subject`, `detail.description`, and `detail.id`
3. Creates a GitHub issue in the configured repository using the subject as title and description as body
4. Posts a comment on the created GitHub issue with a link to the Zendesk ticket
5. Returns the GitHub issue number, issue URL, comment ID, and comment URL

## Configuration

| Config Property | Environment Variable | Description |
|-----------------|---------------------|-------------|
| `githubToken` | `GITHUB_TOKEN` | GitHub personal access token with `repo` scope (or `public_repo` for public repos) |
| `githubOwner` | `GITHUB_OWNER` | GitHub repository owner (user or organization) |
| `githubRepo` | `GITHUB_REPO` | GitHub repository name |
| `zendeskSubdomain` | `ZENDESK_SUBDOMAIN` | Your Zendesk subdomain (e.g., `yoursubdomain` for `yoursubdomain.zendesk.com`) |

All secrets come from the config object at runtime. The connector never reads environment variables directly.

## Usage

```typescript
import { handle } from './connector'

const config = {
  githubToken: process.env.GITHUB_TOKEN!,
  githubOwner: process.env.GITHUB_OWNER!,
  githubRepo: process.env.GITHUB_REPO!,
  zendeskSubdomain: process.env.ZENDESK_SUBDOMAIN!,
}

const result = await handle(zendeskWebhookPayload, config)
console.log(`Created GitHub issue #${result.githubIssueNumber}: ${result.githubIssueUrl}`)
console.log(`Posted comment: ${result.githubCommentUrl}`)
```

## Assumptions

- The Zendesk ticket payload includes `detail.subject`, `detail.description`, and `detail.id` fields.
- The GitHub repository is pre-configured and accessible via the provided API token.
- The integration has permission to create issues and post comments in the target repository.
- The Zendesk webhook delivers the full ticket object upon creation in the `detail` field.
- The GitHub issue URL can be constructed as `https://github.com/{owner}/{repo}/issues/{issue_number}` after creation.
- The Zendesk ticket URL follows the pattern `https://{subdomain}.zendesk.com/agent/tickets/{ticket_id}`.

export interface ConnectorConfig {
  mailchimpApiKey: string
  mailchimpDatacenter: string
  mailchimpListId: string
  planIdToTagId?: Record<string, string>
  fetch?: typeof fetch
}

export interface StripeWebhookPayload {
  id: string
  object: string
  api_version: string
  created: number
  data?: {
    object?: {
      id: string
      object: string
      customer: string
      customer_email?: string
      metadata?: {
        plan_id?: string
      }
      payment_status?: string
      mode?: string
    }
  }
  livemode: boolean
}

export interface HandleResult {
  tagId: string
  subscriberEmail: string
  addedCount: number
}

async function addSubscriberToTag(
  config: ConnectorConfig,
  tagId: string,
  email: string
): Promise<number> {
  const url = `https://${config.mailchimpDatacenter}.api.mailchimp.com/3.0/lists/${config.mailchimpListId}/tags/${tagId}`
  const fetch = config.fetch ?? globalThis.fetch
  const response = await fetch(url, {
    method: 'POST',
    headers: {
      'Authorization': `Bearer ${config.mailchimpApiKey}`,
      'Content-Type': 'application/json',
    },
    body: JSON.stringify({
      members: [
        {
          email_address: email,
          status: 'subscribed',
        },
      ],
    }),
  })

  if (!response.ok) {
    throw new Error(`Mailchimp POST tag failed: ${response.status} ${response.statusText} at ${url}`)
  }

  const data = await response.json() as { added_count: number }
  return data.added_count
}

export async function handle(
  payload: StripeWebhookPayload,
  config: ConnectorConfig
): Promise<HandleResult> {
  if (!payload.data?.object) {
    throw new Error('Missing data.object in Stripe webhook payload')
  }

  const session = payload.data.object

  if (session.payment_status !== 'paid') {
    throw new Error(`Payment status is "${session.payment_status}", expected "paid"`)
  }

  if (session.mode !== 'subscription') {
    throw new Error(`Checkout mode is "${session.mode}", expected "subscription"`)
  }

  const email = session.customer_email
  if (!email) {
    throw new Error('Missing customer_email in Stripe checkout session')
  }

  const planId = session.metadata?.plan_id
  if (!planId) {
    throw new Error('Missing metadata.plan_id in Stripe checkout session')
  }

  const tagId = config.planIdToTagId?.[planId]
  if (!tagId) {
    throw new Error(`No tag ID configured for plan_id: ${planId}`)
  }

  const addedCount = await addSubscriberToTag(config, tagId, email)

  return {
    tagId,
    subscriberEmail: email,
    addedCount,
  }
}

<file path="README.md">
# Stripe to Mailchimp Connector

Adds a Stripe customer to a Mailchimp audience tag when a checkout session completes successfully.

## What it does

When a Stripe `checkout.session.completed` webhook fires with `payment_status: "paid"` and `mode: "subscription"`, this connector:

1. Extracts the customer email and plan identifier from the session metadata
2. Looks up the corresponding tag ID from the configured `planIdToTagId` mapping
3. Adds the subscriber to that tag in the specified Mailchimp audience (list)

## Configuration

| Environment Variable | Config Property | Description |
|---------------------|-----------------|-------------|
| `MAILCHIMP_API_KEY` | `mailchimpApiKey` | Mailchimp API key (format: `key-us1`) |
| `MAILCHIMP_DATACENTER` | `mailchimpDatacenter` | Mailchimp datacenter prefix (e.g., `us1`, `us2`) |
| `MAILCHIMP_LIST_ID` | `mailchimpListId` | The audience/list ID to add subscribers to |
| (none) | `planIdToTagId` | Optional mapping from Stripe `plan_id` to Mailchimp tag ID |

The first three are required. The connector also accepts an optional `fetch` function for testing.

## Usage Example

```typescript
import { handle, ConnectorConfig } from './connector'

const config: ConnectorConfig = {
  mailchimpApiKey: process.env.MAILCHIMP_API_KEY!,
  mailchimpDatacenter: process.env.MAILCHIMP_DATACENTER!,
  mailchimpListId: process.env.MAILCHIMP_LIST_ID!,
  planIdToTagId: {
    'pro_monthly': 'tag_abc123',
    'basic_monthly': 'tag_def456',
  },
}

// In your webhook handler:
const result = await handle(stripeWebhookPayload, config)
console.log(`Added ${result.subscriberEmail} to tag ${result.tagId}`)
```

## Assumptions

- The Stripe checkout session includes `metadata.plan_id` set at session creation time
- The Mailchimp audience (list) and tag already exist
- The `planIdToTagId` config maps each Stripe `plan_id` to the corresponding Mailchimp tag ID
- If the subscriber doesn't exist in the audience, they will be created with `subscribed` status
- The webhook payload includes `customer_email` (set during Checkout Session creation)

## Field Mapping

| Stripe Field | Mailchimp Field | Notes |
|-------------|----------------|-------|
| `data.object.customer_email` | `members[].email_address` | Direct mapping |
| `data.object.metadata.plan_id` | Used to look up tag ID via `planIdToTagId` config | Must have entry in config mapping |

## Error Handling

The connector throws descriptive errors for:
- Missing required fields in the webhook payload
- Non-paid payment status or non-subscription mode
- No tag ID configured for the given plan_id
- Non-2xx responses from Mailchimp API (includes status code and endpoint)

export interface DocumentedEndpoint {
  method: string
  /** As documented; may contain placeholders such as {id}, :id, <id> or a region host like usX. */
  url: string
  response: unknown
}

/** Target endpoints the connector may call, in the documented order, with their documented responses. */
export const TARGET_ENDPOINTS: DocumentedEndpoint[] = [
  {
    "method": "POST",
    "url": "https://<dc>.api.mailchimp.com/3.0/lists/{list_id}/tags/{tag_id}",
    "response": {
      "added_count": 1,
      "errors": []
    }
  }
]

export interface RecordedCall {
  method: string
  url: string
  /** The request body exactly as sent (usually a JSON string). */
  body: string | undefined
  /** The body parsed as JSON, or undefined when it is not JSON. */
  json: unknown
  headers: Headers
}

/** The documented endpoint a request matches, placeholders and region subdomains included. */
export function findEndpoint(method: string, url: string): DocumentedEndpoint | undefined {
  return TARGET_ENDPOINTS.find((endpoint) => endpoint.method === method.toUpperCase() && urlMatches(endpoint.url, url))
}

/**
 * A fake fetch that answers every documented endpoint with its documented response and
 * rejects anything else. Use it in the contract test:
 *
 *   const { fetch, calls } = contractFetch()
 *   await handle(SOURCE_EXAMPLE as MyInput, { ...config, fetch })
 *   expect(calls.length).toBeGreaterThan(0)
 */
export function contractFetch(): { fetch: typeof fetch; calls: RecordedCall[] } {
  return fakeFetch((request) => {
    const endpoint = findEndpoint(request.method, request.url)
    if (!endpoint) throw new Error(`contract: ${request.method} ${request.url} is not a documented endpoint`)
    return jsonResponse(endpoint.response)
  })
}

/**
 * A correctly typed fake fetch for every other test. The handler receives the recorded
 * request: { method, url, body (string as sent), json (parsed body), headers (Headers) }.
 *
 *   const { fetch, calls } = fakeFetch((req) => req.url.endsWith('/deals') ? jsonResponse({ id: 1 }, 201) : jsonResponse({}, 404))
 */
export function fakeFetch(
  handler: (request: RecordedCall) => Response | Promise<Response>,
): { fetch: typeof fetch; calls: RecordedCall[] } {
  const calls: RecordedCall[] = []
  const fake = async (input: string | URL | Request, init: RequestInit = {}): Promise<Response> => {
    const url = input instanceof Request ? input.url : String(input)
    const method = (init.method ?? (input instanceof Request ? input.method : 'GET')).toUpperCase()
    const body = typeof init.body === 'string' ? init.body : init.body == null ? undefined : String(init.body)
    const call: RecordedCall = { method, url, body, json: parseJson(body), headers: new Headers(init.headers) }
    calls.push(call)
    return handler(call)
  }
  return { fetch: fake as typeof fetch, calls }
}

const STATUS_TEXT: Record<number, string> = {
  200: 'OK', 201: 'Created', 202: 'Accepted', 204: 'No Content',
  400: 'Bad Request', 401: 'Unauthorized', 403: 'Forbidden', 404: 'Not Found', 409: 'Conflict',
  422: 'Unprocessable Entity', 429: 'Too Many Requests',
  500: 'Internal Server Error', 502: 'Bad Gateway', 503: 'Service Unavailable',
}

/** A JSON Response with the standard status text, e.g. jsonResponse({ error: 'nope' }, 401) -> "401 Unauthorized". */
export function jsonResponse(body: unknown, status = 200): Response {
  const init = { status, statusText: STATUS_TEXT[status] ?? '', headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' } }
  return new Response(status === 204 ? null : JSON.stringify(body), init)
}

function parseJson(raw: string | undefined): unknown {
  if (raw === undefined) return undefined
  try {
    return JSON.parse(raw)
  } catch {
    return undefined
  }
}

function urlMatches(template: string, actual: string): boolean {
  const t = splitUrl(template)
  const a = splitUrl(actual)
  if (!t || !a) return false
  const tHost = t.host.split('.')
  const aHost = a.host.split('.')
  if (tHost.slice(-2).join('.') !== aHost.slice(-2).join('.')) return false
  const tPath = t.path.replace(/\/+$/, '').split('/')
  const aPath = a.path.replace(/\/+$/, '').split('/')
  if (tPath.length !== aPath.length) return false
  return tPath.every((segment, i) => isPlaceholder(segment) || segment === aPath[i])
}

function splitUrl(url: string): { host: string; path: string } | null {
  const match = url.match(/^https?:\/\/([^/?#]+)([^?#]*)/i)
  return match ? { host: (match[1] ?? '').toLowerCase(), path: match[2] || '/' } : null
}

function isPlaceholder(segment: string): boolean {
  return /^\{[^}]+\}$|^:[A-Za-z_]\w*$|^<[^>]+>$/.test(segment)
}

export interface StripeInvoiceLineItem {
  id: string;
  description: string;
  amount: number;
  quantity?: number;
  discountable?: boolean;
  tax_rates?: Array<{ id: string }>;
}

export interface StripeInvoicePayload {
  id: string;
  url: string;
  lines: {
    data: StripeInvoiceLineItem[];
  };
}

export interface ConnectorConfig {
  stripeWebhookSecret: string;
  quickbooksOAuthAccessToken: string;
  quickbooksCompanyId: string;
  quickbooksCustomFieldDefinitionId?: string;
  defaultItemRef: { value: string; name: string };
  defaultTaxCodeRef: { value: string };
  fetch?: typeof fetch;
}

export interface HandleResult {
  quickbooksInvoiceId: string;
  syncToken: string;
  lineItemCount: number;
}

function validatePayload(payload: unknown): asserts payload is StripeInvoicePayload {
  if (!payload || typeof payload !== 'object') {
    throw new Error('Payload must be an object');
  }
  const p = payload as Record<string, unknown>;
  if (typeof p.id !== 'string' || !p.id) {
    throw new Error('Missing required field: id');
  }
  if (typeof p.url !== 'string' || !p.url) {
    throw new Error('Missing required field: url');
  }
  if (!p.lines || typeof p.lines !== 'object' || !('data' in p.lines)) {
    throw new Error('Missing required field: lines.data');
  }
  const lines = (p.lines as { data: unknown }).data;
  if (!Array.isArray(lines)) {
    throw new Error('lines.data must be an array');
  }
  for (const [index, line] of lines.entries()) {
    if (!line || typeof line !== 'object') {
      throw new Error(`lines.data[${index}] must be an object`);
    }
    const l = line as Record<string, unknown>;
    if (typeof l.id !== 'string' || !l.id) {
      throw new Error(`lines.data[${index}].id is required`);
    }
    if (typeof l.description !== 'string') {
      throw new Error(`lines.data[${index}].description is required`);
    }
    if (typeof l.amount !== 'number' || !Number.isFinite(l.amount)) {
      throw new Error(`lines.data[${index}].amount must be a finite number`);
    }
  }
}

function centsToDecimal(cents: number): number {
  return Math.round(cents) / 100;
}

export async function handle(
  payload: StripeInvoicePayload,
  config: ConnectorConfig
): Promise<HandleResult> {
  validatePayload(payload);

  const {
    quickbooksOAuthAccessToken,
    quickbooksCompanyId,
    quickbooksCustomFieldDefinitionId = '1',
    defaultItemRef,
    defaultTaxCodeRef,
    fetch,
  } = config;

  if (!fetch) {
    throw new Error('fetch implementation is required');
  }

  const lineItems = payload.lines.data.map((line) => {
    const unitPrice = centsToDecimal(line.amount);
    const quantity = line.quantity ?? 1;
    const amount = unitPrice * quantity;
    return {
      Description: line.description,
      Amount: amount,
      DetailType: 'SalesItemLineDetail',
      SalesItemLineDetail: {
        ItemRef: defaultItemRef,
        UnitPrice: unitPrice,
        Qty: quantity,
        TaxCodeRef: defaultTaxCodeRef,
      },
    };
  });

  const requestBody = {
    Line: lineItems,
    CustomField: [
      {
        DefinitionId: quickbooksCustomFieldDefinitionId,
        StringValue: payload.url,
      },
    ],
  };

  const url = `https://quickbooks.api.intuit.com/v3/company/${quickbooksCompanyId}/invoice`;
  const response = await fetch(url, {
    method: 'POST',
    headers: {
      Authorization: `Bearer ${quickbooksOAuthAccessToken}`,
      Accept: 'application/json',
      'Content-Type': 'application/json',
    },
    body: JSON.stringify(requestBody),
  });

  if (!response.ok) {
    const text = await response.text().catch(() => '');
    throw new Error(
      `QuickBooks API error: ${response.status} ${response.statusText} for POST ${url}: ${text}`
    );
  }

  const data = (await response.json()) as {
    Invoice?: { Id?: string; SyncToken?: string };
  };

  if (!data.Invoice?.Id) {
    throw new Error('QuickBooks response missing Invoice.Id');
  }

  return {
    quickbooksInvoiceId: data.Invoice.Id,
    syncToken: data.Invoice.SyncToken ?? '',
    lineItemCount: lineItems.length,
  };
}

# Stripe Invoice to QuickBooks Connector

Creates a QuickBooks invoice with line items when a Stripe invoice is finalized, and attaches the Stripe invoice URL as a custom field.

## What it does

1. Receives a Stripe `invoice.finalized` webhook payload (already verified).
2. Validates the payload contains required fields: invoice ID, hosted URL, and line items.
3. Maps each Stripe line item to a QuickBooks sales line item:
   - Converts amount from cents to decimal (e.g., 1000 → 10.00)
   - Uses configured default QuickBooks item reference (`ItemRef`) and tax code reference (`TaxCodeRef`)
   - Applies quantity (defaults to 1)
4. Posts a single invoice creation request to QuickBooks Online API with all line items.
5. Stores the Stripe hosted invoice URL in a QuickBooks custom field (pre-defined in the company file).
6. Returns the created QuickBooks invoice ID, sync token, and line item count.

## Configuration

| Config Property | Environment Variable | Required | Description |
|-----------------|----------------------|----------|-------------|
| `stripeWebhookSecret` | `STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET` | Yes | Stripe webhook signing secret (used by the webhook receiver, not directly by this connector). |
| `quickbooksOAuthAccessToken` | `QUICKBOOKS_OAUTH_ACCESS_TOKEN` | Yes | OAuth 2.0 Bearer token for QuickBooks API authentication. |
| `quickbooksCompanyId` | `QUICKBOOKS_COMPANY_ID` | Yes | QuickBooks company ID (realm ID) for the API endpoint. |
| `quickbooksCustomFieldDefinitionId` | `QUICKBOOKS_CUSTOM_FIELD_DEFINITION_ID` | No (default: `"1"`) | Definition ID of the pre-created custom field in QuickBooks that will hold the Stripe invoice URL. |
| `defaultItemRef` | — | Yes | Default QuickBooks item reference for line items: `{ value: string, name: string }`. Used when a Stripe line item cannot be matched to a specific QuickBooks item. |
| `defaultTaxCodeRef` | — | Yes | Default QuickBooks tax code reference: `{ value: string }`. Used for all line items. |
| `fetch` | — | No | Injected `fetch` implementation (for testing or non-browser environments). |

## Usage Example

```typescript
import { handle, ConnectorConfig, StripeInvoicePayload } from './connector';

const config: ConnectorConfig = {
  stripeWebhookSecret: process.env.STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET!,
  quickbooksOAuthAccessToken: process.env.QUICKBOOKS_OAUTH_ACCESS_TOKEN!,
  quickbooksCompanyId: process.env.QUICKBOOKS_COMPANY_ID!,
  quickbooksCustomFieldDefinitionId: process.env.QUICKBOOKS_CUSTOM_FIELD_DEFINITION_ID ?? '1',
  defaultItemRef: { value: '1', name: 'Service' },
  defaultTaxCodeRef: { value: 'TAX' },
};

// Inside your Stripe webhook handler (after signature verification):
const stripePayload: StripeInvoicePayload = req.body; // parsed JSON
const result = await handle(stripePayload, config);
console.log(`Created QuickBooks invoice ${result.quickbooksInvoiceId} with ${result.lineItemCount} line items`);
```

## Assumptions

- The Stripe webhook secret is configured and the `invoice.finalized` event fires with full line item data.
- A QuickBooks company file is already set up and the integration has OAuth credentials with write access.
- Each Stripe line item can be matched to an existing QuickBooks item by ID or description; if no match exists, the integration uses the configured `defaultItemRef`.
- The QuickBooks API allows line items to be posted to an invoice in a single request; the payload includes all line items for the invoice.
- The Stripe invoice URL is stored in a pre-defined QuickBooks custom field (DefinitionId) as the standard QuickBooks API does not have a dedicated URL field.
- Amounts in Stripe are in cents (smallest currency unit); QuickBooks expects decimal format (e.g., 1000 cents = 10.00).
- Tax codes and items referenced in `defaultTaxCodeRef` and `defaultItemRef` exist in the QuickBooks company file.
- The connector does not verify the Stripe webhook signature; that should be done by the webhook receiver before calling `handle`.

export interface RecordedCall {
  method: string
  url: string
  /** The request body exactly as sent (usually a JSON string). */
  body: string | undefined
  /** The body parsed as JSON, or undefined when it is not JSON. */
  json: unknown
  headers: Headers

/** The documented endpoint a request matches, placeholders and region subdomains included. */
export function findEndpoint(method: string, url: string): DocumentedEndpoint | undefined {
  return TARGET_ENDPOINTS.find((endpoint) => endpoint.method === method.toUpperCase() && urlMatches(endpoint.url, url))
}

/**
 * A fake fetch that answers every documented endpoint with its documented response and
 * rejects anything else. Use it in the contract test:
 *
 *   const { fetch, calls } = contractFetch()
 *   await handle(SOURCE_EXAMPLE as MyInput, { ...config, fetch })
 *   expect(calls.length).toBeGreaterThan(0)
 */
export function contractFetch(): { fetch: typeof fetch; calls: RecordedCall[] } {
  return fakeFetch((request) => {
    const endpoint = findEndpoint(request.method, request.url)
    if (!endpoint) throw new Error(`contract: ${request.method} ${request.url} is not a documented endpoint`)
    return jsonResponse(endpoint.response)
  })
}

/**
 * A correctly typed fake fetch for every other test. The handler receives the recorded
 * request: { method, url, body (string as sent), json (parsed body), headers (Headers) }.
 *
 *   const { fetch, calls } = fakeFetch((req) => req.url.endsWith('/deals') ? jsonResponse({ id: 1 }, 201) : jsonResponse({}, 404))
 */
export function fakeFetch(
  handler: (request: RecordedCall) => Response | Promise<Response>,
): { fetch: typeof fetch; calls: RecordedCall[] } {
  const calls: RecordedCall[] = []
  const fake = async (input: string | URL | Request, init: RequestInit = {}): Promise<Response> => {
    const url = input instanceof Request ? input.url : String(input)
    const method = (init.method ?? (input instanceof Request ? input.method : 'GET')).toUpperCase()
    const body = typeof init.body === 'string' ? init.body : init.body == null ? undefined : String(init.body)
    const call: RecordedCall = { method, url, body, json: parseJson(body), headers: new Headers(init.headers) }
    calls.push(call)
    return handler(call)
  }
  return { fetch: fake as typeof fetch, calls }
}

const STATUS_TEXT: Record<number, string> = {
  200: 'OK', 201: 'Created', 202: 'Accepted', 204: 'No Content',
  400: 'Bad Request', 401: 'Unauthorized', 403: 'Forbidden', 404: 'Not Found', 409: 'Conflict',
  422: 'Unprocessable Entity', 429: 'Too Many Requests',
  500: 'Internal Server Error', 502: 'Bad Gateway', 503: 'Service Unavailable',
}

/** A JSON Response with the standard status text, e.g. jsonResponse({ error: 'nope' }, 401) -> "401 Unauthorized". */
export function jsonResponse(body: unknown, status = 200): Response {
  const init = { status, statusText: STATUS_TEXT[status] ?? '', headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' } }
  return new Response(status === 204 ? null : JSON.stringify(body), init)
}

function parseJson(raw: string | undefined): unknown {
  if (raw === undefined) return undefined
  try {
    return JSON.parse(raw)
  } catch {
    return undefined
  }
}

function urlMatches(template: string, actual: string): boolean {
  const t = splitUrl(template)
  const a = splitUrl(actual)
  if (!t || !a) return false
  const tHost = t.host.split('.')
  const aHost = a.host.split('.')
  if (tHost.slice(-2).join('.') !== aHost.slice(-2).join('.')) return false
  const tPath = t.path.replace(/\/+$/, '').split('/')
  const aPath = a.path.replace(/\/+$/, '').split('/')
  if (tPath.length !== aPath.length) return false
  return tPath.every((segment, i) => isPlaceholder(segment) || segment === aPath[i])
}

function splitUrl(url: string): { host: string; path: string } | null {
  const match = url.match(/^https?:\/\/([^/?#]+)([^?#]*)/i)
  return match ? { host: (match[1] ?? '').toLowerCase(), path: match[2] || '/' } : null
}

function isPlaceholder(segment: string): boolean {
  return /^\{[^}]+\}$|^:[A-Za-z_]\w*$|^<[^>]+>$/.test(segment)
}
