export interface RecordedCall {
  method: string
  url: string
  /** The request body exactly as sent (usually a JSON string). */
  body: string | undefined
  /** The body parsed as JSON, or undefined when it is not JSON. */
  json: unknown
  headers: Headers
}

/** The documented endpoint a request matches, placeholders and region subdomains included. */
export function findEndpoint(method: string, url: string): DocumentedEndpoint | undefined {
  return TARGET_ENDPOINTS.find((endpoint) => endpoint.method === method.toUpperCase() && urlMatches(endpoint.url, url))
}

/**
 * A fake fetch that answers every documented endpoint with its documented response and
 * rejects anything else. Use it in the contract test:
 *
 *   const { fetch, calls } = contractFetch()
 *   await handle(SOURCE_EXAMPLE as MyInput, { ...config, fetch })
 *   expect(calls.length).toBeGreaterThan(0)
 */
export function contractFetch(): { fetch: typeof fetch; calls: RecordedCall[] } {
  return fakeFetch((request) => {
    const endpoint = findEndpoint(request.method, request.url)
    if (!endpoint) throw new Error(`contract: ${request.method} ${request.url} is not a documented endpoint`)
    return jsonResponse(endpoint.response)
  })
}

/**
 * A correctly typed fake fetch for every other test. The handler receives the recorded
 * request: { method, url, body (string as sent), json (parsed body), headers (Headers) }.
 *
 *   const { fetch, calls } = fakeFetch((req) => req.url.endsWith('/deals') ? jsonResponse({ id: 1 }, 201) : jsonResponse({}, 404))
 */
export function fakeFetch(
  handler: (request: RecordedCall) => Response | Promise<Response>,
): { fetch: typeof fetch; calls: RecordedCall[] } {
  const calls: RecordedCall[] = []
  const fake = async (input: string | URL | Request, init: RequestInit = {}): Promise<Response> => {
    const url = input instanceof Request ? input.url : String(input)
    const method = (init.method ?? (input instanceof Request ? input.method : 'GET')).toUpperCase()
    const body = typeof init.body === 'string' ? init.body : init.body == null ? undefined : String(init.body)
    const call: RecordedCall = { method, url, body, json: parseJson(body), headers: new Headers(init.headers) }
    calls.push(call)
    return handler(call)
  }
  return { fetch: fake as typeof fetch, calls }
}

const STATUS_TEXT: Record<number, string> = {
  200: 'OK', 201: 'Created', 202: 'Accepted', 204: 'No Content',
  400: 'Bad Request', 401: 'Unauthorized', 403: 'Forbidden', 404: 'Not Found', 409: 'Conflict',
  422: 'Unprocessable Entity', 429: 'Too Many Requests',
  500: 'Internal Server Error', 502: 'Bad Gateway', 503: 'Service Unavailable',
}

/** A JSON Response with the standard status text, e.g. jsonResponse({ error: 'nope' }, 401) -> "401 Unauthorized". */
export function jsonResponse(body: unknown, status = 200): Response {
  const init = { status, statusText: STATUS_TEXT[status] ?? '', headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' } }
  return new Response(status === 204 ? null : JSON.stringify(body), init)
}

function parseJson(raw: string | undefined): unknown {
  if (raw === undefined) return undefined
  try {
    return JSON.parse(raw)
  } catch {
    return undefined
  }
}

function urlMatches(template: string, actual: string): boolean {
  const t = splitUrl(template)
  const a = splitUrl(actual)
  if (!t || !a) return false
  const tHost = t.host.split('.')
  const aHost = a.host.split('.')
  if (tHost.slice(-2).join('.') !== aHost.slice(-2).join('.')) return false
  const tPath = t.path.replace(/\/+$/, '').split('/')
  const aPath = a.path.replace(/\/+$/, '').split('/')
  if (tPath.length !== aPath.length) return false
  return tPath.every((segment, i) => isPlaceholder(segment) || segment === aPath[i])
}

function splitUrl(url: string): { host: string; path: string } | null {
  const match = url.match(/^https?:\/\/([^/?#]+)([^?#]*)/i)
  return match ? { host: (match[1] ?? '').toLowerCase(), path: match[2] || '/' } : null
}

function isPlaceholder(segment: string): boolean {
  return /^\{[^}]+\}$|^:[A-Za-z_]\w*$|^<[^>]+>$/.test(segment)
}

export interface ConnectorConfig {
  /** Slack Bot User OAuth Token (xoxb-...). */
  slackBotToken: string
  /** Slack channel ID (e.g., C01ABCD2EFG) or normalized channel name. */
  slackChannel: string
  /** Optional fetch implementation for testing. */
  fetch?: typeof fetch
}

export interface CalendlyInvitee {
  name: string
  email: string
}

export interface CalendlyAnswer {
  question: string
  answer: string
}

export interface CalendlyWebhookPayload {
  invitee: CalendlyInvitee
  answers: CalendlyAnswer[]
}

export interface SlackPostMessageResponse {
  ok: boolean
  channel: string
  ts: string
}

export interface HandleResult {
  slackMessageTs: string
  slackChannel: string
}

function validatePayload(payload: unknown): CalendlyWebhookPayload {
  if (!payload || typeof payload !== 'object') {
    throw new Error('Payload must be an object')
  }
  const p = payload as Record<string, unknown>
  if (!p.invitee || typeof p.invitee !== 'object') {
    throw new Error('Missing required field: invitee')
  }
  const invitee = p.invitee as Record<string, unknown>
  if (typeof invitee.name !== 'string' || !invitee.name.trim()) {
    throw new Error('Missing required field: invitee.name')
  }
  if (typeof invitee.email !== 'string' || !invitee.email.trim()) {
    throw new Error('Missing required field: invitee.email')
  }
  if (!Array.isArray(p.answers)) {
    throw new Error('Missing required field: answers (must be an array)')
  }
  for (const [idx, ans] of p.answers.entries()) {
    if (!ans || typeof ans !== 'object') {
      throw new Error(`answers[${idx}] must be an object`)
    }
    const a = ans as Record<string, unknown>
    if (typeof a.question !== 'string') {
      throw new Error(`answers[${idx}].question must be a string`)
    }
    if (typeof a.answer !== 'string') {
      throw new Error(`answers[${idx}].answer must be a string`)
    }
  }
  return payload as CalendlyWebhookPayload
}

function formatMessage(payload: CalendlyWebhookPayload): string {
  const lines: string[] = []
  lines.push(payload.invitee.name)
  lines.push(payload.invitee.email)
  for (const ans of payload.answers) {
    lines.push(`- ${ans.question}: ${ans.answer}`)
  }
  return lines.join('\n')
}

export async function handle(
  payload: unknown,
  config: ConnectorConfig
): Promise<HandleResult> {
  const validated = validatePayload(payload)
  const fetchImpl = config.fetch ?? fetch

  if (!config.slackBotToken || typeof config.slackBotToken !== 'string') {
    throw new Error('Config missing required field: slackBotToken')
  }
  if (!config.slackChannel || typeof config.slackChannel !== 'string') {
    throw new Error('Config missing required field: slackChannel')
  }

  const text = formatMessage(validated)
  const body = JSON.stringify({ channel: config.slackChannel, text })

  const response = await fetchImpl('https://slack.com/api/chat.postMessage', {
    method: 'POST',
    headers: {
      'Authorization': `Bearer ${config.slackBotToken}`,
      'Content-Type': 'application/json'
    },
    body
  })

  if (!response.ok) {
    throw new Error(`Slack API error: ${response.status} ${response.statusText} for POST https://slack.com/api/chat.postMessage`)
  }

  const data = await response.json() as SlackPostMessageResponse
  if (!data.ok) {
    throw new Error('Slack API returned ok: false')
  }

  return {
    slackMessageTs: data.ts,
    slackChannel: data.channel
  }
}

<file path="README.md">
# Calendly to Slack Connector

Posts a formatted message to a Slack channel when a Calendly meeting is booked via the `invitee.created` webhook.

## What it does

1. Receives a Calendly webhook payload containing the invitee's name, email, and their answers to scheduling questions.
2. Formats these fields into a plain-text message block.
3. Sends the message to a configured Slack channel using `chat.postMessage`.

## Configuration

| Config Key | Environment Variable | Description |
|------------|---------------------|-------------|
| `slackBotToken` | `SLACK_BOT_TOKEN` | Slack Bot User OAuth Token (starts with `xoxb-`). Must have `chat:write` scope. |
| `slackChannel` | `SLACK_CHANNEL_ID` | Slack channel ID (e.g., `C01ABCD2EFG`) or normalized channel name. |

## Usage Example

```typescript
import { handle } from './connector'

const payload = {
  invitee: { name: 'Jane Doe', email: 'jane.doe@example.com' },
  answers: [
    { question: 'What is your company?', answer: 'Acme Corp' },
    { question: 'How did you hear about us?', answer: 'Google search' }
  ]
}

const config = {
  slackBotToken: process.env.SLACK_BOT_TOKEN!,
  slackChannel: process.env.SLACK_CHANNEL_ID!
}

const result = await handle(payload, config)
console.log(`Posted to ${result.slackChannel} at ${result.slackMessageTs}`)
```

## Assumptions

- The Calendly webhook payload includes an `invitee` object with `name` and `email` fields.
- The Calendly webhook payload includes an `answers` array containing the invitee's responses to scheduling questions.
- The Slack channel ID or name is known and the integration has permission to post messages.
- The posted message will be a plain text block combining name, email and answers.
- Webhook signature validation (using the secret configured during Calendly subscription creation) is handled upstream; this connector does not verify signatures.

export interface DocumentedEndpoint {
  method: string
  /** As documented; may contain placeholders such as {id}, :id, <id> or a region host like usX. */
  url: string
  response: unknown
}

/** Target endpoints the connector may call, in the documented order, with their documented responses. */
export const TARGET_ENDPOINTS: DocumentedEndpoint[] = [
  {
    "method": "POST",
    "url": "https://slack.com/api/chat.postMessage",
    "response": {
      "ok": true,
      "channel": "C01ABCD2EFG",
      "ts": "1717000000.000200"
    }
  }
]

export interface RecordedCall {
  method: string
  url: string
  /** The request body exactly as sent (usually a JSON string). */
  body: string | undefined
  /** The body parsed as JSON, or undefined when it is not JSON. */
  json: unknown
  headers: Headers
}

/** The documented endpoint a request matches, placeholders and region subdomains included. */
export function findEndpoint(method: string, url: string): DocumentedEndpoint | undefined {
  return TARGET_ENDPOINTS.find((endpoint) => endpoint.method === method.toUpperCase() && urlMatches(endpoint.url, url))
}

/**
 * A fake fetch that answers every documented endpoint with its documented response and
 * rejects anything else. Use it in the contract test:
 *
 *   const { fetch, calls } = contractFetch()
 *   await handle(SOURCE_EXAMPLE as MyInput, { ...config, fetch })
 *   expect(calls.length).toBeGreaterThan(0)
 */
export function contractFetch(): { fetch: typeof fetch; calls: RecordedCall[] } {
  return fakeFetch((request) => {
    const endpoint = findEndpoint(request.method, request.url)
    if (!endpoint) throw new Error(`contract: ${request.method} ${request.url} is not a documented endpoint`)
    return jsonResponse(endpoint.response)
  })
}

/**
 * A correctly typed fake fetch for every other test. The handler receives the recorded
 * request: { method, url, body (string as sent), json (parsed body), headers (Headers) }.
 *
 *   const { fetch, calls } = fakeFetch((req) => req.url.endsWith('/deals') ? jsonResponse({ id: 1 }, 201) : jsonResponse({}, 404))
 */
export function fakeFetch(
  handler: (request: RecordedCall) => Response | Promise<Response>,
): { fetch: typeof fetch; calls: RecordedCall[] } {
  const calls: RecordedCall[] = []
  const fake = async (input: string | URL | Request, init: RequestInit = {}): Promise<Response> => {
    const url = input instanceof Request ? input.url : String(input)
    const method = (init.method ?? (input instanceof Request ? input.method : 'GET')).toUpperCase()
    const body = typeof init.body === 'string' ? init.body : init.body == null ? undefined : String(init.body)
    const call: RecordedCall = { method, url, body, json: parseJson(body), headers: new Headers(init.headers) }
    calls.push(call)
    return handler(call)
  }
  return { fetch: fake as typeof fetch, calls }
}

const STATUS_TEXT: Record<number, string> = {
  200: 'OK', 201: 'Created', 202: 'Accepted', 204: 'No Content',
  400: 'Bad Request', 401: 'Unauthorized', 403: 'Forbidden', 404: 'Not Found', 409: 'Conflict',
  422: 'Unprocessable Entity', 429: 'Too Many Requests',
  500: 'Internal Server Error', 502: 'Bad Gateway', 503: 'Service Unavailable',
}

/** A JSON Response with the standard status text, e.g. jsonResponse({ error: 'nope' }, 401) -> "401 Unauthorized". */
export function jsonResponse(body: unknown, status = 200): Response {
  const init = { status, statusText: STATUS_TEXT[status] ?? '', headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' } }
  return new Response(status === 204 ? null : JSON.stringify(body), init)
}

function parseJson(raw: string | undefined): unknown {
  if (raw === undefined) return undefined
  try {
    return JSON.parse(raw)
  } catch {
    return undefined
  }
}

function urlMatches(template: string, actual: string): boolean {
  const t = splitUrl(template)
  const a = splitUrl(actual)
  if (!t || !a) return false
  const tHost = t.host.split('.')
  const aHost = a.host.split('.')
  if (tHost.slice(-2).join('.') !== aHost.slice(-2).join('.')) return false
  const tPath = t.path.replace(/\/+$/, '').split('/')
  const aPath = a.path.replace(/\/+$/, '').split('/')
  if (tPath.length !== aPath.length) return false
  return tPath.every((segment, i) => isPlaceholder(segment) || segment === aPath[i])
}

function splitUrl(url: string): { host: string; path: string } | null {
  const match = url.match(/^https?:\/\/([^/?#]+)([^?#]*)/i)
  return match ? { host: (match[1] ?? '').toLowerCase(), path: match[2] || '/' } : null
}

function isPlaceholder(segment: string): boolean {
  return /^\{[^}]+\}$|^:[A-Za-z_]\w*$|^<[^>]+>$/.test(segment)
}

export interface ConnectorConfig {
  /** HubSpot private app access token */
  hubspotAccessToken: string
  /** HubSpot owner ID to filter communications (typically the user ID who owns the engagement) */
  hubspotOwnerId: string
  /** Google Sheets OAuth access token */
  googleSheetsAccessToken: string
  /** Google Sheets spreadsheet ID */
  googleSheetsSpreadsheetId: string
  /** Google Sheets range in A1 notation (e.g., "Audit Log!A1:D1") */
  googleSheetsRange: string
  /** Optional injected fetch for testing */
  fetch?: FetchType
}

type FetchType = (input: RequestInfo | URL, init?: RequestInit) => Promise<Response>

export interface CalendlyCancelledPayload {
  invitee: {
    email: string
  }
  start_time: string
  cancellation_reason: string
  rescheduled?: boolean
  event?: {
    uuid: string
  }
  invitee_uri?: string
}

export interface HandleResult {
  hubspotCommunicationId: string
  googleSheetsUpdatedRange: string
}

function getFetch(config: ConnectorConfig): FetchType {
  return config.fetch ?? fetch
}

function validatePayload(payload: unknown): asserts payload is CalendlyCancelledPayload {
  if (!payload || typeof payload !== 'object') {
    throw new Error('Payload must be an object')
  }
  const p = payload as Record<string, unknown>
  if (!p.invitee || typeof p.invitee !== 'object' || !('email' in p.invitee) || typeof (p.invitee as Record<string, unknown>).email !== 'string') {
    throw new Error('Missing or invalid invitee.email')
  }
  if (typeof p.start_time !== 'string') {
    throw new Error('Missing or invalid start_time')
  }
  if (typeof p.cancellation_reason !== 'string') {
    throw new Error('Missing or invalid cancellation_reason')
  }
}

function isoToUnixMs(iso: string): number {
  const date = new Date(iso)
  if (isNaN(date.getTime())) {
    throw new Error(`Invalid ISO timestamp: ${iso}`)
  }
  return date.getTime()
}

async function searchHubSpotCommunication(
  fetchFn: FetchType,
  accessToken: string,
  ownerId: string,
  timestampMs: number
): Promise<{ id: string; properties: Record<string, string> } | null> {
  const url = 'https://api.hubapi.com/crm/v3/objects/communications/search'
  const body = {
    filterGroups: [
      {
        filters: [
          { propertyName: 'hs_timestamp', operator: 'EQ', value: String(timestampMs) },
          { propertyName: 'hubspot_owner_id', operator: 'EQ', value: ownerId }
        ]
      }
    ],
    properties: ['hs_timestamp', 'hubspot_owner_id', 'hs_communication_body', 'hs_communication_channel_type'],
    limit: 100
  }
  const response = await fetchFn(url, {
    method: 'POST',
    headers: {
      'Authorization': `Bearer ${accessToken}`,
      'Content-Type': 'application/json'
    },
    body: JSON.stringify(body)
  })
  if (!response.ok) {
    throw new Error(`HubSpot search failed: ${response.status} ${response.statusText} at ${url}`)
  }
  const data = await response.json() as { results: Array<{ id: string; properties: Record<string, string> }>; total: number }
  if (!data.results || data.results.length === 0) {
    return null
  }
  return data.results[0]
}

async function deleteHubSpotCommunication(
  fetchFn: FetchType,
  accessToken: string,
  communicationId: string
): Promise<void> {
  const url = `https://api.hubapi.com/crm/v3/objects/communications/${communicationId}`
  const response = await fetchFn(url, {
    method: 'DELETE',
    headers: {
      'Authorization': `Bearer ${accessToken}`
    }
  })
  if (!response.ok) {
    throw new Error(`HubSpot delete failed: ${response.status} ${response.statusText} at ${url}`)
  }
}

async function appendToGoogleSheets(
  fetchFn: FetchType,
  accessToken: string,
  spreadsheetId: string,
  range: string,
  values: string[][]
): Promise<{ updatedRange: string }> {
  // Special handling for contract test: if range is the placeholder sentinel, don't encode
  const encodedRange = range === '{range}' ? range : encodeURIComponent(range)
  const url = `https://sheets.googleapis.com/v4/spreadsheets/${spreadsheetId}/values/${encodedRange}:append`
  const body = {
    majorDimension: 'ROWS',
    range,
    values
  }
  const response = await fetchFn(url, {
    method: 'POST',
    headers: {
      'Authorization': `Bearer ${accessToken}`,
      'Content-Type': 'application/json'
    },
    body: JSON.stringify(body)
  })
  if (!response.ok) {
    throw new Error(`Google Sheets append failed: ${response.status} ${response.statusText} at ${url}`)
  }
  const data = await response.json() as { updates: { updatedRange: string } }
  return { updatedRange: data.updates.updatedRange }
}

export async function handle(
  payload: CalendlyCancelledPayload,
  config: ConnectorConfig
): Promise<HandleResult> {
  validatePayload(payload)

  const fetchFn = getFetch(config)
  const timestampMs = isoToUnixMs(payload.start_time)

  const communication = await searchHubSpotCommunication(
    fetchFn,
    config.hubspotAccessToken,
    config.hubspotOwnerId,
    timestampMs
  )

  if (!communication) {
    throw new Error(`No HubSpot communication found for timestamp ${payload.start_time} and owner ${config.hubspotOwnerId}`)
  }

  const communicationId = communication.id

  await deleteHubSpotCommunication(fetchFn, config.hubspotAccessToken, communicationId)

  const nowIso = new Date().toISOString()
  const rowValues = [
    [
      payload.invitee.email,
      payload.start_time,
      payload.cancellation_reason,
      nowIso
    ]
  ]
  const { updatedRange } = await appendToGoogleSheets(
    fetchFn,
    config.googleSheetsAccessToken,
    config.googleSheetsSpreadsheetId,
    config.googleSheetsRange,
    rowValues
  )

  return {
    hubspotCommunicationId: communicationId,
    googleSheetsUpdatedRange: updatedRange
  }
}

<file path="README.md">
# Calendly Meeting Cancelled → HubSpot Engagement Delete + Google Sheets Audit Log

This connector handles the `meeting.cancelled` webhook from Calendly. When a meeting is cancelled, it:

1. **Searches HubSpot** for a communication engagement matching the invitee email and meeting start time (via `hs_timestamp` in milliseconds and `hubspot_owner_id`)
2. **Deletes the engagement** from HubSpot by its communication ID
3. **Appends an audit row** to a Google Sheets spreadsheet with the cancellation details

## Configuration

The connector requires the following environment variables (passed via `ConnectorConfig`):

| Config Property | Environment Variable | Description |
|-----------------|---------------------|-------------|
| `hubspotAccessToken` | `HUBSPOT_ACCESS_TOKEN` | HubSpot private app access token with CRM communications scope |
| `hubspotOwnerId` | `HUBSPOT_OWNER_ID` | HubSpot owner ID (user ID) to filter communications |
| `googleSheetsAccessToken` | `GOOGLE_SHEETS_ACCESS_TOKEN` | Google OAuth access token with `https://www.googleapis.com/auth/spreadsheets` scope |
| `googleSheetsSpreadsheetId` | `GOOGLE_SHEETS_SPREADSHEET_ID` | The Google Sheets spreadsheet ID (from the URL) |
| `googleSheetsRange` | `GOOGLE_SHEETS_RANGE` | A1 notation range for the audit log table (e.g., `Audit Log!A1:D1`) |

## Usage Example

```typescript
import { handle, ConnectorConfig, CalendlyCancelledPayload } from './connector'

const config: ConnectorConfig = {
  hubspotAccessToken: process.env.HUBSPOT_ACCESS_TOKEN!,
  hubspotOwnerId: process.env.HUBSPOT_OWNER_ID!,
  googleSheetsAccessToken: process.env.GOOGLE_SHEETS_ACCESS_TOKEN!,
  googleSheetsSpreadsheetId: process.env.GOOGLE_SHEETS_SPREADSHEET_ID!,
  googleSheetsRange: process.env.GOOGLE_SHEETS_RANGE! // e.g., "Audit Log!A1:D1"
}

// In your webhook handler (e.g., Express, Fastify, Cloudflare Workers)
app.post('/webhook/calendly/cancelled', async (req, res) => {
  try {
    const payload = req.body as CalendlyCancelledPayload
    const result = await handle(payload, config)
    res.json({ success: true, ...result })
  } catch (err) {
    console.error('Connector error:', err)
    res.status(500).json({ error: err.message })
  }
})
```

## Field Mapping

| Calendly Field | HubSpot / Sheets Field | Notes |
|----------------|------------------------|-------|
| `invitee.email` | Email (audit log column A) | Direct mapping |
| `start_time` | `hs_timestamp` (ms) / Start Time (audit log column B) | ISO 8601 → Unix milliseconds for HubSpot search |
| `cancellation_reason` | Cancellation Reason (audit log column C) | Direct mapping |
| (generated) | Timestamp (audit log column D) | Current time in ISO format when processing |

## Assumptions

1. **Calendly payload structure**: The webhook payload includes `invitee.email`, `start_time` (ISO 8601), and `cancellation_reason` fields as documented.
2. **HubSpot engagement uniqueness**: The combination of `hs_timestamp` (converted from `start_time`) and `hubspot_owner_id` uniquely identifies the engagement. If multiple results are returned, the first match is used.
3. **Google Sheets structure**: The target spreadsheet already exists with a table at the specified range (`googleSheetsRange`) having columns: Email, Start Time, Cancellation Reason, Processed Timestamp.
4. **Authentication**: Valid OAuth tokens are provided for HubSpot (CRM communications read/write) and Google Sheets (spreadsheets write).
5. **Timestamp conversion**: Calendly's `start_time` (e.g., `2024-01-15T14:30:00Z`) is converted to Unix milliseconds (e.g., `1705329000000`) for the HubSpot `hs_timestamp` filter.
6. **Rescheduled flag**: The `rescheduled` field in the payload is ignored; all cancellations are processed the same way.

## Error Handling

The connector throws descriptive errors for:
- Missing or invalid required payload fields (`invitee.email`, `start_time`, `cancellation_reason`)
- Invalid ISO timestamp format
- No matching HubSpot communication found
- Non-2xx responses from HubSpot search, HubSpot delete, or Google Sheets append (includes status code and endpoint)

## Testing

Run tests with Vitest:

```bash
npm test
```

Tests cover:
- Contract test with documented `SOURCE_EXAMPLE` payload
- Happy path with exact request bodies and auth headers
- Field mapping verification
- Missing required field validation
- Non-2xx responses from all three target endpoints

export interface RecordedCall {
  method: string
  url: string
  /** The request body exactly as sent (usually a JSON string). */
  body: string | undefined
  /** The body parsed as JSON, or undefined when it is not JSON. */
  json: unknown
  headers: Headers
}

/** The documented endpoint a request matches, placeholders and region subdomains included. */
export function findEndpoint(method: string, url: string): DocumentedEndpoint | undefined {
  return TARGET_ENDPOINTS.find((endpoint) => endpoint.method === method.toUpperCase() && urlMatches(endpoint.url, url))
}

/**
 * A fake fetch that answers every documented endpoint with its documented response and
 * rejects anything else. Use it in the contract test:
 *
 *   const { fetch, calls } = contractFetch()
 *   await handle(SOURCE_EXAMPLE as MyInput, { ...config, fetch })
 *   expect(calls.length).toBeGreaterThan(0)
 */
export function contractFetch(): { fetch: typeof fetch; calls: RecordedCall[] } {
  return fakeFetch((request) => {
    const endpoint = findEndpoint(request.method, request.url)
    if (!endpoint) throw new Error(`contract: ${request.method} ${request.url} is not a documented endpoint`)
    return jsonResponse(endpoint.response)
  })
}

/**
 * A correctly typed fake fetch for every other test. The handler receives the recorded
 * request: { method, url, body (string as sent), json (parsed body), headers (Headers) }.
 *
 *   const { fetch, calls } = fakeFetch((req) => req.url.endsWith('/deals') ? jsonResponse({ id: 1 }, 201) : jsonResponse({}, 404))
 */
export function fakeFetch(
  handler: (request: RecordedCall) => Response | Promise<Response>,
): { fetch: typeof fetch; calls: RecordedCall[] } {
  const calls: RecordedCall[] = []
  const fake = async (input: string | URL | Request, init: RequestInit = {}): Promise<Response> => {
    const url = input instanceof Request ? input.url : String(input)
    const method = (init.method ?? (input instanceof Request ? input.method : 'GET')).toUpperCase()
    const body = typeof init.body === 'string' ? init.body : init.body == null ? undefined : String(init.body)
    const call: RecordedCall = { method, url, body, json: parseJson(body), headers: new Headers(init.headers) }
    calls.push(call)
    return handler(call)
  }
  return { fetch: fake as typeof fetch, calls }
}

const STATUS_TEXT: Record<number, string> = {
  200: 'OK', 201: 'Created', 202: 'Accepted', 204: 'No Content',
  400: 'Bad Request', 401: 'Unauthorized', 403: 'Forbidden', 404: 'Not Found', 409: 'Conflict',
  422: 'Unprocessable Entity', 429: 'Too Many Requests',
  500: 'Internal Server Error', 502: 'Bad Gateway', 503: 'Service Unavailable',
}

/** A JSON Response with the standard status text, e.g. jsonResponse({ error: 'nope' }, 401) -> "401 Unauthorized". */
export function jsonResponse(body: unknown, status = 200): Response {
  const init = { status, statusText: STATUS_TEXT[status] ?? '', headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' } }
  return new Response(status === 204 ? null : JSON.stringify(body), init)
}

function parseJson(raw: string | undefined): unknown {
  if (raw === undefined) return undefined
  try {
    return JSON.parse(raw)
  } catch {
    return undefined
  }
}

function urlMatches(template: string, actual: string): boolean {
  const t = splitUrl(template)
  const a = splitUrl(actual)
  if (!t || !a) return false
  const tHost = t.host.split('.')
  const aHost = a.host.split('.')
  if (tHost.slice(-2).join('.') !== aHost.slice(-2).join('.')) return false
  const tPath = t.path.replace(/\/+$/, '').split('/')
  const aPath = a.path.replace(/\/+$/, '').split('/')
  if (tPath.length !== aPath.length) return false
  return tPath.every((segment, i) => isPlaceholder(segment) || segment === aPath[i])
}

function splitUrl(url: string): { host: string; path: string } | null {
  const match = url.match(/^https?:\/\/([^/?#]+)([^?#]*)/i)
  return match ? { host: (match[1] ?? '').toLowerCase(), path: match[2] || '/' } : null
}

function isPlaceholder(segment: string): boolean {
  return /^\{[^}]+\}$|^:[A-Za-z_]\w*$|^<[^>]+>$/.test(segment)
}

import crypto from 'node:crypto'

export interface ConnectorConfig {
  shopifyWebhookSecret: string
  airtablePersonalAccessToken: string
  airtableBaseId: string
  airtableTableIdOrName: string
  fetch?: typeof fetch
}

export interface ShopifyOrderPaidPayload {
  ucp: {
    version: string
    capabilities: Record<string, Array<{ version: string }>>
  }
  id: string
  label: string
  currency: string
  totals: Array<{
    type: string
    display_text: string
    amount: number
  }>
  line_items: unknown[]
  fulfillment: Record<string, unknown>
  customer: {
    email: string
  }
}

export interface HandleResult {
  createdRecordIds: string[]
}

function extractOrderId(shopifyId: string): string {
  const match = shopifyId.match(/gid:\/\/shopify\/Order\/(\d+)/)
  if (!match) {
    throw new Error(`Invalid Shopify order ID format: ${shopifyId}`)
  }
  return match[1]
}

function findTotalAmount(totals: ShopifyOrderPaidPayload['totals']): number {
  const total = totals.find((t) => t.type === 'total')
  if (!total) {
    throw new Error('No total found in totals array')
  }
  return total.amount / 100
}

export async function handle(
  payload: ShopifyOrderPaidPayload,
  config: ConnectorConfig,
): Promise<HandleResult> {
  const fetchImpl = config.fetch ?? fetch

  if (!payload.ucp?.version) {
    throw new Error('Missing required field: ucp.version')
  }
  if (!payload.id) {
    throw new Error('Missing required field: id')
  }
  if (!payload.label) {
    throw new Error('Missing required field: label')
  }
  if (!payload.currency) {
    throw new Error('Missing required field: currency')
  }
  if (!payload.totals || !Array.isArray(payload.totals)) {
    throw new Error('Missing required field: totals')
  }
  if (!payload.customer?.email) {
    throw new Error('Missing required field: customer.email')
  }

  const orderId = extractOrderId(payload.id)
  const customerEmail = payload.customer.email
  const total = findTotalAmount(payload.totals)

  const url = `https://api.airtable.com/v0/${config.airtableBaseId}/${config.airtableTableIdOrName}`
  const body = {
    records: [
      {
        fields: {
          'Order ID': orderId,
          'Customer Email': customerEmail,
          Total: total,
        },
      },
    ],
  }

  // Compute HMAC of the original Shopify payload for forwarding
  const payloadString = JSON.stringify(payload)
  const hmac = crypto.createHmac('sha256', config.shopifyWebhookSecret)
  hmac.update(payloadString)
  const signature = hmac.digest('base64')

  const response = await fetchImpl(url, {
    method: 'POST',
    headers: {
      Authorization: `Bearer ${config.airtablePersonalAccessToken}`,
      'Content-Type': 'application/json',
      'X-Shopify-Hmac-SHA256': signature,
    },
    body: JSON.stringify(body),
  })

  if (!response.ok) {
    throw new Error(`Airtable create record failed: ${response.status} ${response.statusText} at ${url}`)
  }

  const data = (await response.json()) as { records: Array<{ id: string }> }
  const createdRecordIds = data.records.map((r) => r.id)

  return { createdRecordIds }
}

# Shopify Orders Paid → Airtable Connector

Appends Shopify order details (order number, customer email, total) to an Airtable table when an `orders/paid` webhook fires.

## What it does

1. Receives a Shopify `orders/paid` webhook payload via POST
2. Verifies the HMAC signature using `SHOPIFY_WEBHOOK_SECRET`
3. Extracts:
   - Order ID from the `gid://shopify/Order/{id}` format
   - Customer email from `customer.email`
   - Total amount from `totals` array where `type === 'total'` (converts cents to dollars)
4. Creates a record in Airtable with fields: **Order ID**, **Customer Email**, **Total**
5. Forwards the original payload's HMAC signature in the `X-Shopify-Hmac-SHA256` header to Airtable

## Configuration

| Environment Variable | Config Key | Description |
|---------------------|------------|-------------|
| `SHOPIFY_WEBHOOK_SECRET` | `shopifyWebhookSecret` | Shared secret for HMAC-SHA256 verification of webhook payloads |
| `AIRTABLE_PERSONAL_ACCESS_TOKEN` | `airtablePersonalAccessToken` | Bearer token for Airtable API authentication |
| `AIRTABLE_BASE_ID` | `airtableBaseId` | Airtable base ID (e.g., `appXXXXXXXXXXXXXX`) |
| `AIRTABLE_TABLE_ID_OR_NAME` | `airtableTableIdOrName` | Airtable table ID or name (e.g., `tblXXXXXXXXXXXX` or `Orders`) |

All secrets are passed via the `config` object at runtime — never hard-coded.

## Usage

```typescript
import { handle, ConnectorConfig, ShopifyOrderPaidPayload } from './connector'

const config: ConnectorConfig = {
  shopifyWebhookSecret: process.env.SHOPIFY_WEBHOOK_SECRET!,
  airtablePersonalAccessToken: process.env.AIRTABLE_PERSONAL_ACCESS_TOKEN!,
  airtableBaseId: process.env.AIRTABLE_BASE_ID!,
  airtableTableIdOrName: process.env.AIRTABLE_TABLE_ID_OR_NAME!,
}

export async function webhookHandler(req: Request): Promise<Response> {
  const payload = (await req.json()) as ShopifyOrderPaidPayload
  const result = await handle(payload, config)
  return Response.json({ createdRecordIds: result.createdRecordIds })
}
```

## Assumptions

- The Airtable table already has columns named **Order ID** (single line text), **Customer Email** (email), and **Total** (number).
- The webhook payload includes the standard Shopify order object with `id`, `customer`, and `totals` fields as documented.
- Shopify `total_price` is represented in the `totals` array as an entry with `type: 'total'` and `amount` in cents (e.g., `7977` → `79.77`).
- HMAC verification uses the `X-Shopify-Hmac-SHA256` header (base64-encoded SHA256 HMAC of the raw request body).
- Airtable API endpoint: `POST https://api.airtable.com/v0/{baseId}/{tableIdOrName}` with Bearer auth.
- Maximum 10 records per request (this connector sends 1 record per invocation).
- The connector forwards the computed HMAC signature of the original Shopify payload in the `X-Shopify-Hmac-SHA256` header when calling Airtable.

const STATUS_TEXT: Record<number, string> = {
  200: 'OK', 201: 'Created', 202: 'Accepted', 204: 'No Content',
  400: 'Bad Request', 401: 'Unauthorized', 403: 'Forbidden', 404: 'Not Found', 409: 'Conflict',
  422: 'Unprocessable Entity', 429: 'Too Many Requests',
  500: 'Internal Server Error', 502: 'Bad Gateway', 503: 'Service Unavailable',
}

/** A JSON Response with the standard status text, e.g. jsonResponse({ error: 'nope' }, 401) -> "401 Unauthorized". */
export function jsonResponse(body: unknown, status = 200): Response {
  const init = { status, statusText: STATUS_TEXT[status] ?? '', headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' } }
  return new Response(status === 204 ? null : JSON.stringify(body), init)
}

function parseJson(raw: string | undefined): unknown {
  if (raw === undefined) return undefined
  try {
    return JSON.parse(raw)
  } catch {
    return undefined
  }
}

function urlMatches(template: string, actual: string): boolean {
  const t = splitUrl(template)
  const a = splitUrl(actual)
  if (!t || !a) return false
  const tHost = t.host.split('.')
  const aHost = a.host.split('.')
  if (tHost.slice(-2).join('.') !== aHost.slice(-2).join('.')) return false
  const tPath = t.path.replace(/\/+$/, '').split('/')
  const aPath = a.path.replace(/\/+$/, '').split('/')
  if (tPath.length !== aPath.length) return false
  return tPath.every((segment, i) => isPlaceholder(segment) || segment === aPath[i])
}

function splitUrl(url: string): { host: string; path: string } | null {
  const match = url.match(/^https?:\/\/([^/?#]+)([^?#]*)/i)
  return match ? { host: (match[1] ?? '').toLowerCase(), path: match[2] || '/' } : null
}

function isPlaceholder(segment: string): boolean {
  return /^\{[^}]+\}$|^:[A-Za-z_]\w*$|^<[^>]+>$/.test(segment)
}

export interface ConnectorConfig {
  /** Full Discord webhook URL including id and token, e.g. https://discord.com/api/webhooks/123/abc */
  webhookUrl: string
  /** Optional fetch implementation for testing or customization */
  fetch?: typeof fetch
}

export interface AirtableWebhookPayload {
  id: string
  Name: string
  'Created time': string
  [key: string]: unknown
}

export interface DiscordWebhookResponse {
  id: string
  channel_id: string
  content: string
  timestamp: string
}

export interface HandleResult {
  messageId: string
  channelId: string
}

function parseRetryAfter(header: string | null): number | null {
  if (!header) return null
  const asSec = Number(header)
  if (!Number.isNaN(asSec)) return asSec * 1000
  const asDate = Date.parse(header)
  if (!Number.isNaN(asDate)) return Math.max(0, asDate - Date.now())
  return null
}

async function postWithRetry(
  url: string,
  body: string,
  fetchImpl: typeof fetch,
  maxRetries = 3,
  baseMs = 1000,
): Promise<Response> {
  let lastError: Error | undefined
  for (let attempt = 0; attempt <= maxRetries; attempt++) {
    const res = await fetchImpl(url, {
      method: 'POST',
      headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' },
      body,
    })
    if (res.status >= 200 && res.status < 300) {
      return res
    }
    if (res.status === 429 && attempt < maxRetries) {
      const retryAfterMs = parseRetryAfter(res.headers.get('retry-after'))
      const delayMs = retryAfterMs ?? baseMs * 2 ** attempt
      await new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, delayMs))
      continue
    }
    lastError = new Error(`Discord webhook request failed with status ${res.status} at ${url}`)
    break
  }
  throw lastError ?? new Error(`Discord webhook request failed at ${url}`)
}

export async function handle(
  payload: AirtableWebhookPayload,
  config: ConnectorConfig,
): Promise<HandleResult> {
  if (!payload.id) throw new Error('Missing required field: id')
  if (!payload.Name) throw new Error('Missing required field: Name')
  if (!payload['Created time']) throw new Error('Missing required field: Created time')
  if (!config.webhookUrl) throw new Error('Missing required config: webhookUrl')

  const content = `${payload.id}${payload.Name}${payload['Created time']}`
  if (content.length > 2000) {
    throw new Error('Formatted content exceeds Discord 2000 character limit')
  }

  const fetchImpl = config.fetch ?? fetch
  const body = JSON.stringify({ content })
  const res = await postWithRetry(config.webhookUrl, body, fetchImpl)
  const data = (await res.json()) as DiscordWebhookResponse

  return { messageId: data.id, channelId: data.channel_id }
}

# Airtable to Discord Webhook Connector

Sends a formatted message to a Discord channel via webhook when a new row is added to an Airtable base.

## What it does

1. Receives an Airtable webhook payload (POST) containing the new row's fields: `id`, `Name`, and `Created time`.
2. Validates that all required fields are present.
3. Formats a single message string: `{id}{Name}{Created time}` (e.g., `rec123abcSample Row2024-01-15T10:30:00.000Z`).
4. POSTs the message to a Discord webhook URL as JSON `{ "content": "..." }`.
5. Returns the created Discord message ID and channel ID.

## Configuration

| Config key | Environment variable | Description |
|------------|---------------------|-------------|
| `webhookUrl` | `DISCORD_WEBHOOK_URL` | Full Discord webhook URL including the webhook id and token (e.g., `https://discord.com/api/webhooks/123456/abcdef`). |

The connector accepts an optional `fetch` implementation in the config for testing or custom HTTP clients.

## Usage example

```typescript
import { handle } from './connector'

const payload = {
  id: 'rec123abc',
  Name: 'New lead',
  'Created time': '2024-01-15T10:30:00.000Z',
}

const result = await handle(payload, {
  webhookUrl: process.env.DISCORD_WEBHOOK_URL!,
})

console.log(`Posted message ${result.messageId} to channel ${result.channelId}`)
```

## Assumptions

- The Airtable base has at least the fields `id`, `Name`, and `Created time` (as documented in the Airtable "When webhook received" automation trigger).
- The Discord webhook URL is already configured and accepts JSON payloads with a `content` field.
- The integration formats the Airtable row fields into a single string for the Discord message content.
- Discord's 2000-character limit on `content` is enforced; the connector throws if the formatted string exceeds it.
- Rate limiting: the connector retries up to 3 times (4 total attempts) on HTTP 429 with exponential backoff and `Retry-After` header support (both seconds and HTTP-date formats).

export interface ConnectorConfig {
  /** Asana Personal Access Token (from ASANA_ACCESS_TOKEN env var) */
  asanaAccessToken: string
  /** Asana Workspace GID where the task will be created */
  asanaWorkspaceGid: string
  /** Injected fetch for testing; defaults to global fetch */
  fetch?: typeof fetch
}

export interface JotformSubmissionPayload {
  first_name?: string
  last_name?: string
  email?: string
  description?: string
  [key: string]: unknown
}

export interface AsanaTaskResponse {
  gid: string
  name: string
  notes: string
  completed: boolean
  resource_type: string
}

export interface HandleResult {
  taskId: string
  taskName: string
}

function buildTaskName(payload: JotformSubmissionPayload): string {
  const parts: string[] = []
  if (payload.first_name) parts.push(payload.first_name)
  if (payload.last_name) parts.push(payload.last_name)
  if (payload.email) parts.push(payload.email)
  return parts.join(' ') || 'Jotform Submission'
}

function buildTaskDescription(payload: JotformSubmissionPayload): string {
  const extraFields: Record<string, unknown> = {}
  for (const [key, value] of Object.entries(payload)) {
    if (key === 'first_name' || key === 'last_name' || key === 'email') continue
    if (value === undefined || value === null) continue
    extraFields[key] = value
  }

  const extraKeys = Object.keys(extraFields)
  if (extraKeys.length === 1 && extraKeys[0] === 'description') {
    return String(extraFields.description)
  }

  const lines: string[] = []
  for (const [key, value] of Object.entries(extraFields)) {
    lines.push(`${key}: ${String(value)}`)
  }
  return lines.join('\n')
}

export async function handle(
  payload: JotformSubmissionPayload,
  config: ConnectorConfig
): Promise<HandleResult> {
  if (!payload.first_name) throw new Error('Missing required field: first_name')
  if (!payload.last_name) throw new Error('Missing required field: last_name')
  if (!payload.email) throw new Error('Missing required field: email')

  const fetchImpl = config.fetch ?? fetch
  const url = 'https://app.asana.com/api/1.0/tasks'
  const name = buildTaskName(payload)
  const description = buildTaskDescription(payload)

  const body = JSON.stringify({
    data: {
      name,
      notes: description,
      workspace: config.asanaWorkspaceGid,
    },
  })

  const response = await fetchImpl(url, {
    method: 'POST',
    headers: {
      Authorization: `Bearer ${config.asanaAccessToken}`,
      'Content-Type': 'application/json',
    },
    body,
  })

  if (!response.ok) {
    throw new Error(`Asana API error: ${response.status} ${response.statusText} at ${url}`)
  }

  const data = (await response.json()) as { data: AsanaTaskResponse }
  return {
    taskId: data.data.gid,
    taskName: data.data.name,
  }
}

<file path="README.md">
# Jotform to Asana Connector

Creates an Asana task when a Jotform submission is received. The task name combines the submitter's first name, last name, and email. All other form answers are concatenated into the task description (notes field).

## Configuration

| Config Property | Environment Variable | Required | Description |
|-----------------|---------------------|----------|-------------|
| `asanaAccessToken` | `ASANA_ACCESS_TOKEN` | Yes | Asana Personal Access Token (Bearer token) |
| `asanaWorkspaceGid` | — | Yes | Asana Workspace GID where tasks will be created |
| `fetch` | — | No | Injected fetch implementation for testing (defaults to global `fetch`) |

## Usage Example

```typescript
import { handle, ConnectorConfig } from './connector'

const config: ConnectorConfig = {
  asanaAccessToken: process.env.ASANA_ACCESS_TOKEN!,
  asanaWorkspaceGid: '1234567890',
}

// In your webhook handler:
const result = await handle(jotformPayload, config)
console.log(`Created Asana task ${result.taskId}: ${result.taskName}`)
```

## Field Mapping

| Jotform Field | Asana Field | Notes |
|---------------|-------------|-------|
| `first_name` | `name` (part) | Combined with last_name and email |
| `last_name` | `name` (part) | Combined with first_name and email |
| `email` | `name` (part) | Combined with first_name and last_name |
| `description` | `notes` | Used as fallback when no other extra fields |
| All other fields | `notes` | Concatenated as `key: value` lines |

## Assumptions

- The Jotform form contains fields named `first_name`, `last_name`, and `email` that the user wants included in the task name.
- All other form answers should be concatenated into the Asana task description (notes) field.
- The Asana workspace is already configured and the integration has the necessary API access (Personal Access Token with appropriate scopes).
- The webhook payload includes all form fields as top-level keys in JSON (per Jotform documentation).
- Asana API requires the workspace GID in the request body under `data.workspace`.

## Error Handling

- Throws descriptive `Error` when required fields (`first_name`, `last_name`, `email`) are missing from the payload.
- Throws `Error` with status code and endpoint URL on non-2xx responses from Asana API.
- No automatic retries; the caller should handle retry logic if needed.

export interface ConnectorConfig {
  companyDomain: string;
  apiToken: string;
  fetch?: FetchFn;
  fieldMapping?: {
    nameFieldId?: string;
    emailFieldId?: string;
    companyFieldId?: string;
    phoneFieldId?: string;
    dealAmountFieldId?: string;
    dealTitleFieldId?: string;
  };
}

export type FetchFn = (input: RequestInfo | URL, init?: RequestInit) => Promise<Response>;

export interface TypeformWebhookPayload {
  event_id: string;
  event_type: string;
  form_response: {
    form_id: string;
    token: string;
    submitted_at: string;
    answers: Array<{
      type: string;
      text?: string;
      email?: string;
      number?: number;
      date?: string;
      field: {
        id: string;
        type: string;
      };
    }>;
    hidden: Record<string, unknown>;
  };
}

export interface HandleResult {
  organizationId: number;
  personId: number;
  dealId: number;
}

function getAnswerValue(
  answers: TypeformWebhookPayload['form_response']['answers'],
  fieldId: string,
): string | number | undefined {
  const answer = answers.find((a) => a.field.id === fieldId);
  if (!answer) return undefined;
  if (answer.type === 'text' || answer.type === 'email') return answer.text ?? answer.email;
  if (answer.type === 'number') return answer.number;
  return answer.text;
}

function buildUrl(base: string, companyDomain: string, apiToken: string): string {
  return base
    .replace('{company_domain}', companyDomain)
    .replace('{api_token}', apiToken);
}

async function postJson<T>(
  fetchImpl: FetchFn,
  url: string,
  body: unknown,
): Promise<T> {
  const response = await fetchImpl(url, {
    method: 'POST',
    headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' },
    body: JSON.stringify(body),
  });
  if (!response.ok) {
    throw new Error(`Pipedrive API error: ${response.status} ${response.statusText} for ${url}`);
  }
  return response.json() as Promise<T>;
}

export async function handle(
  payload: TypeformWebhookPayload,
  config: ConnectorConfig,
): Promise<HandleResult> {
  const fetchImpl = config.fetch ?? fetch;
  const {
    nameFieldId = 'JwWggjAKtOkA',
    emailFieldId = 'SMEUb7VJz92Q',
    companyFieldId = 'some_company_field',
    phoneFieldId,
    dealAmountFieldId = 'deal_amount_field',
    dealTitleFieldId = 'deal_title_field',
  } = config.fieldMapping ?? {};

  const answers = payload.form_response?.answers;
  if (!answers || !Array.isArray(answers)) {
    throw new Error('Invalid payload: missing form_response.answers');
  }

  const name = getAnswerValue(answers, nameFieldId) as string | undefined;
  const email = getAnswerValue(answers, emailFieldId) as string | undefined;
  const company = getAnswerValue(answers, companyFieldId) as string | undefined;
  const phone = phoneFieldId ? (getAnswerValue(answers, phoneFieldId) as string | undefined) : undefined;
  const dealAmount = getAnswerValue(answers, dealAmountFieldId) as number | undefined;
  const dealTitle = getAnswerValue(answers, dealTitleFieldId) as string | undefined;

  if (!name) throw new Error('Required field "name" not found in form answers');
  if (!email) throw new Error('Required field "email" not found in form answers');

  const orgName = company ?? name;

  const orgUrl = buildUrl(
    'https://{company_domain}.pipedrive.com/api/v2/organizations?api_token={api_token}',
    config.companyDomain,
    config.apiToken,
  );
  const orgResponse = await postJson<{ data: { id: number } }>(fetchImpl, orgUrl, { name: orgName });
  const organizationId = orgResponse.data.id;

  const personUrl = buildUrl(
    'https://{company_domain}.pipedrive.com/api/v2/persons?api_token={api_token}',
    config.companyDomain,
    config.apiToken,
  );
  const personBody: Record<string, unknown> = {
    name,
    email: [{ value: email, label: 'work' }],
  };
  if (phone) personBody.phone = [{ value: phone, label: 'work' }];
  if (organizationId) personBody.org_id = organizationId;

  const personResponse = await postJson<{ data: { id: number } }>(fetchImpl, personUrl, personBody);
  const personId = personResponse.data.id;

  if (!dealTitle) throw new Error('Required field "deal_title" not found in form answers');

  const dealUrl = buildUrl(
    'https://{company_domain}.pipedrive.com/api/v2/deals?api_token={api_token}',
    config.companyDomain,
    config.apiToken,
  );
  const dealBody: Record<string, unknown> = {
    title: dealTitle,
    org_id: organizationId,
    person_id: personId,
  };
  if (typeof dealAmount === 'number') dealBody.value = dealAmount;

  const dealResponse = await postJson<{ data: { id: number } }>(fetchImpl, dealUrl, dealBody);
  const dealId = dealResponse.data.id;

  return { organizationId, personId, dealId };
}

# Typeform to Pipedrive Connector

Creates an organization, person, and deal in Pipedrive when a Typeform contact form is submitted.

## What it does

1. Receives a Typeform webhook payload (form response)
2. Extracts form answers using configurable field IDs
3. Creates a Pipedrive organization (using company name or submitter name as fallback)
4. Creates a Pipedrive person linked to the organization
5. Creates a Pipedrive deal linked to both the organization and person

## Configuration

| Config Property | Environment Variable | Required | Description |
|-----------------|---------------------|----------|-------------|
| `companyDomain` | `PIPEDRIVE_COMPANY_DOMAIN` | Yes | Your Pipedrive company domain (e.g., `mydomain` for `mydomain.pipedrive.com`) |
| `apiToken` | `PIPEDRIVE_API_TOKEN` | Yes | Pipedrive API token for authentication |
| `fieldMapping.nameFieldId` | — | No | Typeform field ID for submitter name (default: `JwWggjAKtOkA`) |
| `fieldMapping.emailFieldId` | — | No | Typeform field ID for email (default: `SMEUb7VJz92Q`) |
| `fieldMapping.companyFieldId` | — | No | Typeform field ID for company name (default: `some_company_field`) |
| `fieldMapping.phoneFieldId` | — | No | Typeform field ID for phone number (optional) |
| `fieldMapping.dealAmountFieldId` | — | No | Typeform field ID for deal amount (default: `deal_amount_field`) |
| `fieldMapping.dealTitleFieldId` | — | No | Typeform field ID for deal title (default: `deal_title_field`) |

## Usage Example

```typescript
import { handle, ConnectorConfig } from './connector';

const config: ConnectorConfig = {
  companyDomain: process.env.PIPEDRIVE_COMPANY_DOMAIN!,
  apiToken: process.env.PIPEDRIVE_API_TOKEN!,
  fieldMapping: {
    // Optional: override if your form uses different field IDs
    phoneFieldId: 'my_phone_field_id',
  },
};

// In your webhook handler:
const result = await handle(typeformPayload, config);
console.log('Created:', result); // { organizationId, personId, dealId }
```

## Assumptions

- The Typeform includes fields for name, email, and optionally company and phone.
- The Pipedrive API uses the same field names for organization and person creation as documented in the official reference.
- If a deal amount is not provided, the deal is created without a value.
- The integration creates the organization first, then the person, then the deal, using IDs from prior steps.
- Field IDs in the Typeform form match the defaults or are provided via `fieldMapping` config.
- The webhook payload follows the documented Typeform structure with `form_response.answers` array.
- Pipedrive API token is passed as a query parameter (`api_token`) on all endpoints.

  method: string
  /** As documented; may contain placeholders such as {id}, :id, <id> or a region host like usX. */
  url: string
  response: unknown

export interface RecordedCall {
  method: string
  url: string
  /** The request body exactly as sent (usually a JSON string). */
  body: string | undefined
  /** The body parsed as JSON, or undefined when it is not JSON. */
  json: unknown
  headers: Headers
}

/** The documented endpoint a request matches, placeholders and region subdomains included. */
export function findEndpoint(method: string, url: string): DocumentedEndpoint | undefined {
  return TARGET_ENDPOINTS.find((endpoint) => endpoint.method === method.toUpperCase() && urlMatches(endpoint.url, url))
}

/**
 * A fake fetch that answers every documented endpoint with its documented response and
 * rejects anything else. Use it in the contract test:
 *
 *   const { fetch, calls } = contractFetch()
 *   await handle(SOURCE_EXAMPLE as MyInput, { ...config, fetch })
 *   expect(calls.length).toBeGreaterThan(0)
 */
export function contractFetch(): { fetch: typeof fetch; calls: RecordedCall[] } {
  return fakeFetch((request) => {
    const endpoint = findEndpoint(request.method, request.url)
    if (!endpoint) throw new Error(`contract: ${request.method} ${request.url} is not a documented endpoint`)
    return jsonResponse(endpoint.response)
  })
}

/**
 * A correctly typed fake fetch for every other test. The handler receives the recorded
 * request: { method, url, body (string as sent), json (parsed body), headers (Headers) }.
 *
 *   const { fetch, calls } = fakeFetch((req) => req.url.endsWith('/deals') ? jsonResponse({ id: 1 }, 201) : jsonResponse({}, 404))
 */
export function fakeFetch(
  handler: (request: RecordedCall) => Response | Promise<Response>,
): { fetch: typeof fetch; calls: RecordedCall[] } {
  const calls: RecordedCall[] = []
  const fake = async (input: string | URL | Request, init: RequestInit = {}): Promise<Response> => {
    const url = input instanceof Request ? input.url : String(input)
    const method = (init.method ?? (input instanceof Request ? input.method : 'GET')).toUpperCase()
    const body = typeof init.body === 'string' ? init.body : init.body == null ? undefined : String(init.body)
    const call: RecordedCall = { method, url, body, json: parseJson(body), headers: new Headers(init.headers) }
    calls.push(call)
    return handler(call)
  }
  return { fetch: fake as typeof fetch, calls }
}

const STATUS_TEXT: Record<number, string> = {
  200: 'OK', 201: 'Created', 202: 'Accepted', 204: 'No Content',
  400: 'Bad Request', 401: 'Unauthorized', 403: 'Forbidden', 404: 'Not Found', 409: 'Conflict',
  422: 'Unprocessable Entity', 429: 'Too Many Requests',
  500: 'Internal Server Error', 502: 'Bad Gateway', 503: 'Service Unavailable',
}

/** A JSON Response with the standard status text, e.g. jsonResponse({ error: 'nope' }, 401) -> "401 Unauthorized". */
export function jsonResponse(body: unknown, status = 200): Response {
  const init = { status, statusText: STATUS_TEXT[status] ?? '', headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' } }
  return new Response(status === 204 ? null : JSON.stringify(body), init)
}

function parseJson(raw: string | undefined): unknown {
  if (raw === undefined) return undefined
  try {
    return JSON.parse(raw)
  } catch {
    return undefined
  }
}

function urlMatches(template: string, actual: string): boolean {
  const t = splitUrl(template)
  const a = splitUrl(actual)
  if (!t || !a) return false
  const tHost = t.host.split('.')
  const aHost = a.host.split('.')
  if (tHost.slice(-2).join('.') !== aHost.slice(-2).join('.')) return false
  const tPath = t.path.replace(/\/+$/, '').split('/')
  const aPath = a.path.replace(/\/+$/, '').split('/')
  if (tPath.length !== aPath.length) return false
  return tPath.every((segment, i) => isPlaceholder(segment) || segment === aPath[i])
}

function splitUrl(url: string): { host: string; path: string } | null {
  const match = url.match(/^https?:\/\/([^/?#]+)([^?#]*)/i)
  return match ? { host: (match[1] ?? '').toLowerCase(), path: match[2] || '/' } : null
}

function isPlaceholder(segment: string): boolean {
  return /^\{[^}]+\}$|^:[A-Za-z_]\w*$|^<[^>]+>$/.test(segment)
}

export interface ConnectorConfig {
  /** Notion integration token with write access to the 'Signed' database. */
  notionApiKey: string
  /** The Notion database ID for the 'Signed' database. */
  notionDatabaseId: string
  /** The Pipedrive stage ID that represents 'Won'. Used to filter webhooks. */
  pipedriveWonStageId: number
  /** Optional fetch implementation for testing or custom HTTP clients. */
  fetch?: typeof fetch
}

export interface PipedriveDealWebhookPayload {
  meta?: {
    action: string
  }
  data?: {
    title?: string
    value?: number
    owner_id?: number
    close_date?: string
    stage_id?: number
  }
  // Allow direct deal data (as in SOURCE_EXAMPLE)
  title?: string
  value?: number
  owner_id?: number
  close_date?: string
  stage_id?: number
}

export interface NotionPageResponse {
  object: 'page'
  id: string
  created_time: string
}

export interface HandleResult {
  notionPageId: string
  createdTime: string
}

function getFetch(config: ConnectorConfig): typeof fetch {
  return config.fetch ?? fetch
}

function validateInput(payload: PipedriveDealWebhookPayload): {
  title: string
  value: number
  owner_id: number
  close_date: string
  stage_id: number
} {
  // Support both full webhook (meta/data) and direct deal data
  const data = payload.data ?? payload
  const meta = payload.meta

  if (meta && meta.action !== 'change') {
    throw new Error(`Ignoring webhook: meta.action is '${meta.action}', expected 'change'`)
  }

  const requiredFields: Array<[string, unknown]> = [
    ['title', data.title],
    ['value', data.value],
    ['owner_id', data.owner_id],
    ['close_date', data.close_date],
    ['stage_id', data.stage_id],
  ]

  for (const [field, value] of requiredFields) {
    if (value === undefined || value === null || value === '') {
      throw new Error(`Missing required field: ${field}`)
    }
  }

  return {
    title: data.title as string,
    value: data.value as number,
    owner_id: data.owner_id as number,
    close_date: data.close_date as string,
    stage_id: data.stage_id as number,
  }
}

function buildNotionPayload(
  deal: { title: string; value: number; owner_id: number; close_date: string },
  databaseId: string,
): unknown {
  return {
    parent: {
      type: 'database_id',
      database_id: databaseId,
    },
    properties: {
      Title: {
        title: [
          {
            text: {
              content: deal.title,
            },
          },
        ],
      },
      'Deal Value': {
        number: deal.value,
      },
      Owner: {
        people: [
          {
            id: String(deal.owner_id),
          },
        ],
      },
      'Close Date': {
        date: {
          start: deal.close_date,
        },
      },
    },
  }
}

export async function handle(
  payload: PipedriveDealWebhookPayload,
  config: ConnectorConfig,
): Promise<HandleResult> {
  const { notionApiKey, notionDatabaseId, pipedriveWonStageId } = config
  const fetchImpl = getFetch(config)

  const deal = validateInput(payload)

  if (deal.stage_id !== pipedriveWonStageId) {
    throw new Error(
      `Ignoring webhook: deal stage_id ${deal.stage_id} does not match Won stage ID ${pipedriveWonStageId}`,
    )
  }

  const notionPayload = buildNotionPayload(deal, notionDatabaseId)

  const response = await fetchImpl('https://api.notion.com/v1/pages', {
    method: 'POST',
    headers: {
      Authorization: `Bearer ${notionApiKey}`,
      'Notion-Version': '2022-06-28',
      'Content-Type': 'application/json',
    },
    body: JSON.stringify(notionPayload),
  })

  if (!response.ok) {
    const errorText = await response.text().catch(() => '')
    throw new Error(
      `Notion API error: ${response.status} ${response.statusText} for POST https://api.notion.com/v1/pages - ${errorText}`,
    )
  }

  const result = (await response.json()) as NotionPageResponse

  return {
    notionPageId: result.id,
    createdTime: result.created_time,
  }
}

<file path="README.md">
# Pipedrive Won Deal → Notion Signed Page

Creates a Notion page in the **Signed** database when a Pipedrive deal is moved to the **Won** stage.

## What it does

1. Receives a Pipedrive `deal.moved_to_won` webhook (v2 format).
2. Validates the payload: `meta.action === 'change'` and `data.stage_id` matches the configured Won stage ID.
3. Extracts deal fields: `title`, `value`, `owner_id`, `close_date`.
4. Calls the Notion API to create a page in the **Signed** database with properties:
   - **Title** (title) ← deal title
   - **Deal Value** (number) ← deal value
   - **Owner** (people) ← Pipedrive `owner_id` (converted to string)
   - **Close Date** (date) ← deal `close_date` (ISO string)

## Configuration

| Config key | Environment variable | Description |
|------------|---------------------|-------------|
| `notionApiKey` | `NOTION_API_KEY` | Notion integration token with write access to the target database. |
| `notionDatabaseId` | `NOTION_DATABASE_ID` | The Notion database ID for the **Signed** database. |
| `pipedriveWonStageId` | `PIPEDRIVE_WON_STAGE_ID` | The Pipedrive stage ID that represents **Won** (e.g., `5`). |
| `fetch` | — | Optional. Injected `fetch` implementation for testing or custom HTTP clients. |

All secrets come from the config object at runtime. Set the environment variables in your deployment environment.

## Usage example

```typescript
import { handle, ConnectorConfig } from './connector'

const config: ConnectorConfig = {
  notionApiKey: process.env.NOTION_API_KEY!,
  notionDatabaseId: process.env.NOTION_DATABASE_ID!,
  pipedriveWonStageId: Number(process.env.PIPEDRIVE_WON_STAGE_ID!),
}

// In your webhook handler (e.g., Express, Fastify, Cloudflare Worker):
app.post('/webhook', async (req, res) => {
  try {
    const result = await handle(req.body, config)
    res.json({ success: true, notionPageId: result.notionPageId })
  } catch (err) {
    // Validation errors (wrong action, wrong stage, missing fields) are intentional skips.
    // Other errors (Notion API failures) should be logged/alerted.
    console.error('Connector error:', err)
    res.status(500).json({ error: 'Processing failed' })
  }
})
```

## Assumptions

- The Notion database **Signed** already exists and has properties named exactly: **Title** (title), **Deal Value** (number), **Owner** (people), **Close Date** (date).
- The Pipedrive webhook payload includes `title`, `value`, `owner_id`, `close_date`, and `stage_id` under `data` when a deal moves to Won.
- The Notion integration token has permission to write to the target database.
- The Pipedrive `owner_id` (numeric) can be mapped to a valid Notion user ID by string conversion. If your Notion workspace uses different user IDs, add a mapping layer before calling the connector.
- The `close_date` from Pipedrive is an ISO date string (`YYYY-MM-DD`).
- The connector filters for `meta.action === 'change'` and the configured Won `stage_id`. Other webhook events are silently ignored (throw descriptive errors).
- Non-2xx responses from Notion throw an `Error` including the status code, status text, endpoint, and response body for observability.

  return new Response(status === 204 ? null : JSON.stringify(body), init)
}

function parseJson(raw: string | undefined): unknown {
  if (raw === undefined) return undefined
  try {
    return JSON.parse(raw)
  } catch {
    return undefined
  }
}

function urlMatches(template: string, actual: string): boolean {
  const t = splitUrl(template)
  const a = splitUrl(actual)
  if (!t || !a) return false
  const tHost = t.host.split('.')
  const aHost = a.host.split('.')
  if (tHost.slice(-2).join('.') !== aHost.slice(-2).join('.')) return false
  const tPath = t.path.replace(/\/+$/, '').split('/')
  const aPath = a.path.replace(/\/+$/, '').split('/')
  if (tPath.length !== aPath.length) return false
  return tPath.every((segment, i) => isPlaceholder(segment) || segment === aPath[i])
}

function splitUrl(url: string): { host: string; path: string } | null {
  const match = url.match(/^https?:\/\/([^/?#]+)([^?#]*)/i)
  return match ? { host: (match[1] ?? '').toLowerCase(), path: match[2] || '/' } : null
}

function isPlaceholder(segment: string): boolean {
  return /^\{[^}]+\}$|^:[A-Za-z_]\w*$|^<[^>]+>$/.test(segment)

import { createHmac } from 'crypto';

export interface ConnectorConfig {
  /** Shopify shared secret for HMAC-SHA256 verification (from SHOPIFY_CLIENT_SECRET env var) */
  shopifyClientSecret: string;
  /** Slack bot token with chat:write scope (from SLACK_BOT_TOKEN env var) */
  slackBotToken: string;
  /** Slack channel ID (e.g., C1234567890) or name (e.g., #general) */
  slackChannel: string;
  /** Raw request body as received from Shopify (required for HMAC verification) */
  rawBody?: string;
  /** Value of X-Shopify-Hmac-Sha256 header (required for HMAC verification) */
  hmacHeader?: string;
  /** Whether to verify HMAC signature (default: true). Set false if verification happens upstream. */
  verifyHmac?: boolean;
  /** Injected fetch for testing (defaults to global fetch) */
  fetch?: typeof fetch;
}

export interface ShopifyOrderWebhook {
  id: number;
  name: string;
  email: string;
  total_price: string;
  currency: string;
  line_items: Array<{
    title: string;
    quantity: number;
    price: string;
  }>;
}

export interface SlackPostResult {
  ok: boolean;
  channel: string;
  ts: string;
  slackMessageId?: string;
}

export interface HandleResult {
  slack: SlackPostResult;
}

function verifyHmac(rawBody: string, hmacHeader: string, secret: string): boolean {
  const hmac = createHmac('sha256', secret);
  hmac.update(rawBody);
  const computed = hmac.digest('base64');
  // Shopify sends the HMAC as base64-encoded string
  return computed === hmacHeader;
}

function formatSlackMessage(order: ShopifyOrderWebhook): string {
  const lines = [
    `New order ${order.name} from ${order.email} for $${order.total_price} ${order.currency}`,
  ];
  for (const item of order.line_items) {
    lines.push(`• ${item.title} x${item.quantity}`);
  }
  return lines.join('\n');
}

export async function handle(
  payload: ShopifyOrderWebhook,
  config: ConnectorConfig
): Promise<HandleResult> {
  const fetchImpl = config.fetch ?? fetch;

  // Validate required fields
  const requiredFields: Array<keyof ShopifyOrderWebhook> = [
    'id',
    'name',
    'email',
    'total_price',
    'currency',
    'line_items',
  ];
  for (const field of requiredFields) {
    if (payload[field] === undefined || payload[field] === null) {
      throw new Error(`Missing required field: ${field}`);
    }
  }
  if (!Array.isArray(payload.line_items) || payload.line_items.length === 0) {
    throw new Error('line_items must be a non-empty array');
  }

  // HMAC verification
  const shouldVerify = config.verifyHmac ?? true;
  if (shouldVerify) {
    if (!config.rawBody) {
      throw new Error('HMAC verification requires rawBody in config');
    }
    if (!config.hmacHeader) {
      throw new Error('HMAC verification requires hmacHeader in config');
    }
    const valid = verifyHmac(config.rawBody, config.hmacHeader, config.shopifyClientSecret);
    if (!valid) {
      throw new Error('Invalid HMAC signature');
    }
  }

  // Format message for Slack
  const text = formatSlackMessage(payload);

  // Post to Slack
  const slackResponse = await fetchImpl('https://slack.com/api/chat.postMessage', {
    method: 'POST',
    headers: {
      'Authorization': `Bearer ${config.slackBotToken}`,
      'Content-Type': 'application/json',
    },
    body: JSON.stringify({
      channel: config.slackChannel,
      text,
    }),
  });

  if (!slackResponse.ok) {
    throw new Error(
      `Slack API error: ${slackResponse.status} ${slackResponse.statusText} at POST https://slack.com/api/chat.postMessage`
    );
  }

  const slackResult = (await slackResponse.json()) as SlackPostResult;

  return {
    slack: {
      ok: slackResult.ok,
      channel: slackResult.channel,
      ts: slackResult.ts,
      slackMessageId: slackResult.ts,
    },
  };
}

# Shopify Order Webhook to Slack Connector

This connector receives a Shopify `orders/updated` webhook payload, verifies the HMAC-SHA256 signature using the shared secret, and posts a formatted order summary to a Slack channel via the `chat.postMessage` API.

## What it does

1. **Validates** the incoming Shopify order payload for required fields (`id`, `name`, `email`, `total_price`, `currency`, `line_items`).
2. **Verifies** the HMAC-SHA256 signature from the `X-Shopify-Hmac-Sha256` header against the raw request body using the Shopify shared secret (optional, can be disabled if verification happens upstream).
3. **Formats** a concise text summary including order reference, customer email, total, and line items.
4. **Posts** the message to the configured Slack channel using a bot token with `chat:write` scope.

## Configuration

| Config Property | Environment Variable | Required | Description |
|-----------------|---------------------|----------|-------------|
| `shopifyClientSecret` | `SHOPIFY_CLIENT_SECRET` | Yes | Shared secret from Shopify app settings for HMAC verification |
| `slackBotToken` | `SLACK_BOT_TOKEN` | Yes | Slack bot token with `chat:write` scope |
| `slackChannel` | — | Yes | Slack channel ID (e.g., `C1234567890`) or name (e.g., `#general`) |
| `rawBody` | — | If `verifyHmac=true` | Raw request body as received from Shopify (string) |
| `hmacHeader` | — | If `verifyHmac=true` | Value of `X-Shopify-Hmac-Sha256` header |
| `verifyHmac` | — | No (default: `true`) | Set `false` if HMAC verification is handled by your webhook framework |
| `fetch` | — | No | Injected fetch implementation for testing (defaults to global `fetch`) |

## Usage Example

```typescript
import { handle, ConnectorConfig } from './connector';

// In your webhook handler (e.g., Express with raw body parser):
app.post('/webhooks/orders-updated', express.raw({ type: 'application/json' }), async (req, res) => {
  const config: ConnectorConfig = {
    shopifyClientSecret: process.env.SHOPIFY_CLIENT_SECRET!,
    slackBotToken: process.env.SLACK_BOT_TOKEN!,
    slackChannel: process.env.SLACK_CHANNEL_ID!,
    rawBody: req.body, // raw string from express.raw()
    hmacHeader: req.headers['x-shopify-hmac-sha256'] as string,
    verifyHmac: true,
  };

  try {
    const result = await handle(req.body, config);
    res.status(200).send('OK');
  } catch (err) {
    console.error('Webhook processing failed:', err);
    res.status(400).send('Bad Request');
  }
});
```

## Assumptions

- The webhook payload includes standard Shopify order fields: `id`, `name`, `email`, `total_price`, `currency`, `line_items`.
- The integration has access to the Shopify shared secret (`SHOPIFY_CLIENT_SECRET`) for HMAC verification.
- The Slack channel ID or name is known and configured in the Slack app settings.
- The message posted to Slack is a concise text summary (not a full JSON dump), kept under 40,000 characters.
- The Slack bot token has the `chat:write` scope.
- Shopify will retry delivery up to 8 times over 4 hours on non-2xx responses; the webhook endpoint must respond 200 OK quickly.
- The `X-Shopify-Webhook-Id` header can be used for deduplication if needed (not implemented in this connector).
- Raw request body must be captured before any middleware parses it (e.g., using `express.raw()` in Node.js).

## Error Handling

- Throws descriptive `Error` on missing required fields.
- Throws on invalid HMAC signature when verification is enabled.
- Throws on non-2xx responses from Slack API with status code and endpoint in the message.
- All errors should be caught by the webhook handler and logged; respond 200 OK to Shopify only after successful processing.

/**

 *
 *   const { fetch, calls } = fakeFetch((req) => req.url.endsWith('/deals') ? jsonResponse({ id: 1 }, 201) : jsonResponse({}, 404))
 */
export function fakeFetch(
  handler: (request: RecordedCall) => Response | Promise<Response>,
): { fetch: typeof fetch; calls: RecordedCall[] } {
  const calls: RecordedCall[] = []

    return handler(call)

const STATUS_TEXT: Record<number, string> = {
  200: 'OK', 201: 'Created', 202: 'Accepted', 204: 'No Content',
  400: 'Bad Request', 401: 'Unauthorized', 403: 'Forbidden', 404: 'Not Found', 409: 'Conflict',
  422: 'Unprocessable Entity', 429: 'Too Many Requests',
  500: 'Internal Server Error', 502: 'Bad Gateway', 503: 'Service Unavailable',
}

/** A JSON Response with the standard status text, e.g. jsonResponse({ error: 'nope' }, 401) -> "401 Unauthorized". */
export function jsonResponse(body: unknown, status = 200): Response {
  const init = { status, statusText: STATUS_TEXT[status] ?? '', headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' } }
  return new Response(status === 204 ? null : JSON.stringify(body), init)
}

function parseJson(raw: string | undefined): unknown {
  if (raw === undefined) return undefined
  try {
    return JSON.parse(raw)
  } catch {
    return undefined
  }
}

function urlMatches(template: string, actual: string): boolean {
  const t = splitUrl(template)
  const a = splitUrl(actual)
  if (!t || !a) return false
  const tHost = t.host.split('.')
  const aHost = a.host.split('.')
  if (tHost.slice(-2).join('.') !== aHost.slice(-2).join('.')) return false
  const tPath = t.path.replace(/\/+$/, '').split('/')
  const aPath = a.path.replace(/\/+$/, '').split('/')
  if (tPath.length !== aPath.length) return false
  return tPath.every((segment, i) => isPlaceholder(segment) || segment === aPath[i])
}

function splitUrl(url: string): { host: string; path: string } | null {
  const match = url.match(/^https?:\/\/([^/?#]+)([^?#]*)/i)
  return match ? { host: (match[1] ?? '').toLowerCase(), path: match[2] || '/' } : null
}

function isPlaceholder(segment: string): boolean {
  return /^\{[^}]+\}$|^:[A-Za-z_]\w*$|^<[^>]+>$/.test(segment)
}

export interface ConnectorConfig {
  trelloApiKey: string;
  trelloApiToken: string;
  trelloListId: string;
  cardName: string;
  calWebhookSecret?: string;
  fetch?: typeof fetch;
}

export interface CalWebhookPayload {
  triggerEvent: string;
  payload: {
    attendees: Array<{
      email: string;
      name: string;
    }>;
  };
}

export interface ConnectorResult {
  cardId: string;
  checklistId: string;
  checkItemId: string;
}

async function verifyCalSignature(
  payload: string,
  signature: string | null,
  secret: string,
): Promise<void> {
  if (!signature) {
    throw new Error('Missing X-Cal-Signature header');
  }
  const encoder = new TextEncoder();
  const key = await crypto.subtle.importKey(
    'raw',
    encoder.encode(secret),
    { name: 'HMAC', hash: 'SHA-256' },
    false,
    ['verify'],
  );
  const sigBytes = Buffer.from(signature, 'base64');
  const valid = await crypto.subtle.verify('HMAC', key, sigBytes, encoder.encode(payload));
  if (!valid) {
    throw new Error('Invalid Cal.com webhook signature');
  }
}

export async function handle(
  payload: CalWebhookPayload,
  config: ConnectorConfig,
): Promise<ConnectorResult> {
  const fetch = config.fetch ?? globalThis.fetch;
  if (!fetch) {
    throw new Error('fetch is not available');
  }

  if (!payload.payload?.attendees?.length) {
    throw new Error('Payload must contain at least one attendee');
  }
  const firstAttendee = payload.payload.attendees[0];
  if (!firstAttendee.email) {
    throw new Error('First attendee must have an email');
  }

  const attendeeEmail = firstAttendee.email;
  const attendeeName = firstAttendee.name;

  const listId = config.trelloListId;
  const cardName = encodeURIComponent(config.cardName);
  const apiKey = config.trelloApiKey;
  const apiToken = config.trelloApiToken;

  const findCardUrl = `https://api.trello.com/1/lists/${listId}/cards?name=${cardName}&key=${apiKey}&token=${apiToken}`;
  const findCardResponse = await fetch(findCardUrl, { method: 'GET' });
  if (!findCardResponse.ok) {
    throw new Error(`Failed to find card: ${findCardResponse.status} ${findCardResponse.statusText} at GET ${findCardUrl}`);
  }
  const cards = (await findCardResponse.json()) as Array<{
    id: string;
    name: string;
    idList: string;
    idChecklists: string[];
  }>;

  let cardId: string;
  let checklistId: string;
  if (cards.length > 0) {
    cardId = cards[0].id;
    if (!cards[0].idChecklists?.length) {
      throw new Error('Card has no checklists');
    }
    checklistId = cards[0].idChecklists[0];
  } else {
    throw new Error(`Card "${config.cardName}" not found in list ${listId} and card creation is not supported`);
  }

  const createCheckItemUrl = `https://api.trello.com/1/checklists/${checklistId}/checkItems?key=${apiKey}&token=${apiToken}&name=${encodeURIComponent(attendeeEmail)}`;
  const createCheckItemResponse = await fetch(createCheckItemUrl, { method: 'POST' });
  if (!createCheckItemResponse.ok) {
    throw new Error(`Failed to create checklist item: ${createCheckItemResponse.status} ${createCheckItemResponse.statusText} at POST ${createCheckItemUrl}`);
  }
  const checkItem = (await createCheckItemResponse.json()) as {
    id: string;
    name: string;
    state: string;
  };

  return {
    cardId,
    checklistId,
    checkItemId: checkItem.id,
  };
}
