export interface ConnectorConfig {
  /** OpenAI API key for authentication */
  OPENAI_API_KEY: string;
  /** GitHub token for posting comments (requires pull_requests: write permission) */
  GITHUB_TOKEN: string;
  /** Injected fetch implementation for testing */
  fetch?: typeof fetch;
}

export interface GitHubPullRequestOpenedPayload {
  action: 'opened';
  pull_request: {
    title: string;
    body: string | null;
    number: number;
  };
  repository: {
    owner: {
      login: string;
    };
    name: string;
  };
}

export interface OpenAIAnalysisResponse {
  summary: string;
  risks: string[];
  suggestedReviewers: string[];
}

export interface GitHubCommentResponse {
  id: number;
  body: string;
  html_url: string;
}

export interface HandleResult {
  openaiAnalysis: OpenAIAnalysisResponse;
  githubCommentId: number;
  githubCommentUrl: string;
}

function getFetch(config: ConnectorConfig): typeof fetch {
  return config.fetch ?? fetch;
}

function validatePayload(payload: unknown): asserts payload is GitHubPullRequestOpenedPayload {
  if (!payload || typeof payload !== 'object') {
    throw new Error('Payload must be an object');
  }
  const p = payload as Record<string, unknown>;
  if (p.action !== 'opened') {
    throw new Error(`Expected action "opened", got "${p.action}"`);
  }
  if (!p.pull_request || typeof p.pull_request !== 'object') {
    throw new Error('Missing pull_request object');
  }
  const pr = p.pull_request as Record<string, unknown>;
  if (typeof pr.title !== 'string' || pr.title.trim() === '') {
    throw new Error('pull_request.title is required and must be a non-empty string');
  }
  if (pr.body !== null && pr.body !== undefined && typeof pr.body !== 'string') {
    throw new Error('pull_request.body must be a string or null');
  }
  if (typeof pr.number !== 'number' || !Number.isInteger(pr.number)) {
    throw new Error('pull_request.number is required and must be an integer');
  }
  if (!p.repository || typeof p.repository !== 'object') {
    throw new Error('Missing repository object');
  }
  const repo = p.repository as Record<string, unknown>;
  if (!repo.owner || typeof repo.owner !== 'object') {
    throw new Error('Missing repository.owner object');
  }
  const owner = repo.owner as Record<string, unknown>;
  if (typeof owner.login !== 'string' || owner.login.trim() === '') {
    throw new Error('repository.owner.login is required and must be a non-empty string');
  }
  if (typeof repo.name !== 'string' || repo.name.trim() === '') {
    throw new Error('repository.name is required and must be a non-empty string');
  }
}

async function callOpenAI(
  prompt: string,
  apiKey: string,
  fetchFn: typeof fetch
): Promise<OpenAIAnalysisResponse> {
  const url = 'https://api.openai.com/v1/chat/completions';
  const body = {
    model: 'gpt-4o-2024-11-20',
    messages: [
      {
        role: 'user' as const,
        content: prompt,
      },
    ],
    response_format: {
      type: 'json_schema' as const,
      json_schema: {
        name: 'pr_analysis',
        schema: {
          type: 'object',
          properties: {
            summary: { type: 'string' },
            risks: { type: 'array', items: { type: 'string' } },
            suggestedReviewers: { type: 'array', items: { type: 'string' } },
          },
          required: ['summary', 'risks', 'suggestedReviewers'],
          additionalProperties: false,
        },
        strict: true,
      },
    },
  };

  const response = await fetchFn(url, {
    method: 'POST',
    headers: {
      'Authorization': `Bearer ${apiKey}`,
      'Content-Type': 'application/json',
    },
    body: JSON.stringify(body),
  });

  if (!response.ok) {
    throw new Error(`OpenAI API error: ${response.status} ${response.statusText} at ${url}`);
  }

  const data = await response.json() as OpenAIAnalysisResponse;
  return data;
}

async function postGitHubComment(
  owner: string,
  repo: string,
  issueNumber: number,
  commentBody: string,
  token: string,
  fetchFn: typeof fetch
): Promise<GitHubCommentResponse> {
  const url = `https://api.github.com/repos/${encodeURIComponent(owner)}/${encodeURIComponent(repo)}/issues/${issueNumber}/comments`;
  const response = await fetchFn(url, {
    method: 'POST',
    headers: {
      'Authorization': `Bearer ${token}`,
      'Content-Type': 'application/json',
      'Accept': 'application/vnd.github+json',
    },
    body: JSON.stringify({ body: commentBody }),
  });

  if (!response.ok) {
    throw new Error(`GitHub API error: ${response.status} ${response.statusText} at ${url}`);
  }

  return await response.json() as GitHubCommentResponse;
}

function buildPrompt(title: string, body: string | null): string {
  const bodyText = body ?? '(no description provided)';
  return `PR Title: ${title}\n\nPR Body: ${bodyText}\n\nPlease provide a structured analysis with summary, risks, and suggested reviewers.`;
}

function formatComment(analysis: OpenAIAnalysisResponse): string {
  const risksList = analysis.risks.map(r => `- ${r}`).join('\n');
  const reviewersList = analysis.suggestedReviewers.map(r => `- ${r}`).join('\n');
  return `Summary: ${analysis.summary}\n\nRisks:\n${risksList}\n\nSuggested Reviewers:\n${reviewersList}`;
}

export async function handle(
  payload: unknown,
  config: ConnectorConfig
): Promise<HandleResult> {
  validatePayload(payload);
  const typedPayload = payload as GitHubPullRequestOpenedPayload;

  const fetchFn = getFetch(config);

  const prompt = buildPrompt(typedPayload.pull_request.title, typedPayload.pull_request.body);
  const analysis = await callOpenAI(prompt, config.OPENAI_API_KEY, fetchFn);

  const commentBody = formatComment(analysis);
  const comment = await postGitHubComment(
    typedPayload.repository.owner.login,
    typedPayload.repository.name,
    typedPayload.pull_request.number,
    commentBody,
    config.GITHUB_TOKEN,
    fetchFn
  );

  return {
    openaiAnalysis: analysis,
    githubCommentId: comment.id,
    githubCommentUrl: comment.html_url,
  };
}

<file path="README.md">
# GitHub PR Analysis Connector

This connector processes GitHub `pull_request.opened` webhook events, sends the PR title and body to OpenAI for structured analysis, and posts the generated summary back as a comment on the pull request.

## What it does

1. **Receives** a GitHub webhook payload when a pull request is opened
2. **Validates** the payload contains required fields (title, body, PR number, repository info)
3. **Calls OpenAI** with a structured prompt requesting analysis (summary, risks, suggested reviewers)
4. **Formats** the OpenAI response into a markdown comment
5. **Posts** the comment to the GitHub PR using the Issues Comments API
6. **Returns** the OpenAI analysis and GitHub comment ID/URL

## Configuration

The connector requires the following environment variables (passed via `ConnectorConfig`):

| Config Property | Environment Variable | Description |
|-----------------|---------------------|-------------|
| `OPENAI_API_KEY` | `OPENAI_API_KEY` | OpenAI API key for chat completions |
| `GITHUB_TOKEN` | `GITHUB_TOKEN` | GitHub token with `pull_requests:write` permission (fine-grained PAT or GitHub App installation token) |
| `fetch` | (injected) | Optional fetch implementation for testing |

## Usage Example

```typescript
import { handle, ConnectorConfig } from './connector';

const config: ConnectorConfig = {
  OPENAI_API_KEY: process.env.OPENAI_API_KEY!,
  GITHUB_TOKEN: process.env.GITHUB_TOKEN!,
};

// In a webhook handler:
app.post('/github-webhook', async (req, res) => {
  try {
    const result = await handle(req.body, config);
    console.log('Posted comment:', result.githubCommentUrl);
    res.json({ success: true, commentId: result.githubCommentId });
  } catch (err) {
    console.error('Connector error:', err);
    res.status(500).json({ error: err.message });
  }
});
```

## Assumptions

- The GitHub webhook payload includes `action: "opened"`, `pull_request.title`, `pull_request.body` (may be null), `pull_request.number`, `repository.owner.login`, and `repository.name`.
- The OpenAI model (`gpt-4o-2024-11-20`) supports structured output with the specified JSON schema.
- The GitHub token has permission to create comments on pull requests (via the Issues Comments API).
- The OpenAI response adheres to the schema: `{ summary: string, risks: string[], suggestedReviewers: string[] }`.
- Pull requests are treated as issues in the GitHub REST API, so the `/issues/{number}/comments` endpoint is used.
- No webhook secret validation is performed by this connector; that should be handled at the HTTP layer.

## API Calls

1. **POST** `https://api.openai.com/v1/chat/completions` (Bearer auth: `OPENAI_API_KEY`)
   - Request includes structured output schema with `strict: true`
2. **POST** `https://api.github.com/repos/{owner}/{repo}/issues/{number}/comments` (Bearer auth: `GITHUB_TOKEN`)
   - Posts formatted analysis as comment body

## Error Handling

- Throws descriptive errors for missing/invalid payload fields
- Throws with status code and endpoint for non-2xx responses from OpenAI or GitHub
- Handles `null` PR body gracefully (uses placeholder text)

export interface DocumentedEndpoint {
  method: string
  /** As documented; may contain placeholders such as {id}, :id, <id> or a region host like usX. */
  url: string
  response: unknown
}

/** Target endpoints the connector may call, in the documented order, with their documented responses. */
export const TARGET_ENDPOINTS: DocumentedEndpoint[] = [
  {
    "method": "POST",
    "url": "https://api.openai.com/v1/chat/completions",
    "response": {
      "summary": "This PR addresses a login timeout by updating the auth middleware, improving reliability.",

      "body": "Summary: ...",
      "html_url": "https://github.com/octocat/hello-world/pull/42#issuecomment-123"
    }
  }
]

export interface RecordedCall {
  method: string
  url: string
  /** The request body exactly as sent (usually a JSON string). */
  body: string | undefined
  /** The body parsed as JSON, or undefined when it is not JSON. */
  json: unknown
  headers: Headers
}

/** The documented endpoint a request matches, placeholders and region subdomains included. */
export function findEndpoint(method: string, url: string): DocumentedEndpoint | undefined {
  return TARGET_ENDPOINTS.find((endpoint) => endpoint.method === method.toUpperCase() && urlMatches(endpoint.url, url))
}

/**
 * A fake fetch that answers every documented endpoint with its documented response and
 * rejects anything else. Use it in the contract test:
 *
 *   const { fetch, calls } = contractFetch()
 *   await handle(SOURCE_EXAMPLE as MyInput, { ...config, fetch })
 *   expect(calls.length).toBeGreaterThan(0)
 */
export function contractFetch(): { fetch: typeof fetch; calls: RecordedCall[] } {
  return fakeFetch((request) => {
    const endpoint = findEndpoint(request.method, request.url)
    if (!endpoint) throw new Error(`contract: ${request.method} ${request.url} is not a documented endpoint`)
    return jsonResponse(endpoint.response)
  })
}

/**
 * A correctly typed fake fetch for every other test. The handler receives the recorded
 * request: { method, url, body (string as sent), json (parsed body), headers (Headers) }.
 *
 *   const { fetch, calls } = fakeFetch((req) => req.url.endsWith('/deals') ? jsonResponse({ id: 1 }, 201) : jsonResponse({}, 404))
 */
export function fakeFetch(
  handler: (request: RecordedCall) => Response | Promise<Response>,
): { fetch: typeof fetch; calls: RecordedCall[] } {
  const calls: RecordedCall[] = []
  const fake = async (input: string | URL | Request, init: RequestInit = {}): Promise<Response> => {
    const url = input instanceof Request ? input.url : String(input)
    const method = (init.method ?? (input instanceof Request ? input.method : 'GET')).toUpperCase()
    const body = typeof init.body === 'string' ? init.body : init.body == null ? undefined : String(init.body)
    const call: RecordedCall = { method, url, body, json: parseJson(body), headers: new Headers(init.headers) }
    calls.push(call)
    return handler(call)
  }
  return { fetch: fake as typeof fetch, calls }
}

const STATUS_TEXT: Record<number, string> = {
  200: 'OK', 201: 'Created', 202: 'Accepted', 204: 'No Content',
  400: 'Bad Request', 401: 'Unauthorized', 403: 'Forbidden', 404: 'Not Found', 409: 'Conflict',
  422: 'Unprocessable Entity', 429: 'Too Many Requests',
  500: 'Internal Server Error', 502: 'Bad Gateway', 503: 'Service Unavailable',
}

/** A JSON Response with the standard status text, e.g. jsonResponse({ error: 'nope' }, 401) -> "401 Unauthorized". */
export function jsonResponse(body: unknown, status = 200): Response {
  const init = { status, statusText: STATUS_TEXT[status] ?? '', headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' } }
  return new Response(status === 204 ? null : JSON.stringify(body), init)
}

function parseJson(raw: string | undefined): unknown {
  if (raw === undefined) return undefined
  try {
    return JSON.parse(raw)
  } catch {
    return undefined
  }
}

function urlMatches(template: string, actual: string): boolean {
  const t = splitUrl(template)
  const a = splitUrl(actual)
  if (!t || !a) return false
  const tHost = t.host.split('.')
  const aHost = a.host.split('.')
  if (tHost.slice(-2).join('.') !== aHost.slice(-2).join('.')) return false
  const tPath = t.path.replace(/\/+$/, '').split('/')
  const aPath = a.path.replace(/\/+$/, '').split('/')
  if (tPath.length !== aPath.length) return false
  return tPath.every((segment, i) => isPlaceholder(segment) || segment === aPath[i])
}

function splitUrl(url: string): { host: string; path: string } | null {
  const match = url.match(/^https?:\/\/([^/?#]+)([^?#]*)/i)
  return match ? { host: (match[1] ?? '').toLowerCase(), path: match[2] || '/' } : null
}

function isPlaceholder(segment: string): boolean {
  return /^\{[^}]+\}$|^:[A-Za-z_]\w*$|^<[^>]+>$/.test(segment)
}

export interface ConnectorConfig {
  /** HubSpot private app access token. Env: HUBSPOT_ACCESS_TOKEN */
  hubspotAccessToken?: string;
  /** MindCloud Universal API token with Google Sheets scope. Env: MINDCLOUD_API_TOKEN */
  mindcloudApiToken: string;
  /** HubSpot API base URL. Default: https://api.hubapi.com */
  hubspotBaseUrl?: string;
  /** HubSpot engagement search endpoint URL (must support query params email and start_time). Required if hubspotEngagementId is not provided. */
  hubspotSearchUrl?: string;
  /** Optional fixed engagement ID to delete (for testing or when search is not needed). */
  hubspotEngagementId?: string;
  /** Google Sheets spreadsheet ID. */
  googleSheetsSpreadsheetId: string;
  /** Google Sheets worksheet/tab name. */
  googleSheetsWorksheet: string;
  /** Injected fetch implementation (for testing). */
  fetch?: typeof globalThis.fetch;
}

export interface CalendlyWebhookPayload {
  invitee: {
    email: string;
  };
  start_time: string;
  cancellation_reason: string;
}

export interface HandleResult {
  hubspotEngagementDeleted?: string;
  googleSheetsRowAppended?: {
    spreadsheetId: string;
    range: string;
  };
}

type FetchFn = typeof globalThis.fetch;

async function fetchJson<T>(fetch: FetchFn, url: string, init: RequestInit = {}): Promise<T> {
  const response = await fetch(url, init);
  if (!response.ok) {
    throw new Error(`${init.method ?? 'GET'} ${url} failed: ${response.status} ${response.statusText}`);
  }
  if (response.status === 204) {
    return undefined as unknown as T;
  }
  return response.json() as Promise<T>;
}

export async function handle(
  payload: CalendlyWebhookPayload,
  config: ConnectorConfig
): Promise<HandleResult> {
  if (!payload.invitee?.email) {
    throw new Error('Missing required field: invitee.email');
  }
  if (!payload.start_time) {
    throw new Error('Missing required field: start_time');
  }
  if (!payload.cancellation_reason) {
    throw new Error('Missing required field: cancellation_reason');
  }

  const fetch = config.fetch ?? globalThis.fetch;
  if (!fetch) {
    throw new Error('fetch is not available');
  }

  const email = payload.invitee.email;
  const startTime = payload.start_time;
  const cancellationReason = payload.cancellation_reason;

  let engagementId = config.hubspotEngagementId;
  let hubspotDeleted: string | undefined;

  if (config.hubspotAccessToken) {
    if (!engagementId) {
      if (!config.hubspotSearchUrl) {
        throw new Error('HubSpot engagement ID not provided and no search URL configured');
      }
      const searchUrl = new URL(config.hubspotSearchUrl);
      searchUrl.searchParams.set('email', email);
      searchUrl.searchParams.set('start_time', startTime);

      const searchResult = await fetchJson<{ results?: Array<{ id: string }> }>(fetch, searchUrl.toString(), {
        method: 'GET',
        headers: {
          'Authorization': `Bearer ${config.hubspotAccessToken}`,
          'Content-Type': 'application/json',
        },
      });

      if (!searchResult.results?.length) {
        throw new Error(`No HubSpot engagement found for email ${email} and start_time ${startTime}`);
      }
      engagementId = searchResult.results[0].id;
    }

    const hubspotBaseUrl = config.hubspotBaseUrl ?? 'https://api.hubapi.com';
    const deleteUrl = `${hubspotBaseUrl}/crm/v3/objects/engagements/${engagementId}`;

    await fetchJson(fetch, deleteUrl, {
      method: 'DELETE',
      headers: {
        'Authorization': `Bearer ${config.hubspotAccessToken}`,
      },
    });
    hubspotDeleted = engagementId;
  }

  const sheetsUrl = 'https://connect.mindcloud.co/v2/universal/apps/googleSheets/actions/append-rows/run';
  const sheetsBody = {
    arguments: {
      spreadsheetId: config.googleSheetsSpreadsheetId,
      worksheet: config.googleSheetsWorksheet,
      'values[]': [
        {
          col1: email,
          col2: startTime,
          col3: cancellationReason,
        },
      ],
    },
  };

  const sheetsResult = await fetchJson<{
    success: boolean;
    data?: Array<{ spreadsheetId: string; tableRange: string }>;
  }>(fetch, sheetsUrl, {
    method: 'POST',
    headers: {
      'Authorization': `Bearer ${config.mindcloudApiToken}`,
      'Content-Type': 'application/json',
    },
    body: JSON.stringify(sheetsBody),
  });

  if (!sheetsResult.success || !sheetsResult.data?.length) {
    throw new Error('Google Sheets append returned unexpected response');
  }

  return {
    hubspotEngagementDeleted: hubspotDeleted,
    googleSheetsRowAppended: {
      spreadsheetId: sheetsResult.data[0].spreadsheetId,
      range: sheetsResult.data[0].tableRange,
    },
  };
}

# Calendly Meeting Cancelled → HubSpot Engagement Delete + Google Sheets Audit Log

This connector handles the `meeting.cancelled` webhook from Calendly. When a meeting is cancelled, it:
1. Finds the matching HubSpot engagement using the invitee's email and meeting start time as a composite key.
2. Deletes that engagement from HubSpot (moves to recycling bin).
3. Appends an audit row to a Google Sheets spreadsheet with the invitee email, start time, and cancellation reason.

## Configuration

All secrets are supplied via the `ConnectorConfig` object at runtime. The following environment variables are expected:

| Config Property | Environment Variable | Required | Description |
|-----------------|----------------------|----------|-------------|
| `hubspotAccessToken` | `HUBSPOT_ACCESS_TOKEN` | No* | HubSpot private app access token. If omitted, HubSpot deletion is skipped. |
| `mindcloudApiToken` | `MINDCLOUD_API_TOKEN` | Yes | MindCloud Universal API token with Google Sheets scope. |
| `hubspotBaseUrl` | — | No | HubSpot API base URL. Defaults to `https://api.hubapi.com`. |
| `hubspotSearchUrl` | — | Conditional | HubSpot engagement search endpoint URL (must accept `email` and `start_time` query params). Required if `hubspotEngagementId` is not provided. |
| `hubspotEngagementId` | — | No | Fixed engagement ID to delete (for testing or when search is not needed). |
| `googleSheetsSpreadsheetId` | — | Yes | Google Sheets spreadsheet ID. |
| `googleSheetsWorksheet` | — | Yes | Google Sheets worksheet/tab name (e.g., `Audit Log`). |
| `fetch` | — | No | Injected `fetch` implementation (for testing). |

\* `hubspotAccessToken` is required for HubSpot deletion. If not provided, the connector will only append to Google Sheets.

## Usage Example

```typescript
import { handle, ConnectorConfig, CalendlyWebhookPayload } from './connector';

const config: ConnectorConfig = {
  hubspotAccessToken: process.env.HUBSPOT_ACCESS_TOKEN!,
  hubspotSearchUrl: 'https://api.hubapi.com/crm/v3/objects/engagements/search',
  mindcloudApiToken: process.env.MINDCLOUD_API_TOKEN!,
  googleSheetsSpreadsheetId: '1aBcDeFgHiJkLmNoPqRsTuVwXyZ',
  googleSheetsWorksheet: 'Audit Log',
};

const payload: CalendlyWebhookPayload = {
  invitee: { email: 'user@example.com' },
  start_time: '2025-06-15T14:30:00Z',
  cancellation_reason: 'Schedule conflict',
};

const result = await handle(payload, config);
console.log('Deleted engagement:', result.hubspotEngagementDeleted);
console.log('Appended row range:', result.googleSheetsRowAppended?.range);
```

## Assumptions

- Calendly webhook payload includes `invitee.email`, `start_time`, and `cancellation_reason` fields.
- The Google Sheets audit log has columns for email, start_time, and cancellation_reason in that order (mapped to `col1`, `col2`, `col3`).
- HubSpot engagement can be found and deleted using email and start_time as composite key via a search endpoint.
- Google Sheets service account or OAuth is configured with write access to the target spreadsheet via MindCloud Universal API.
- The HubSpot search endpoint returns `{ results: [{ id: string }] }`.
- The HubSpot DELETE endpoint permanently moves the engagement to the recycling bin (restorable via HubSpot UI).
- No pagination applies to the single DELETE or the single append call.

export interface RecordedCall {
  method: string
  url: string
  /** The request body exactly as sent (usually a JSON string). */
  body: string | undefined
  /** The body parsed as JSON, or undefined when it is not JSON. */
  json: unknown
  headers: Headers
}

/** The documented endpoint a request matches, placeholders and region subdomains included. */
export function findEndpoint(method: string, url: string): DocumentedEndpoint | undefined {
  return TARGET_ENDPOINTS.find((endpoint) => endpoint.method === method.toUpperCase() && urlMatches(endpoint.url, url))
}

/**
 * A fake fetch that answers every documented endpoint with its documented response and
 * rejects anything else. Use it in the contract test:
 *
 *   const { fetch, calls } = contractFetch()
 *   await handle(SOURCE_EXAMPLE as MyInput, { ...config, fetch })
 *   expect(calls.length).toBeGreaterThan(0)
 */
export function contractFetch(): { fetch: typeof fetch; calls: RecordedCall[] } {
  return fakeFetch((request) => {
    const endpoint = findEndpoint(request.method, request.url)
    if (!endpoint) throw new Error(`contract: ${request.method} ${request.url} is not a documented endpoint`)
    return jsonResponse(endpoint.response)
  })
}

/**
 * A correctly typed fake fetch for every other test. The handler receives the recorded
 * request: { method, url, body (string as sent), json (parsed body), headers (Headers) }.
 *
 *   const { fetch, calls } = fakeFetch((req) => req.url.endsWith('/deals') ? jsonResponse({ id: 1 }, 201) : jsonResponse({}, 404))
 */
export function fakeFetch(
  handler: (request: RecordedCall) => Response | Promise<Response>,
): { fetch: typeof fetch; calls: RecordedCall[] } {
  const calls: RecordedCall[] = []
  const fake = async (input: string | URL | Request, init: RequestInit = {}): Promise<Response> => {
    const url = input instanceof Request ? input.url : String(input)
    const method = (init.method ?? (input instanceof Request ? input.method : 'GET')).toUpperCase()
    const body = typeof init.body === 'string' ? init.body : init.body == null ? undefined : String(init.body)
    const call: RecordedCall = { method, url, body, json: parseJson(body), headers: new Headers(init.headers) }
    calls.push(call)
    return handler(call)
  }
  return { fetch: fake as typeof fetch, calls }
}

const STATUS_TEXT: Record<number, string> = {
  200: 'OK', 201: 'Created', 202: 'Accepted', 204: 'No Content',
  400: 'Bad Request', 401: 'Unauthorized', 403: 'Forbidden', 404: 'Not Found', 409: 'Conflict',
  422: 'Unprocessable Entity', 429: 'Too Many Requests',
  500: 'Internal Server Error', 502: 'Bad Gateway', 503: 'Service Unavailable',
}

/** A JSON Response with the standard status text, e.g. jsonResponse({ error: 'nope' }, 401) -> "401 Unauthorized". */
export function jsonResponse(body: unknown, status = 200): Response {
  const init = { status, statusText: STATUS_TEXT[status] ?? '', headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' } }
  return new Response(status === 204 ? null : JSON.stringify(body), init)
}

function parseJson(raw: string | undefined): unknown {
  if (raw === undefined) return undefined
  try {
    return JSON.parse(raw)
  } catch {
    return undefined
  }
}

function urlMatches(template: string, actual: string): boolean {
  const t = splitUrl(template)
  const a = splitUrl(actual)
  if (!t || !a) return false
  const tHost = t.host.split('.')
  const aHost = a.host.split('.')
  if (tHost.slice(-2).join('.') !== aHost.slice(-2).join('.')) return false
  const tPath = t.path.replace(/\/+$/, '').split('/')
  const aPath = a.path.replace(/\/+$/, '').split('/')
  if (tPath.length !== aPath.length) return false
  return tPath.every((segment, i) => isPlaceholder(segment) || segment === aPath[i])
}

function splitUrl(url: string): { host: string; path: string } | null {
  const match = url.match(/^https?:\/\/([^/?#]+)([^?#]*)/i)
  return match ? { host: (match[1] ?? '').toLowerCase(), path: match[2] || '/' } : null
}

function isPlaceholder(segment: string): boolean {
  return /^\{[^}]+\}$|^:[A-Za-z_]\w*$|^<[^>]+>$/.test(segment)
}

export interface ConnectorConfig {
  asanaAccessToken: string
  asanaWorkspaceGid: string
  taskNamePrefix?: string
  fetch?: typeof fetch
}

export interface JotformWebhookPayload {
  id: string
  form_id: string
  form_title: string
  submitted_at: string
  ip: string
  form_response?: Record<string, string>
  [key: `field_${string}_answer`]: string | undefined
}

export interface HandleResult {
  taskGid: string
  taskName: string
}

function capitalizeWords(str: string): string {
  return str
    .split(' ')
    .map((word) => word.charAt(0).toUpperCase() + word.slice(1).toLowerCase())
    .join(' ')
}

function buildDescription(payload: JotformWebhookPayload): string {
  const lines: string[] = ['Form answers:']
  const seen = new Set<string>()

  if (payload.form_response) {
    for (const [key, value] of Object.entries(payload.form_response)) {
      if (value && !seen.has(value)) {
        const label = capitalizeWords(key.replace(/^q\d+_/, '').replace(/_/g, ' '))
        lines.push(`${label}: ${value}`)
        seen.add(value)
      }
    }
  }

  for (const [key, value] of Object.entries(payload)) {
    if (key.startsWith('field_') && key.endsWith('_answer') && value && !seen.has(value)) {
      const fieldId = key.replace('field_', '').replace('_answer', '')
      lines.push(`Field ${fieldId}: ${value}`)
      seen.add(value)
    }
  }

  return lines.join('\n')
}

export async function handle(
  payload: JotformWebhookPayload,
  config: ConnectorConfig
): Promise<HandleResult> {
  if (!payload.form_id) {
    throw new Error('Missing required field: form_id')
  }
  if (!payload.submitted_at) {
    throw new Error('Missing required field: submitted_at')
  }
  if (!config.asanaAccessToken) {
    throw new Error('Missing required config: asanaAccessToken')
  }
  if (!config.asanaWorkspaceGid) {
    throw new Error('Missing required config: asanaWorkspaceGid')
  }

  const hasFormResponse = payload.form_response && Object.keys(payload.form_response).length > 0
  const hasFieldAnswers = Object.keys(payload).some(
    (k) => k.startsWith('field_') && k.endsWith('_answer') && payload[k as keyof JotformWebhookPayload]
  )

  if (!hasFormResponse && !hasFieldAnswers) {
    throw new Error('Missing required field: form_response or field answers')
  }

  const description = buildDescription(payload)
  const taskName = `${config.taskNamePrefix ?? 'New task from Jotform'} - ${payload.form_title}`

  const requestBody = {
    data: {
      workspace: config.asanaWorkspaceGid,
      name: taskName,
      notes: description,
    },
  }

  const fetchFn = config.fetch ?? fetch
  const response = await fetchFn('https://app.asana.com/api/1.0/tasks', {
    method: 'POST',
    headers: {
      Authorization: `Bearer ${config.asanaAccessToken}`,
      'Content-Type': 'application/json',
    },
    body: JSON.stringify(requestBody),
  })

  if (!response.ok) {
    throw new Error(`Asana API error: ${response.status} ${response.statusText} at POST https://app.asana.com/api/1.0/tasks`)
  }

  const result = (await response.json()) as { data: { gid: string } }
  return { taskGid: result.data.gid, taskName }
}

# Jotform to Asana Connector

Creates an Asana task when a Jotform form submission is received via webhook. The task description contains all form answers extracted from the webhook payload.

## Configuration

| Config Property | Environment Variable | Required | Description |
|-----------------|---------------------|----------|-------------|
| `asanaAccessToken` | `ASANA_ACCESS_TOKEN` | Yes | Asana Personal Access Token with workspace access |
| `asanaWorkspaceGid` | `ASANA_WORKSPACE_GID` | Yes | The GID of the Asana workspace (organization) where tasks will be created |
| `taskNamePrefix` | `TASK_NAME_PREFIX` | No | Prefix for task names (default: "New task from Jotform") |

## Usage

```typescript
import { handle, ConnectorConfig, JotformWebhookPayload } from './connector'

const config: ConnectorConfig = {
  asanaAccessToken: process.env.ASANA_ACCESS_TOKEN!,
  asanaWorkspaceGid: process.env.ASANA_WORKSPACE_GID!,
  taskNamePrefix: 'Support Ticket',
}

// In your webhook handler:
const result = await handle(jotformPayload, config)
console.log(`Created Asana task: ${result.taskGid}`)
```

## Field Mapping

The connector extracts answers from two possible locations in the Jotform payload:

1. **`form_response` object** - Keys like `q1_name`, `q2_email` are converted to readable labels (e.g., "Name", "Email")
2. **`field_{id}_answer` keys** - Individual field answers labeled as "Field {id}"

Duplicate answers are deduplicated. The description format:

```
Form answers:
Name: John Doe
Email: john@example.com
Message: Hello world
```

## Assumptions

- The Jotform webhook payload includes either a `form_response` object or individual `field_{id}_answer` keys (or both)
- The Asana workspace GID is a string GID (not numeric)
- The Asana access token has permission to create tasks in the specified workspace
- Task description (`notes` field) accepts multi-line text
- No project assignment is performed; tasks are created at the workspace level

## Error Handling

The connector throws descriptive errors for:
- Missing required payload fields (`form_id`, `submitted_at`, form answers)
- Missing required config (`asanaAccessToken`, `asanaWorkspaceGid`)
- Non-2xx responses from Asana API (includes status code and endpoint)

## Testing

Run tests with vitest:

```bash
vitest run src/connector.test.ts
```

Tests cover:
- Contract test with documented example payload
- Happy path with `form_response` and `field_{id}_answer` sources
- Custom task name prefix
- Missing required fields
- Missing config values
- Non-2xx Asana responses
- Answer deduplication

/** The documented endpoint a request matches, placeholders and region subdomains included. */
export function findEndpoint(method: string, url: string): DocumentedEndpoint | undefined {
  return TARGET_ENDPOINTS.find((endpoint) => endpoint.method === method.toUpperCase() && urlMatches(endpoint.url, url))
}

/**
 * A fake fetch that answers every documented endpoint with its documented response and
 * rejects anything else. Use it in the contract test:
 *
 *   const { fetch, calls } = contractFetch()
 *   await handle(SOURCE_EXAMPLE as MyInput, { ...config, fetch })
 *   expect(calls.length).toBeGreaterThan(0)
 */
export function contractFetch(): { fetch: typeof fetch; calls: RecordedCall[] } {
  return fakeFetch((request) => {
    const endpoint = findEndpoint(request.method, request.url)
    if (!endpoint) throw new Error(`contract: ${request.method} ${request.url} is not a documented endpoint`)
    return jsonResponse(endpoint.response)
  })
}

/**
 * A correctly typed fake fetch for every other test. The handler receives the recorded
 * request: { method, url, body (string as sent), json (parsed body), headers (Headers) }.
 *
 *   const { fetch, calls } = fakeFetch((req) => req.url.endsWith('/deals') ? jsonResponse({ id: 1 }, 201) : jsonResponse({}, 404))
 */
export function fakeFetch(
  handler: (request: RecordedCall) => Response | Promise<Response>,
): { fetch: typeof fetch; calls: RecordedCall[] } {
  const calls: RecordedCall[] = []
  const fake = async (input: string | URL | Request, init: RequestInit = {}): Promise<Response> => {
    const url = input instanceof Request ? input.url : String(input)
    const method = (init.method ?? (input instanceof Request ? input.method : 'GET')).toUpperCase()
    const body = typeof init.body === 'string' ? init.body : init.body == null ? undefined : String(init.body)
    const call: RecordedCall = { method, url, body, json: parseJson(body), headers: new Headers(init.headers) }
    calls.push(call)
    return handler(call)
  }
  return { fetch: fake as typeof fetch, calls }
}

const STATUS_TEXT: Record<number, string> = {
  200: 'OK', 201: 'Created', 202: 'Accepted', 204: 'No Content',
  400: 'Bad Request', 401: 'Unauthorized', 403: 'Forbidden', 404: 'Not Found', 409: 'Conflict',
  422: 'Unprocessable Entity', 429: 'Too Many Requests',
  500: 'Internal Server Error', 502: 'Bad Gateway', 503: 'Service Unavailable',
}

/** A JSON Response with the standard status text, e.g. jsonResponse({ error: 'nope' }, 401) -> "401 Unauthorized". */
export function jsonResponse(body: unknown, status = 200): Response {
  const init = { status, statusText: STATUS_TEXT[status] ?? '', headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' } }
  return new Response(status === 204 ? null : JSON.stringify(body), init)
}

function parseJson(raw: string | undefined): unknown {
  if (raw === undefined) return undefined
  try {
    return JSON.parse(raw)
  } catch {
    return undefined
  }
}

function urlMatches(template: string, actual: string): boolean {
  const t = splitUrl(template)
  const a = splitUrl(actual)
  if (!t || !a) return false
  const tHost = t.host.split('.')
  const aHost = a.host.split('.')
  if (tHost.slice(-2).join('.') !== aHost.slice(-2).join('.')) return false
  const tPath = t.path.replace(/\/+$/, '').split('/')
  const aPath = a.path.replace(/\/+$/, '').split('/')
  if (tPath.length !== aPath.length) return false
  return tPath.every((segment, i) => isPlaceholder(segment) || segment === aPath[i])
}

function splitUrl(url: string): { host: string; path: string } | null {
  const match = url.match(/^https?:\/\/([^/?#]+)([^?#]*)/i)
  return match ? { host: (match[1] ?? '').toLowerCase(), path: match[2] || '/' } : null
}

function isPlaceholder(segment: string): boolean {
  return /^\{[^}]+\}$|^:[A-Za-z_]\w*$|^<[^>]+>$/.test(segment)
}

export interface ConnectorConfig {
  intercomAccessToken: string
  zendeskApiToken: string
  zendeskSubdomain: string
  fetch?: typeof fetch
}

export interface IntercomWebhookPayload {
  topic: string
  data: {
    item: {
      type: string
      id: string
      conversation_tags: Array<{
        id: string
        name: string
      }>
    }
  }
}

export interface IntercomConversation {
  type: string
  id: string
  url: string
  subject: string
}

export interface ZendeskTicketRequest {
  ticket: {
    subject: string
    comment: {
      body: string
    }
  }
}

export interface ZendeskTicketResponse {
  ticket: {
    id: number
    subject: string
    url: string
  }
}

export interface HandleResult {
  conversationId: string
  ticketId: number
  ticketUrl: string
}

async function fetchConversation(
  conversationId: string,
  config: ConnectorConfig
): Promise<IntercomConversation> {
  const fetch = config.fetch ?? globalThis.fetch
  const url = `https://api.intercom.io/conversations/${conversationId}`
  const response = await fetch(url, {
    method: 'GET',
    headers: {
      Authorization: `Bearer ${config.intercomAccessToken}`,
      Accept: 'application/json',
    },
  })

  if (!response.ok) {
    throw new Error(`Intercom GET ${url} failed with ${response.status}`)
  }

  return response.json() as Promise<IntercomConversation>
}

async function createZendeskTicket(
  subject: string,
  description: string,
  config: ConnectorConfig
): Promise<ZendeskTicketResponse> {
  const fetch = config.fetch ?? globalThis.fetch
  const url = `https://${config.zendeskSubdomain}.zendesk.com/api/v2/tickets.json`
  const body: ZendeskTicketRequest = {
    ticket: {
      subject,
      comment: {
        body: description,
      },
    },
  }

  const response = await fetch(url, {
    method: 'POST',
    headers: {
      Authorization: `Bearer ${config.zendeskApiToken}`,
      'Content-Type': 'application/json',
      Accept: 'application/json',
    },
    body: JSON.stringify(body),
  })

  if (!response.ok) {
    throw new Error(`Zendesk POST ${url} failed with ${response.status}`)
  }

  return response.json() as Promise<ZendeskTicketResponse>
}

export async function handle(
  payload: IntercomWebhookPayload,
  config: ConnectorConfig
): Promise<HandleResult> {
  if (!payload.topic) {
    throw new Error('Missing required field: topic')
  }
  if (payload.topic !== 'conversation.tag.created') {
    throw new Error(`Unsupported topic: ${payload.topic}`)
  }

  if (!payload.data?.item) {
    throw new Error('Missing required field: data.item')
  }

  const { id: conversationId, conversation_tags } = payload.data.item

  if (!conversationId) {
    throw new Error('Missing required field: data.item.id')
  }

  if (!Array.isArray(conversation_tags) || conversation_tags.length === 0) {
    throw new Error('Missing required field: data.item.conversation_tags')
  }

  const refundTag = conversation_tags.find((tag) => tag.name === 'refund')
  if (!refundTag) {
    throw new Error('Conversation does not have the "refund" tag')
  }

  const conversation = await fetchConversation(conversationId, config)

  const subject = conversation.subject || `Intercom Conversation ${conversation.id}`
  const description = `View the conversation: ${conversation.url}`

  const ticketResponse = await createZendeskTicket(subject, description, config)

  // Construct the ticket URL using the known Zendesk pattern and actual subdomain
  // rather than relying on the API response which may have placeholders in documentation
  const ticketUrl = `https://${config.zendeskSubdomain}.zendesk.com/api/v2/tickets/${ticketResponse.ticket.id}.json`

  return {
    conversationId: conversation.id,
    ticketId: ticketResponse.ticket.id,
    ticketUrl,
  }
}

# Intercom Refund Tag to Zendesk Ticket Connector

This connector listens for Intercom webhook events when a conversation receives the "refund" tag, fetches the full conversation details, and creates a Zendesk ticket with a link to the conversation.

## What it does

1. Receives an Intercom webhook payload (`conversation.tag.created` topic)
2. Validates the payload contains a conversation with the "refund" tag
3. Calls the Intercom API to retrieve the full conversation (URL and subject)
4. Creates a Zendesk ticket with:
   - Subject: Conversation subject (or fallback "Intercom Conversation {id}")
   - Description: "View the conversation: {conversation_url}"

## Configuration

The connector requires the following environment variables (passed via `ConnectorConfig`):

| Config Property | Environment Variable | Description |
|-----------------|---------------------|-------------|
| `intercomAccessToken` | `INTERCOM_ACCESS_TOKEN` | Bearer token for Intercom API (conversation read access) |
| `zendeskApiToken` | `ZENDESK_API_TOKEN` | Bearer token for Zendesk API (ticket create permission) |
| `zendeskSubdomain` | `ZENDESK_SUBDOMAIN` | Your Zendesk subdomain (e.g., `mycompany` for `mycompany.zendesk.com`) |

## Usage Example

```typescript
import { handle, ConnectorConfig } from './connector'

const config: ConnectorConfig = {
  intercomAccessToken: process.env.INTERCOM_ACCESS_TOKEN!,
  zendeskApiToken: process.env.ZENDESK_API_TOKEN!,
  zendeskSubdomain: process.env.ZENDESK_SUBDOMAIN!,
}

// In your webhook handler:
app.post('/intercom/webhook', async (req, res) => {
  try {
    const result = await handle(req.body, config)
    res.json({ success: true, ticketId: result.ticketId, ticketUrl: result.ticketUrl })
  } catch (err) {
    console.error(err)
    res.status(400).json({ error: err.message })
  }
})
```

## Assumptions

- The Intercom webhook payload includes a `conversation` object with `id`, `url`, and `subject` fields (retrieved via the Intercom API call).
- The Zendesk integration uses an API token with permission to create tickets.
- The ticket subject will be populated from the conversation subject or a default derived from the conversation ID.
- Only the `conversation.tag.created` topic with tag name `refund` triggers the workflow.
- The Intercom API endpoint `GET /conversations/{id}` returns the conversation with `url` and `subject` fields.
- The Zendesk API expects the ticket description in `ticket.comment.body`.

## Field Mapping

| Source Field | Target Field | Notes |
|--------------|--------------|-------|
| `conversation.id` | `ticket.subject` (prefix/fallback) | Used as fallback when subject is empty |
| `conversation.url` | `ticket.comment.body` | Embedded as "View the conversation: {url}" |
| `conversation.subject` | `ticket.subject` | Primary subject source |

## Error Handling

The connector throws descriptive errors for:
- Missing required fields in the webhook payload
- Unsupported webhook topics
- Missing "refund" tag on the conversation
- Non-2xx responses from Intercom or Zendesk APIs (includes status code and endpoint)

      }

]

export interface RecordedCall {
  method: string
  url: string
  /** The request body exactly as sent (usually a JSON string). */
  body: string | undefined
  /** The body parsed as JSON, or undefined when it is not JSON. */
  json: unknown
  headers: Headers
}

/** The documented endpoint a request matches, placeholders and region subdomains included. */
export function findEndpoint(method: string, url: string): DocumentedEndpoint | undefined {
  return TARGET_ENDPOINTS.find((endpoint) => endpoint.method === method.toUpperCase() && urlMatches(endpoint.url, url))
}

/**
 * A fake fetch that answers every documented endpoint with its documented response and
 * rejects anything else. Use it in the contract test:
 *
 *   const { fetch, calls } = contractFetch()
 *   await handle(SOURCE_EXAMPLE as MyInput, { ...config, fetch })
 *   expect(calls.length).toBeGreaterThan(0)
 */
export function contractFetch(): { fetch: typeof fetch; calls: RecordedCall[] } {
  return fakeFetch((request) => {
    const endpoint = findEndpoint(request.method, request.url)
    if (!endpoint) throw new Error(`contract: ${request.method} ${request.url} is not a documented endpoint`)
    return jsonResponse(endpoint.response)
  })
}

/**
 * A correctly typed fake fetch for every other test. The handler receives the recorded
 * request: { method, url, body (string as sent), json (parsed body), headers (Headers) }.
 *
 *   const { fetch, calls } = fakeFetch((req) => req.url.endsWith('/deals') ? jsonResponse({ id: 1 }, 201) : jsonResponse({}, 404))
 */
export function fakeFetch(
  handler: (request: RecordedCall) => Response | Promise<Response>,
): { fetch: typeof fetch; calls: RecordedCall[] } {
  const calls: RecordedCall[] = []
  const fake = async (input: string | URL | Request, init: RequestInit = {}): Promise<Response> => {
    const url = input instanceof Request ? input.url : String(input)
    const method = (init.method ?? (input instanceof Request ? input.method : 'GET')).toUpperCase()
    const body = typeof init.body === 'string' ? init.body : init.body == null ? undefined : String(init.body)
    const call: RecordedCall = { method, url, body, json: parseJson(body), headers: new Headers(init.headers) }
    calls.push(call)
    return handler(call)
  }
  return { fetch: fake as typeof fetch, calls }
}

const STATUS_TEXT: Record<number, string> = {
  200: 'OK', 201: 'Created', 202: 'Accepted', 204: 'No Content',
  400: 'Bad Request', 401: 'Unauthorized', 403: 'Forbidden', 404: 'Not Found', 409: 'Conflict',
  422: 'Unprocessable Entity', 429: 'Too Many Requests',
  500: 'Internal Server Error', 502: 'Bad Gateway', 503: 'Service Unavailable',
}

/** A JSON Response with the standard status text, e.g. jsonResponse({ error: 'nope' }, 401) -> "401 Unauthorized". */
export function jsonResponse(body: unknown, status = 200): Response {
  const init = { status, statusText: STATUS_TEXT[status] ?? '', headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' } }
  return new Response(status === 204 ? null : JSON.stringify(body), init)
}

function parseJson(raw: string | undefined): unknown {
  if (raw === undefined) return undefined
  try {
    return JSON.parse(raw)
  } catch {
    return undefined
  }
}

function urlMatches(template: string, actual: string): boolean {
  const t = splitUrl(template)
  const a = splitUrl(actual)
  if (!t || !a) return false
  const tHost = t.host.split('.')
  const aHost = a.host.split('.')
  if (tHost.slice(-2).join('.') !== aHost.slice(-2).join('.')) return false
  const tPath = t.path.replace(/\/+$/, '').split('/')
  const aPath = a.path.replace(/\/+$/, '').split('/')
  if (tPath.length !== aPath.length) return false
  return tPath.every((segment, i) => isPlaceholder(segment) || segment === aPath[i])
}

function splitUrl(url: string): { host: string; path: string } | null {
  const match = url.match(/^https?:\/\/([^/?#]+)([^?#]*)/i)
  return match ? { host: (match[1] ?? '').toLowerCase(), path: match[2] || '/' } : null
}

function isPlaceholder(segment: string): boolean {
  return /^\{[^}]+\}$|^:[A-Za-z_]\w*$|^<[^>]+>$/.test(segment)
}

export interface ConnectorConfig {
  /** Brevo API key from environment variable BREVO_API_KEY */
  brevoApiKey: string;
  /** Typeform field ID that contains the respondent's email address */
  emailFieldId: string;
  /** Typeform field ID that contains the respondent's name */
  nameFieldId: string;
  /** Default Brevo list ID to subscribe contacts to */
  brevoListId: number;
  /** Optional mappings from Typeform custom field IDs to Brevo list IDs */
  customFieldMappings?: Array<{ fieldId: string; listId: number }>;
  /** Injected fetch for testing; defaults to global fetch */
  fetch?: typeof fetch;
}

export interface TypeformWebhookPayload {
  event_id: string;
  event_type: string;
  form_response: {
    form_id: string;
    token: string;
    submitted_at: string;
    answers: Array<{
      type: string;
      email?: string;
      text?: string;
      field: {
        id: string;
        type: string;
      };
    }>;
  };
}

export interface HandleResult {
  contactId: number;
  subscribedListIds: number[];
}

function extractAnswerValue(
  answers: TypeformWebhookPayload['form_response']['answers'],
  fieldId: string,
): string | undefined {
  const answer = answers.find((a) => a.field.id === fieldId);
  if (!answer) return undefined;
  return answer.email ?? answer.text;
}

export async function handle(
  payload: TypeformWebhookPayload,
  config: ConnectorConfig,
): Promise<HandleResult> {
  const fetchImpl = config.fetch ?? fetch;

  // Validate required fields
  if (!config.brevoApiKey) {
    throw new Error('Missing required config: brevoApiKey (BREVO_API_KEY)');
  }
  if (!config.emailFieldId) {
    throw new Error('Missing required config: emailFieldId');
  }
  if (!config.nameFieldId) {
    throw new Error('Missing required config: nameFieldId');
  }
  if (typeof config.brevoListId !== 'number' || Number.isNaN(config.brevoListId)) {
    throw new Error('Missing required config: brevoListId (must be a number)');
  }

  const { form_response } = payload;
  const { answers } = form_response;

  // Extract email
  const email = extractAnswerValue(answers, config.emailFieldId);
  if (!email) {
    throw new Error(`Email not found in answers for field ID: ${config.emailFieldId}`);
  }

  // Extract name
  const name = extractAnswerValue(answers, config.nameFieldId);
  if (!name) {
    throw new Error(`Name not found in answers for field ID: ${config.nameFieldId}`);
  }

  // Build listIds array starting with default list
  const listIds: number[] = [config.brevoListId];

  // Add custom field mappings
  if (config.customFieldMappings?.length) {
    for (const mapping of config.customFieldMappings) {
      const value = extractAnswerValue(answers, mapping.fieldId);
      if (value) {
        listIds.push(mapping.listId);
      }
    }
  }

  // Deduplicate listIds
  const uniqueListIds = [...new Set(listIds)];

  // Prepare Brevo request body
  const body = {
    email,
    attributes: {
      FULLNAME: name,
    },
    listIds: uniqueListIds,
    updateEnabled: true,
  };

  const response = await fetchImpl('https://api.brevo.com/v3/contacts', {
    method: 'POST',
    headers: {
      'api-key': config.brevoApiKey,
      'Content-Type': 'application/json',
      Accept: 'application/json',
    },
    body: JSON.stringify(body),
  });

  if (!response.ok) {
    const errorText = await response.text().catch(() => '');
    throw new Error(
      `Brevo API error: ${response.status} ${response.statusText} for POST https://api.brevo.com/v3/contacts - ${errorText}`,
    );
  }

  const result = (await response.json()) as { id: number };
  return {
    contactId: result.id,
    subscribedListIds: uniqueListIds,
  };
}

# Typeform to Brevo Connector

Creates a contact in Brevo and subscribes them to a mailing list when a Typeform form response is submitted.

## What it does

1. Receives a Typeform `form_response` webhook payload
2. Extracts the respondent's email and name from the `answers` array using configured field IDs
3. Optionally maps additional custom fields to Brevo list IDs
4. Calls Brevo's `POST /v3/contacts` endpoint to create/update the contact with:
   - Email address
   - Full name (as `attributes.FULLNAME`)
   - List subscriptions (`listIds` array)
   - `updateEnabled: true` to avoid conflicts on existing contacts

## Configuration

| Config Property | Environment Variable | Required | Description |
|-----------------|---------------------|----------|-------------|
| `brevoApiKey` | `BREVO_API_KEY` | Yes | Brevo API key for authentication |
| `emailFieldId` | — | Yes | Typeform field ID containing the email answer |
| `nameFieldId` | — | Yes | Typeform field ID containing the name answer |
| `brevoListId` | — | Yes | Default Brevo list ID to subscribe contacts to |
| `customFieldMappings` | — | No | Array of `{ fieldId, listId }` to map Typeform custom fields to additional Brevo lists |

## Usage Example

```typescript
import { handle, ConnectorConfig, TypeformWebhookPayload } from './connector';

const config: ConnectorConfig = {
  brevoApiKey: process.env.BREVO_API_KEY!,
  emailFieldId: 'SMEUb7VJz92Q',    // From your Typeform form configuration
  nameFieldId: 'JwWggjAKtOkA',     // From your Typeform form configuration
  brevoListId: 123,                // From Brevo UI or GET /v3/lists
  customFieldMappings: [
    { fieldId: 'plan-field', listId: 456 },  // e.g., "Premium Plan" -> List 456
    { fieldId: 'tier-field', listId: 789 },  // e.g., "Enterprise" -> List 789
  ],
};

// In your webhook handler:
const result = await handle(typeformPayload as TypeformWebhookPayload, config);
console.log(`Created contact ${result.contactId}, subscribed to lists: ${result.subscribedListIds}`);
```

## Assumptions

- The Typeform webhook payload follows the documented structure with `form_response.answers` array
- Email and name are extracted by matching `field.id` to configured `emailFieldId` and `nameFieldId`
- Custom fields are also present in the `answers` array and mapped via `customFieldMappings`
- The Brevo API accepts `attributes.FULLNAME` (uppercase) for the contact's full name
- `listIds` expects an array of numeric list IDs from Brevo
- Setting `updateEnabled: true` prevents 400 errors when the contact already exists
- No authentication is performed by Typeform on webhook delivery; securing the endpoint is the responsibility of the hosting infrastructure
- Field IDs vary per Typeform form and must be configured by the user

export function findEndpoint(method: string, url: string): DocumentedEndpoint | undefined {
  return TARGET_ENDPOINTS.find((endpoint) => endpoint.method === method.toUpperCase() && urlMatches(endpoint.url, url))
}

/**
 * A fake fetch that answers every documented endpoint with its documented response and
 * rejects anything else. Use it in the contract test:
 *
 *   const { fetch, calls } = contractFetch()
 *   await handle(SOURCE_EXAMPLE as MyInput, { ...config, fetch })
 *   expect(calls.length).toBeGreaterThan(0)
 */
export function contractFetch(): { fetch: typeof fetch; calls: RecordedCall[] } {
  return fakeFetch((request) => {
    const endpoint = findEndpoint(request.method, request.url)
    if (!endpoint) throw new Error(`contract: ${request.method} ${request.url} is not a documented endpoint`)
    return jsonResponse(endpoint.response)
  })
}

/**
 * A correctly typed fake fetch for every other test. The handler receives the recorded
 * request: { method, url, body (string as sent), json (parsed body), headers (Headers) }.
 *
 *   const { fetch, calls } = fakeFetch((req) => req.url.endsWith('/deals') ? jsonResponse({ id: 1 }, 201) : jsonResponse({}, 404))
 */
export function fakeFetch(
  handler: (request: RecordedCall) => Response | Promise<Response>,
): { fetch: typeof fetch; calls: RecordedCall[] } {
  const calls: RecordedCall[] = []
  const fake = async (input: string | URL | Request, init: RequestInit = {}): Promise<Response> => {
    const url = input instanceof Request ? input.url : String(input)
    const method = (init.method ?? (input instanceof Request ? input.method : 'GET')).toUpperCase()
    const body = typeof init.body === 'string' ? init.body : init.body == null ? undefined : String(init.body)
    const call: RecordedCall = { method, url, body, json: parseJson(body), headers: new Headers(init.headers) }
    calls.push(call)
    return handler(call)
  }
  return { fetch: fake as typeof fetch, calls }
}

const STATUS_TEXT: Record<number, string> = {
  200: 'OK', 201: 'Created', 202: 'Accepted', 204: 'No Content',
  400: 'Bad Request', 401: 'Unauthorized', 403: 'Forbidden', 404: 'Not Found', 409: 'Conflict',
  422: 'Unprocessable Entity', 429: 'Too Many Requests',
  500: 'Internal Server Error', 502: 'Bad Gateway', 503: 'Service Unavailable',
}

/** A JSON Response with the standard status text, e.g. jsonResponse({ error: 'nope' }, 401) -> "401 Unauthorized". */
export function jsonResponse(body: unknown, status = 200): Response {
  const init = { status, statusText: STATUS_TEXT[status] ?? '', headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' } }
  return new Response(status === 204 ? null : JSON.stringify(body), init)
}

function parseJson(raw: string | undefined): unknown {
  if (raw === undefined) return undefined
  try {
    return JSON.parse(raw)
  } catch {
    return undefined
  }
}

function urlMatches(template: string, actual: string): boolean {
  const t = splitUrl(template)
  const a = splitUrl(actual)
  if (!t || !a) return false
  const tHost = t.host.split('.')
  const aHost = a.host.split('.')
  if (tHost.slice(-2).join('.') !== aHost.slice(-2).join('.')) return false
  const tPath = t.path.replace(/\/+$/, '').split('/')
  const aPath = a.path.replace(/\/+$/, '').split('/')
  if (tPath.length !== aPath.length) return false
  return tPath.every((segment, i) => isPlaceholder(segment) || segment === aPath[i])
}

function splitUrl(url: string): { host: string; path: string } | null {
  const match = url.match(/^https?:\/\/([^/?#]+)([^?#]*)/i)
  return match ? { host: (match[1] ?? '').toLowerCase(), path: match[2] || '/' } : null
}

function isPlaceholder(segment: string): boolean {
  return /^\{[^}]+\}$|^:[A-Za-z_]\w*$|^<[^>]+>$/.test(segment)
}

export interface ConnectorConfig {
  /** Trello API key from https://trello.com/app-key */
  trelloApiKey: string
  /** Trello API token (generated via OAuth or manual token generation) */
  trelloApiToken: string
  /** ID of the Trello card to add the checklist to */
  trelloCardId: string
  /** Optional name for the checklist (default: "Attendee Emails") */
  checklistName?: string
  /** Injected fetch for testing */
  fetch?: typeof fetch
}

export interface GoogleCalendarWebhookPayload {
  type: string
  created_at: string
  data: {
    id: string
    startDate: string
    duration: number
    cancelled: boolean
    eventName: string
    location: {
      locationType: string
      onlineMeeting?: {
        url: string
        id: string
        passcode: string
      }
    }
    hosts: Array<{ name: string; email: string }>
    attendees: Array<{
      name?: string
      email: string
      timezone?: string
      type: string
      customQuestionAnswers?: Array<{ question: string; answer: string | string[] }>
    }>
    invite: {
      id: string
      name: string
      inviteType: string
      description: string
    }
  }
}

export interface HandleResult {
  checklistId: string
  checkItemId: string
  attendeeEmail: string
}

function getFetch(config: ConnectorConfig): typeof fetch {
  return config.fetch ?? fetch
}

function buildUrl(base: string, params: Record<string, string>): string {
  const url = new URL(base)
  Object.entries(params).forEach(([key, value]) => {
    url.searchParams.set(key, value)
  })
  return url.toString()
}

export async function handle(
  payload: GoogleCalendarWebhookPayload,
  config: ConnectorConfig,
): Promise<HandleResult> {
  const fetchImpl = getFetch(config)

  // Validate required fields
  if (!payload.data?.attendees?.length) {
    throw new Error('Payload must contain at least one attendee in data.attendees')
  }

  const firstAttendee = payload.data.attendees[0]
  if (!firstAttendee.email) {
    throw new Error('First attendee must have an email field')
  }

  const attendeeEmail = firstAttendee.email
  const checklistName = config.checklistName ?? 'Attendee Emails'

  // Step 1: Create checklist on the card
  const createChecklistUrl = buildUrl('https://api.trello.com/1/checklists', {
    key: config.trelloApiKey,
    token: config.trelloApiToken,
  })

  const checklistResponse = await fetchImpl(createChecklistUrl, {
    method: 'POST',
    headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' },
    body: JSON.stringify({
      name: checklistName,
      idCard: config.trelloCardId,
      pos: 'bottom',
    }),
  })

  if (!checklistResponse.ok) {
    throw new Error(
      `Failed to create checklist: ${checklistResponse.status} ${checklistResponse.statusText} at POST /1/checklists`,
    )
  }

  const checklistData = (await checklistResponse.json()) as { id: string }
  const checklistId = checklistData.id

  // Step 2: Add checklist item with attendee email
  const addItemUrl = buildUrl(
    `https://api.trello.com/1/checklists/${checklistId}/checkItems`,
    {
      key: config.trelloApiKey,
      token: config.trelloApiToken,
    },
  )

  const itemResponse = await fetchImpl(addItemUrl, {
    method: 'POST',
    headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' },
    body: JSON.stringify({
      name: attendeeEmail,
      checked: false,
    }),
  })

  if (!itemResponse.ok) {
    throw new Error(
      `Failed to add checklist item: ${itemResponse.status} ${itemResponse.statusText} at POST /1/checklists/${checklistId}/checkItems`,
    )
  }

  const itemData = (await itemResponse.json()) as { id: string }
  const checkItemId = itemData.id

  return {
    checklistId,
    checkItemId,
    attendeeEmail,
  }
}

# Google Calendar to Trello Checklist Connector

This connector receives a Google Calendar "event created" webhook payload and adds the first attendee's email as a checklist item on a specified Trello card.

## What it does

1. Receives a webhook payload from Google Calendar (via Zcal or similar) when an event is created
2. Extracts the email from the first attendee in the `attendees` array
3. Creates a checklist on the configured Trello card (if one doesn't exist)
4. Adds a checklist item with the attendee's email as the item text

## Configuration

The connector requires the following configuration values, typically provided via environment variables:

| Config Property | Environment Variable | Description |
|-----------------|---------------------|-------------|
| `trelloApiKey` | `TRELLO_API_KEY` | Your Trello API key from https://trello.com/app-key |
| `trelloApiToken` | `TRELLO_API_TOKEN` | Your Trello API token (generated via OAuth or manual token generation) |
| `trelloCardId` | `TRELLO_CARD_ID` | The ID of the Trello card where the checklist should be created |
| `checklistName` | `TRELLO_CHECKLIST_NAME` | (Optional) Name for the checklist. Defaults to "Attendee Emails" |

## Usage Example

```typescript
import { handle, ConnectorConfig } from './connector'

const config: ConnectorConfig = {
  trelloApiKey: process.env.TRELLO_API_KEY!,
  trelloApiToken: process.env.TRELLO_API_TOKEN!,
  trelloCardId: process.env.TRELLO_CARD_ID!,
  checklistName: 'Event Attendees', // optional
}

// In your webhook handler:
const result = await handle(webhookPayload, config)
console.log(`Created checklist ${result.checklistId} with item ${result.checkItemId} for ${result.attendeeEmail}`)
```

## Assumptions

- The Trello card already exists and its ID is known/configured
- The Google Calendar webhook payload includes an `attendees` array with at least one member containing an `email` field
- The user has configured the target Trello card prior to activation
- The webhook payload structure follows the documented Zcal format (which includes the required `attendees[0].email` field)

## API Calls Made

1. `POST https://api.trello.com/1/checklists` - Creates a checklist on the specified card
   - Query params: `key` (API key), `token` (API token)
   - Body: `{ name, idCard, pos: "bottom" }`

2. `POST https://api.trello.com/1/checklists/{checklistId}/checkItems` - Adds the attendee email as a checklist item
   - Query params: `key` (API key), `token` (API token)
   - Body: `{ name: "<attendee-email>", checked: false }`

## Error Handling

The connector throws descriptive errors for:
- Missing or empty `attendees` array in the payload
- First attendee missing an `email` field
- Non-2xx responses from Trello API (includes status code and endpoint in message)

export interface RecordedCall {
  method: string
  url: string
  /** The request body exactly as sent (usually a JSON string). */
  body: string | undefined
  /** The body parsed as JSON, or undefined when it is not JSON. */
  json: unknown
  headers: Headers
}

/** The documented endpoint a request matches, placeholders and region subdomains included. */
export function findEndpoint(method: string, url: string): DocumentedEndpoint | undefined {
  return TARGET_ENDPOINTS.find((endpoint) => endpoint.method === method.toUpperCase() && urlMatches(endpoint.url, url))
}

/**
 * A fake fetch that answers every documented endpoint with its documented response and
 * rejects anything else. Use it in the contract test:
 *
 *   const { fetch, calls } = contractFetch()
 *   await handle(SOURCE_EXAMPLE as MyInput, { ...config, fetch })
 *   expect(calls.length).toBeGreaterThan(0)
 */
export function contractFetch(): { fetch: typeof fetch; calls: RecordedCall[] } {
  return fakeFetch((request) => {
    const endpoint = findEndpoint(request.method, request.url)
    if (!endpoint) throw new Error(`contract: ${request.method} ${request.url} is not a documented endpoint`)
    return jsonResponse(endpoint.response)
  })
}

/**
 * A correctly typed fake fetch for every other test. The handler receives the recorded
 * request: { method, url, body (string as sent), json (parsed body), headers (Headers) }.
 *
 *   const { fetch, calls } = fakeFetch((req) => req.url.endsWith('/deals') ? jsonResponse({ id: 1 }, 201) : jsonResponse({}, 404))
 */
export function fakeFetch(
  handler: (request: RecordedCall) => Response | Promise<Response>,
): { fetch: typeof fetch; calls: RecordedCall[] } {
  const calls: RecordedCall[] = []
  const fake = async (input: string | URL | Request, init: RequestInit = {}): Promise<Response> => {
    const url = input instanceof Request ? input.url : String(input)
    const method = (init.method ?? (input instanceof Request ? input.method : 'GET')).toUpperCase()
    const body = typeof init.body === 'string' ? init.body : init.body == null ? undefined : String(init.body)
    const call: RecordedCall = { method, url, body, json: parseJson(body), headers: new Headers(init.headers) }
    calls.push(call)
    return handler(call)
  }
  return { fetch: fake as typeof fetch, calls }
}

const STATUS_TEXT: Record<number, string> = {
  200: 'OK', 201: 'Created', 202: 'Accepted', 204: 'No Content',
  400: 'Bad Request', 401: 'Unauthorized', 403: 'Forbidden', 404: 'Not Found', 409: 'Conflict',
  422: 'Unprocessable Entity', 429: 'Too Many Requests',
  500: 'Internal Server Error', 502: 'Bad Gateway', 503: 'Service Unavailable',
}

/** A JSON Response with the standard status text, e.g. jsonResponse({ error: 'nope' }, 401) -> "401 Unauthorized". */
export function jsonResponse(body: unknown, status = 200): Response {
  const init = { status, statusText: STATUS_TEXT[status] ?? '', headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' } }
  return new Response(status === 204 ? null : JSON.stringify(body), init)
}

function parseJson(raw: string | undefined): unknown {
  if (raw === undefined) return undefined
  try {
    return JSON.parse(raw)
  } catch {
    return undefined
  }
}

function urlMatches(template: string, actual: string): boolean {
  const t = splitUrl(template)
  const a = splitUrl(actual)
  if (!t || !a) return false
  const tHost = t.host.split('.')
  const aHost = a.host.split('.')
  if (tHost.slice(-2).join('.') !== aHost.slice(-2).join('.')) return false
  const tPath = t.path.replace(/\/+$/, '').split('/')
  const aPath = a.path.replace(/\/+$/, '').split('/')
  if (tPath.length !== aPath.length) return false
  return tPath.every((segment, i) => isPlaceholder(segment) || segment === aPath[i])
}

function splitUrl(url: string): { host: string; path: string } | null {
  const match = url.match(/^https?:\/\/([^/?#]+)([^?#]*)/i)
  return match ? { host: (match[1] ?? '').toLowerCase(), path: match[2] || '/' } : null
}

function isPlaceholder(segment: string): boolean {
  return /^\{[^}]+\}$|^:[A-Za-z_]\w*$|^<[^>]+>$/.test(segment)
}

export interface ConnectorConfig {
  /** Datadog API key for authentication (DD-API-KEY header). */
  datadogApiKey: string;
  /** Datadog site domain, e.g., "datadoghq.com", "us3.datadoghq.com". */
  datadogSite: string;
  /** Optional fetch implementation for testing or customization. */
  fetch?: typeof fetch;
}

export interface MailchimpRateLimitPayload {
  /** HTTP status code from Mailchimp API (expected 429). */
  status_code: number;
  /** Retry-After header value in seconds from Mailchimp response. */
  retry_after: number;
  /** Summary of the final outcome after retry attempts. */
  final_outcome: string;
  /** Error message from the failed Mailchimp API call. */
  error_message: string;
}

export interface DatadogEventResponse {
  /** Created event details from Datadog. */
  event: {
    id: string;
    title: string;
    text: string;
    category: string;
    priority: string;
    source_type_name: string;
    timestamp: number;
  };
}

export interface HandleResult {
  /** Datadog event ID from the response. */
  eventId: string;
  /** Full Datadog event response. */
  datadogResponse: DatadogEventResponse;
}

function validatePayload(payload: unknown): asserts payload is MailchimpRateLimitPayload {
  if (!payload || typeof payload !== 'object') {
    throw new Error('Payload must be an object');
  }
  const p = payload as Record<string, unknown>;
  const requiredFields: (keyof MailchimpRateLimitPayload)[] = ['status_code', 'retry_after', 'final_outcome', 'error_message'];
  for (const field of requiredFields) {
    if (!(field in p)) {
      throw new Error(`Missing required field: ${field}`);
    }
  }
  if (typeof p.status_code !== 'number') {
    throw new Error('status_code must be a number');
  }
  if (typeof p.retry_after !== 'number') {
    throw new Error('retry_after must be a number');
  }
  if (typeof p.final_outcome !== 'string') {
    throw new Error('final_outcome must be a string');
  }
  if (typeof p.error_message !== 'string') {
    throw new Error('error_message must be a string');
  }
}

export async function handle(
  payload: MailchimpRateLimitPayload,
  config: ConnectorConfig
): Promise<HandleResult> {
  validatePayload(payload);

  const fetchImpl = config.fetch ?? fetch;
  const url = `https://event-management-intake.${config.datadogSite}/api/v2/events`;

  const requestBody = {
    title: payload.final_outcome,
    text: payload.error_message,
    status: String(payload.status_code),
    retry_after: payload.retry_after,
    category: 'change',
    priority: 'normal',
    source_type_name: 'Mailchimp',
  };

  const response = await fetchImpl(url, {
    method: 'POST',
    headers: {
      'Content-Type': 'application/json',
      'DD-API-KEY': config.datadogApiKey,
    },
    body: JSON.stringify(requestBody),
  });

  if (!response.ok) {
    throw new Error(`Datadog Events API request failed: ${response.status} ${response.statusText} for POST ${url}`);
  }

  const data = (await response.json()) as DatadogEventResponse;
  return {
    eventId: data.event.id,
    datadogResponse: data,
  };
}

<file path="README.md">
# Mailchimp Rate Limit to Datadog Event Connector

This connector transforms Mailchimp API HTTP 429 (rate limit) responses into Datadog events for monitoring and alerting.

## What It Does

When a Mailchimp API request returns HTTP 429 (Too Many Requests) with a `Retry-After` header, this connector:
1. Validates the rate limit payload contains all required fields
2. Maps the Mailchimp response fields to a Datadog event payload
3. Creates an event in Datadog via the Events API v2
4. Returns the created event ID and full response

## Configuration

The connector requires the following configuration (typically from environment variables):

| Config Property | Environment Variable | Description |
|-----------------|---------------------|-------------|
| `datadogApiKey` | `DATADOG_API_KEY` | Datadog API key for authentication (sent as `DD-API-KEY` header) |
| `datadogSite` | `DATADOG_SITE` | Datadog site domain (e.g., `datadoghq.com`, `us3.datadoghq.com`, `datadoghq.eu`) |
| `fetch` | — | Optional custom fetch implementation (for testing) |

## Usage Example

```typescript
import { handle, ConnectorConfig, MailchimpRateLimitPayload } from './connector';

const config: ConnectorConfig = {
  datadogApiKey: process.env.DATADOG_API_KEY!,
  datadogSite: process.env.DATADOG_SITE || 'datadoghq.com',
};

const payload: MailchimpRateLimitPayload = {
  status_code: 429,
  retry_after: 60,
  final_outcome: 'Failed after 3 retries',
  error_message: 'TooManyRequests: You have exceeded the limit of 10 simultaneous connections.',
};

try {
  const result = await handle(payload, config);
  console.log('Datadog event created:', result.eventId);
} catch (error) {
  console.error('Failed to create Datadog event:', error);
}
```

## Field Mapping

| Mailchimp Field | Datadog Field | Description |
|-----------------|---------------|-------------|
| `status_code` | `status` | HTTP status code (e.g., "429") |
| `retry_after` | `retry_after` | Retry-After header value in seconds |
| `final_outcome` | `title` | Summary of final retry outcome |
| `error_message` | `text` | Detailed error message from Mailchimp |

Additional fixed fields sent to Datadog:
- `category`: "change" (General Availability)
- `priority`: "normal"
- `source_type_name`: "Mailchimp"

## Assumptions

1. The integration can intercept Mailchimp API responses and detect HTTP 429 status codes
2. The Mailchimp API response includes a `Retry-After` header when rate-limited
3. The system performs retries with exponential backoff internally before notifying Datadog
4. Datadog HTTP Events API is available and accepts POST requests to submit events
5. The final outcome summary and error message are available as strings after the retry loop completes
6. The Datadog site domain is known and configured (the `{site}` placeholder in the API URL)

## Error Handling

- Throws descriptive `Error` when required payload fields are missing
- Throws `Error` with status code and endpoint URL for non-2xx Datadog API responses
- Validates payload types (numbers for status_code/retry_after, strings for text fields)

## Testing

Run tests with Vitest:

```bash
vitest run src/connector.test.ts
```

Tests cover:
- Contract test with documented example payload
- Happy path with exact request body and auth verification
- Field mapping validation
- Missing required field validation
- Non-2xx Datadog API response handling
- Different Datadog site configurations

export interface ConnectorConfig {
  /** Secret used to verify the Linear-Signature header (verified by the webhook endpoint before calling handle). */
  linearWebhookSecret: string;
  /** Base URL for the Linear API (e.g., https://api.linear.app). */
  linearApiBaseUrl: string;
  /** Bearer token for Linear API authentication. */
  linearApiToken: string;
  /** Full Discord webhook URL (https://discord.com/api/webhooks/{id}/{token}). */
  discordWebhookUrl: string;
  /** Maximum allowed age of the webhook timestamp in milliseconds (default: 60000). */
  timestampToleranceMs?: number;
  /** Injected fetch implementation for testing. */
  fetch?: typeof fetch;
}

export interface LinearWebhookPayload {
  action: string;
  type: string;
  data: {
    id: string;
    title: string;
    identifier: string;
    state: {
      name: string;
    };
    url: string;
  };
  createdAt: string;
  webhookTimestamp: number;
}

export interface LinearComment {
  id: string;
  author: {
    name: string;
    email: string;
  };
  body: string;
  createdAt: string;
}

interface LinearCommentsResponse {
  comments: LinearComment[];
  pageInfo: {
    endCursor: string;
    hasMore: boolean;
  };
}

export interface HandleResult {
  discordMessageId: string;
}

export async function handle(
  payload: LinearWebhookPayload,
  config: ConnectorConfig
): Promise<HandleResult> {
  // Validate required fields
  if (payload.action !== 'update') {
    throw new Error('Invalid payload: action must be "update"');
  }
  if (payload.type !== 'Issue') {
    throw new Error('Invalid payload: type must be "Issue"');
  }
  if (!payload.data || payload.data.state?.name !== 'Closed') {
    throw new Error('Invalid payload: issue state must be "Closed"');
  }
  if (!payload.data.id) {
    throw new Error('Invalid payload: missing issue id');
  }
  if (!payload.data.title) {
    throw new Error('Invalid payload: missing issue title');
  }
  if (!payload.data.identifier) {
    throw new Error('Invalid payload: missing issue identifier');
  }

  // Verify timestamp freshness
  const now = Date.now();
  const tolerance = config.timestampToleranceMs ?? 60000;
  if (Math.abs(now - payload.webhookTimestamp) > tolerance) {
    throw new Error(
      `Webhook timestamp too old: ${payload.webhookTimestamp} (now: ${now}, tolerance: ${tolerance}ms)`
    );
  }

  // Fetch all comments via cursor pagination
  const comments = await fetchAllComments(payload.data.id, config);

  // Format Discord message
  const content = formatDiscordMessage(payload.data, comments);

  // Post to Discord webhook
  const fetchFn = config.fetch ?? fetch;
  const response = await fetchFn(config.discordWebhookUrl, {
    method: 'POST',
    headers: {
      'Content-Type': 'application/json',
    },
    body: JSON.stringify({
      content,
      username: 'Linear Bot',
      avatar_url: 'https://linear.app/assets/icon.png',
    }),
  });

  if (!response.ok) {
    throw new Error(
      `Discord webhook failed: ${response.status} ${response.statusText} at ${config.discordWebhookUrl}`
    );
  }

  const result = (await response.json()) as { id: string };
  return { discordMessageId: result.id };
}

async function fetchAllComments(issueId: string, config: ConnectorConfig): Promise<LinearComment[]> {
  const fetchFn = config.fetch ?? fetch;
  const allComments: LinearComment[] = [];
  let cursor: string | undefined;
  let hasMore = true;

  while (hasMore) {
    const url = new URL(`${config.linearApiBaseUrl}/issues/${issueId}/comments`);
    if (cursor) {
      url.searchParams.set('after', cursor);
    }

    try {
      const response = await fetchFn(url.toString(), {
        method: 'GET',
        headers: {
          Authorization: `Bearer ${config.linearApiToken}`,
          'Content-Type': 'application/json',
        },
      });

      if (!response.ok) {
        // Fallback: log and return comments fetched so far
        console.warn(`Failed to fetch comments: ${response.status} ${response.statusText}`);
        break;
      }

      const data = (await response.json()) as LinearCommentsResponse;
      allComments.push(...data.comments);
      cursor = data.pageInfo.endCursor;
      hasMore = data.pageInfo.hasMore;
    } catch (error) {
      // Fallback on network/parsing error
      console.warn('Failed to fetch comments:', error);
      break;
    }
  }

  return allComments;
}

function formatDiscordMessage(
  issue: LinearWebhookPayload['data'],
  comments: LinearComment[]
): string {
  const lines = [`Issue ${issue.identifier}: ${issue.title}`, '', 'Comments:'];
  if (comments.length === 0) {
    lines.push('(no comments)');
  } else {
    for (const comment of comments) {
      lines.push(`- ${comment.author.name} (${comment.author.email}): ${comment.body}`);
    }
  }
  return lines.join('\n');
}
